articles.headline: Cabinet approves bill to freeze Lok Sabha seat proportions until 2051
articles.title: Centre proposes freeze on Lok Sabha seat proportions for States until 2051
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet approved a constitutional amendment bill on November 27, 2026, extending the freeze on inter-state Lok Sabha seat distribution until 2051. The legislation removes the 1971 Census linkage and pairs seat allocation with women's reservation provisions. If passed by Parliament during special sittings ending December 3, the bill will increase total Lok Sabha seats by 50 percent, raising the lower house maximum strength from 550 to 850.
articles.description: The new Constitutional Amendment Bill, accompanied by a fresh Delimitation Bill, proposes to increase the number of Lok Sabha seats in each State by 50%; they also bring into force the 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha

articles.headline: Israeli strike on Doctors Without Borders clinic in Gaza kills two
articles.title: Israeli strike on Doctors Without Borders clinic in Gaza kills two staff
articles.summary: An Israeli military strike on a clearly marked Doctors Without Borders clinic in Gaza City killed two watchmen who worked as staff members for the humanitarian agency. The October 2025 attack brings the organization's death toll among personnel in the region to 17. While the Israeli military claimed the victims were members of Hamas without providing evidence, international figures and agencies strongly condemned the incident.
articles.description: MSF says Israeli attack on Gaza clinic a 'direct hit' and calls for those responsible to be held accountable.

articles.headline: Israel kills two MSF staff in targeted strike on Gaza clinic
articles.title: Israel kills two MSF staff in targeted strike on Gaza clinic
articles.description: An Israeli strike on a clinic operated by Doctors Without Borders (MSF) in Gaza has killed two watchmen.

articles.headline: Volodymyr Zelenskyy criticises Donald Trump and urges increased pressure on Russia
articles.title: Zelenskyy urges U.S. to pressure Russia and questions Trump referring Putin as ‘friend’
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy criticised United States President Donald Trump during a British Broadcasting Corporation interview on November 27, 2026, for referring to Russian leader Vladimir Putin as a friend. Zelenskyy urged the U.S. to increase pressure on Moscow to end the nearly five-year invasion, which has caused hundreds of thousands of military and civilian casualties. Meanwhile, European Union leaders failed to agree on a new $49 billion loan for Ukraine.
articles.description: In an interview to BBC broadcast, the Ukrainian President wants the U.S. to apply more pressure on Russia to stop invation of Ukraine

articles.headline: Union Cabinet approves Constitution Amendment Bill for delimitation and women reservation
articles.title: Union Cabinet clears delimitation bill
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi approved a Constitution Amendment Bill on November 27, 2026, to implement delimitation and increase parliamentary seats by fifty percent with a current ratio ceiling until 2051. The legislation also provides women reservation. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju announced a special session beginning November 30. Securing passage requires a two thirds majority in both houses.
articles.description: A similar attempt by the government was rejected in the Lok Sabha during the Monsoon session in April

articles.headline: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warns citizens of a new mass missile strike
articles.title: Zelenskyy warns of major Russian attack as Trump urges Putin to ‘pull back’
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned citizens to watch for missile alerts as Russia prepares a new mass strike. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump stated he urged Russian President Vladimir Putin to ease military actions in Europe. In separate developments, European Union leaders debated a forty-five billion euro loan for Ukraine in Brussels, and military intelligence reported North Korea paused certain arms deliveries.
articles.description: Trump says he urged Putin to 'pull back' military aggression in Europe amid escalating Russian and Ukrainian attacks.

articles.headline: Saudi air defences intercept cruise missile over Riyadh following Yemen strikes
articles.title: Saudi Arabia, Houthis trade attacks on rival capitals
articles.summary: Saudi air defences intercepted and destroyed a cruise missile targeting the capital Riyadh on November 28, 2026. Coalition spokesperson Turki Al-Malki attributed the launch to Houthi militia forces. The escalation followed reported Saudi airstrikes on the Yemeni capital of Sanaa, which Houthi news outlets stated damaged residential neighborhoods and injured 13 people in the Al-Tahrir district.
articles.description: A Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's internationally recognised government has been regularly bombing areas controlled by the Iran-backed group since Yemen's civil war reignited over the summer

articles.headline: Congress reaches out to opposition parties to stall delimitation Bill
articles.title: Congress reaches out to DMK, other Opposition parties to stall passage of delimitation Bill
articles.summary: The Congress party initiated outreach efforts on November 27, 2026, engaging with opposition groups including the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam and the Nationalist Congress Party to block the proposed delimitation legislation in Parliament. Leaders warned the exercise is divisive and threatens national unity. The move follows discussions in New Delhi regarding parliamentary strategies to challenge the government's legislative agenda before upcoming sessions.
articles.description: The party may urge CMs of southern States to hold press conferences, and is likely to hold a nationwide campaign against ‘divisive’ delimitation exercise

articles.headline: Lok Sabha seat distribution freeze extended for twenty five years
articles.title: Lok Sabha seat freeze is no longer linked to population stabilisation
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet has approved a constitutional amendment to maintain the current proportion of Lok Sabha seats for individual states for another twenty five years until 2051. According to The Hindu, the upcoming 132nd Constitutional Amendment Bill removes the previous link between population stabilisation and seat share, allowing the freeze to continue as a special measure to accommodate thirty three percent reservation for women.
articles.description: The distribution of seats based on 1971 Census continued for 50 years for the reason that a readjustment would adversely affect the proportion of States that stabilised population. Population stability was a stated objective of the government. That link between population stability and Lok Sabha share has been removed in the 132nd Constitutional Amendment Bill

articles.headline: Indian forces kill suspected Lashkar-e-Taiba commander in Kulgam district
articles.title: ‘Last local militant’: India declares victory but Kashmir’s rebels adapt
articles.summary: Indian security forces killed Mohammad Lateef Bhat, described as a commander of the Pakistan-based group Lashkar-e-Taiba, during a gunfight in Zangalpora village on November 18. Indian Home Minister Amit Shah stated Bhat was the final local militant in the valley. However, analysts and former police officials cautioned that armed conflict continues to evolve through unrecorded fighters and shifting violence.
articles.description: Analysts say that shifting tactics, names and geography challenge claims of win against Kashmir's separatist movement.

articles.headline: Union Cabinet approves revised Delimitation Bill ahead of Parliament session
articles.title: Centre’s delimitation fix steadies Yogi Adityanath’s nerves ahead of polls
articles.summary: Following Union Cabinet approval of a revised Delimitation Bill ahead of a special parliamentary session, Uttar Pradesh's state legislature will expand past its 500-member constitutional ceiling without dividing the state. In Lucknow and New Delhi, observers interpret the policy as a signal from the central leadership to end speculation about division and steady Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.
articles.description: By raising the constitutional ceiling on State assemblies from 500 to 650 seats, the Union Cabinet’s revised delimitation bill allows U.P. assembly to expand to 605 members without dividing the State

articles.headline: Nepal and India issue ten-pillared vision statement during Prime Minister Balendra Shah visit
articles.title: Ten pillars of Nepal-India vision statement issued during Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s visit
articles.summary: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah visited New Delhi in November 2026 following an invitation delivered by Indian Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri. During the official two-day trip, the two nations issued a ten-pillared vision statement designed to establish a new bilateral direction for post-uprising Nepal, following domestic political shifts earlier in the year that led to Shah taking office in March.
articles.description: Indian and Nepali delegations came up with the ten-pillar vision document titled ‘Viksit Bharat-Samunnat Nepal: Reimagining the Partnership’

articles.headline: Supreme Court directs Food Safety and Standards Authority of India to introduce red warning labels
articles.title: Why the Supreme Court wants red warning labels on unhealthy packaged foods | Explained
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India directed the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India to implement a single-phase front-of-pack nutrition labelling regime within four months. The regulatory change will require packaged food products high in sugar, saturated fat or salt to display prominent red warning labels if they exceed prescribed nutritional limits for even a single nutrient.
articles.description: The Supreme Court, earlier this week, directed the FSSAI to introduce a single-phase front-of-pack nutrition labelling (FoPNL) regime and gave the regulator four months to finalise the draft regulations

articles.headline: Tanzanian opposition activist Twaha Salim Mwaipaya forcibly abducted by unidentified individuals in Kenya
articles.title: Hunted beyond borders: Allegations of Tanzanian repression in Kenya
articles.summary: Tanzanian opposition activist Twaha Salim Mwaipaya was forcibly removed from a taxi by unidentified individuals in Machakos County on October 25, 2026, and remains missing. Human rights organizations, including the Kenya National Commission on Human Rights and Amnesty International, have urged Kenyan authorities to investigate the disappearance and determine his whereabouts amid ongoing concerns regarding transnational political repression.
articles.description: The case of a missing activist raises fears for the safety of Tanzanian dissidents.

articles.headline: Taiwan holds competitive local elections to choose mayors and council members across 22 cities
articles.title: Taiwan votes in local elections to choose mayors, other leaders
articles.summary: Taiwan voters cast ballots in local elections on Saturday to choose mayors, council members, and other leaders across 22 cities and counties. The highly competitive vote involves roughly 11,000 positions, including a closely watched mayoral race in Taipei between incumbent Chiang Wan-an of the Kuomintang and Puma Shen of the Democratic Progressive Party, amidst rising military pressure and warnings from Beijing.
articles.description: Key mayoral race in Taipei, a stronghold of the opposition Kuomintang, tests the governing Democratic Progressive Party.

articles.headline: US disables ship attempting to breach Iran blockade
articles.title: US disables ship attempting to breach Iran blockade
articles.description: The US military says it disabled a commercial ship after it left an Iranian port and ignored warnings to stop.

articles.headline: Uyghur activists report declining protest numbers amid China's rising global economic influence
articles.title: Behind China's spectacular rise, voices who defied it say they are being drowned out
articles.summary: Uyghur activists state that protests against China have dwindled as Beijing expands its global economic and soft power influence. Speaking to the BBC, exiled figures note that international focus has shifted due to economic interests. Additionally, activists claim Chinese authorities have offered family reunions and safety to exiles in exchange for information, allegations dismissed by the Chinese embassy in the UK.
articles.description: China's immense clout now also has the flex of soft power. Critics and dissidents say their voices are being drowned out.

articles.headline: Kenyan court convicts cult leader Paul Mackenzie of manslaughter over starvation deaths
articles.title: Kenyan cult leader guilty of manslaughter more than 123 starvation deaths
articles.summary: A Kenyan court in Mombasa found Good News International Church founder Paul Mackenzie and 29 followers guilty of manslaughter on Friday regarding 123 starvation deaths. Magistrate Alex Ithuku stated Mackenzie ordered followers to fast to death in the Shakahola Forest. Mackenzie, who pleaded not guilty and plans to appeal, previously received a 200-year prison sentence for other murders.
articles.description: Paul Mackenzie, already serving 200 years, is the founder and pastor of the Good News International Church.

articles.headline: US military disables Palau-flagged merchant ship in Gulf of Oman
articles.title: US military says it disabled merchant ship trying to breach Iran blockade
articles.summary: The United States Central Command stated that military aircraft disabled the Palau-flagged merchant vessel Pacific Archer in the Gulf of Oman on Thursday after it attempted to breach a blockade on Iranian ports. The civilian crew remained unharmed during the strike, which marks the fifteenth vessel the US military has publicly acknowledged disabling since April.
articles.description: The US military says it disabled the Palau-flagged ship’s propulsion but its crew was unharmed.

articles.headline: Spanish party leaders hold final rallies ahead of Sunday parliamentary election
articles.title: Spanish PM and rivals rally supporters in final pitch for votes
articles.summary: Main party leaders in Spain held final campaign rallies ahead of the election on Sunday, with Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez expressing confidence while conservative rival Alberto Nunez Feijoo leads in polls. Nearly 39 million voters will participate in the closely contested vote. Feijoo hopes to form a government supported by the right-wing Vox party, while Sanchez aims to maintain a progressive coalition amid sharply polarised political divisions over housing and immigration.
articles.description: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez wants to defy the polls, and his main rivals accuse him of not telling the truth and of "betrayal".

articles.headline: Northern Yemen families face severe hunger as prices rise and aid stops
articles.title: Why are families going hungry in northern Yemen even where food is on sale?
articles.summary: Families in northern Yemen are struggling with surging food prices and dwindling incomes while UN food assistance remains suspended. According to assessments from the Famine Early Warning Systems Network and the World Food Programme, basic food costs in Houthi-controlled areas rose significantly. Residents report earning barely enough to cover daily necessities, and international humanitarian organisations warn that severe funding shortfalls are compounding the crisis.
articles.description: Flour and oil still reach markets in Hodeidah and Sanaa. But high costs and lack of work and aid put it out of reach.

articles.headline: Venezuela to repeal legislation that bans opposition figures from holding office
articles.title: Venezuela to repeal law that bans opposition figures from office
articles.summary: National Assembly Chief Jorge Rodriguez announced that Venezuela will repeal a controversial 2024 law targeting opposition figures who supported sanctions. The decision follows a political transition led by interim president Delcy Rodriguez after the removal of Nicolas Maduro. Meanwhile, opposition leader Maria Corina Machado launched neighbourhood assemblies to gather public proposals for a democratic transition despite her ongoing exclusion from official talks and previous political bans.
articles.description: It comes a month after opposition leader Maria Corina Machado returned to Venezuela.

articles.headline: OpenAI files counterclaims against Apple over trade secrets and supplier access
articles.title: OpenAI countersues Apple over trade secrets as AI race heats up
articles.summary: OpenAI filed counterclaims against Apple in a California federal court on Friday, accusing the technology giant of stealing trade secrets and blocking hardware supplier access. The legal escalation follows a July lawsuit by Apple alleging that OpenAI misappropriated secrets by poaching employees. The dispute highlights intense competition between the companies over artificial intelligence talent and the development of future devices that could eventually challenge the iPhone.
articles.description: Tensions between the two tech companies have escalated as intensifying race to develop AI products fuels competition.

articles.headline: Putin unveils nuclear-powered submarine equipped with Zircon hypersonic missiles
articles.title: Putin unveils new Russian nuclear-powered submarine with hypersonic weapons
articles.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin attended a flag-raising ceremony for the nuclear-powered submarine Perm at the Sevmash shipyard in Severodvinsk on Friday. Putin stated that the vessel is equipped with Zircon hypersonic missiles and announced plans to add five more submarines to the Russian naval fleet by 2030. The expansion aims to maintain Russia's maritime nuclear deterrent capabilities and modernize its naval forces for global operations.
articles.description: The Kremlin plans to expand its naval fleet with five new nuclear submarines by 2030.

articles.headline: Hamas chief’s last surviving son escapes Israeli strike in Gaza
articles.title: Hamas chief’s last surviving son escapes Israeli strike in Gaza
articles.description: Hamas leader Khalil al-Hayya's last surviving son Izzeldeen survived an Israeli assassination attempt on Friday.

articles.headline: Hamas leader son survives Israeli strike as violence continues in Gaza
articles.title: Israel kills four in Gaza as Hamas chief al-Hayya’s son survives strike
articles.summary: Izzeldeen al-Hayya and his family survived an Israeli air strike in Gaza on Friday, according to Hamas official Basem Naim, while separate attacks across the strip killed four Palestinians. The incident comes amid ongoing violations of the October 2025 ceasefire, which Gaza health authorities report have killed at least 1705 Palestinians since taking effect across the besieged Palestinian territory.
articles.description: Four of Khalil al-Hayya's other sons were previously killed by Israeli forces, according to the Palestinian group.

articles.headline: Prime Minister invokes Lord Murugan following Supreme Court directive
articles.title: Modi invokes Lord Murugan; BJP says Tamil Nadu govt. acted against Hindus
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi posted messages on social media invoking Lord Murugan on November 27, 2026, hours after the Supreme Court ordered the Karthigai Deepam to be lit on a stone pillar in Madurai. Bharatiya Janata Party leaders welcomed the decision, accusing the Tamil Nadu government of acting against Hindu interests and alleging political collusion in the initial failure to execute the ritual properly.
articles.description: Supreme Court has exposed Tamil Nadu Government’s anti-Sanatan mindset, says Nitin Nabin

articles.headline: United States military disables commercial vessel near Gulf of Oman
articles.title: U.S. disables ship trying to leave Iran, as Tehran vows to confront blockade
articles.summary: The United States military announced on November 27, 2026, that it disabled a Palau-flagged commercial ship in the Gulf of Oman the previous day after the crew attempted to bypass a maritime blockade against Iran. United States Central Command reported that military aircraft used precision munitions to strike the stern of the vessel, successfully halting its propulsion without injuring any civilian crew members.
articles.description: Mohammad Mokhber, an adviser to ⁠Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, said: “Neither will the Strait of Hormuz be ‌reopened, nor will we allow the blockade to remain in place,” Iranian state media reported

articles.headline: Global fashion brands shift clothing orders from Bangladesh to India
articles.title: Global fashion brands shift orders from Bangladesh to India amid unrest
articles.summary: Major international fashion retailers including Zara and H&M diverted nearly ten percent of their monthly orders from Bangladesh to alternative Asian manufacturing hubs like India during the first half of November. Factory owners reported that ongoing labour unrest and production losses totalling over four hundred million dollars prompted the sourcing shift, following a thirty six percent minimum wage increase approved on Wednesday.
articles.description: Between November 1 and 18, brands diverted about $254 million worth ⁠of orders from Bangladesh, with most moving to neighbouring India, the owners said

articles.headline: U.S. levies new 25% tariff on Indian goods citing excess capacity
articles.title: U.S. announces new 25% tariffs on India, second-highest in the 14 countries against which action has been taken
articles.summary: The United States government announced a 25% import tariff on Indian goods on November 25, 2026, citing structural excess capacity that burdens American commerce. According to the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative, the rate could drop to 17% if a trade agreement is reached. The Indian Ministry of Commerce and Industry stated it is examining the notice while bilateral negotiations continue.
articles.description: The order by the U.S. Trade Representative also opens the door for a lower 17% tariff if India and the U.S. sign a trade deal

articles.headline: India must strengthen military capabilities across domains, says defence chief
articles.title: War and peace distinction blurring, India faces continuous state of contestation: CDS
articles.summary: Chief of Defence Staff General N.S. Raja Subramani stated that nations face continuous contestation as the boundary between war and peace blurs. Speaking in New Delhi, he emphasised the necessity for India to modernise its electronic and cognitive warfare capabilities. He highlighted lessons from recent global conflicts and pointed to Operation Sindoor as an example of effective joint military operations and intelligence-led strikes.
articles.description: ‘A nation’s military power is as good as its industrial power,’ said Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) General N.S. Raja Subramani

articles.headline: Ukraine faces freezing winter as Russian strikes continue
articles.title: Weary of war but with no sign of backing down, Kyiv faces another punishing winter
articles.summary: Kyiv residents endure frequent blackouts and freezing temperatures as Russian ballistic missiles and drones target critical infrastructure, including bridges across the River Dnipro. Despite the ongoing bombardment and severe damage to power grids, recent public opinion polls indicate that a majority of Ukrainians remain determined to continue fighting rather than surrender to Russia. The conflict has persisted for more than four and a half years.
articles.description: Ukraine settles in for another devastating winter as the questions persists: how will it all end?

articles.headline: Supreme Court orders ritual lamp lighting and suspends temple trustees
articles.title: Supreme Court orders Karthigai Deepam to be lit at ‘deepathoon’ on November 28; issues contempt notice
articles.summary: The Supreme Court on November 27, 2026, suspended temple trustees and appointed former High Court judges as receivers after ruling that officials engaged in wilful disobedience of a previous directive concerning the Thirupparankundram hill ritual in Madurai. The bench ordered central forces to provide security as the Karthigai Deepam is lit on the stone pillar on November 28, issuing contempt notices to multiple state administrative officials.
articles.description: Bench directs Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary, DGP, Madurai District Collector, temple authorities to be present for next hearing on Dec. 15; court sees ‘pre-meditated conspiracy' between State and temple trustees

articles.headline: M.K. Stalin blames state government for Thirupparankundram hill row
articles.title: Thirupparankundram row: Vijay-led govt. brought unprecedented threats to Tamil Nadu’s traditions, religious harmony and State rights, says Stalin
articles.summary: Former Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M.K. Stalin stated on November 27, 2026, that a recent Supreme Court order regarding the Thirupparankundram hillock lamp lighting demonstrates a failure by the Tamil Nadu government. He criticized the administration for allegedly compromising state rights and religious harmony through poor legal representation, while appealing to citizens to maintain peace across the region.

articles.headline: Akhilesh Yadav questions Uttar Pradesh leaders over conflicting missing voter figures
articles.title: BJP, poll body conspiring to add fake voters in U.P., says Akhilesh
articles.summary: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav questioned differing figures from Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa regarding missing voters during a Lucknow press conference on November 27, 2026. Mr. Yadav alleged electoral roll manipulation ahead of the 2027 assembly elections and demanded Aadhaar-linked voter identity cards with biometric verification to prevent bogus voting.
articles.description: Akhilesh Yadav said delimitation would be the BJP’s biggest mistake; he said the BJP, in collaboration with the Election Commission, has added 2,84,000 fake votes to the voter list

articles.headline: Zelensky criticises US policy on Russia and missile delivery delays
articles.title: Zelensky criticises 'strange' Trump-Putin friendship in BBC interview
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated in Kyiv that United States delays in supplying anti-ballistic missiles are causing fatalities and claimed Washington is insufficiently pressuring Russia during peace negotiations. Speaking to the BBC, he also expressed concern over restricted Starlink services in occupied territories and defended recent Ukrainian long-range strikes against Russian military assets ahead of a challenging winter.
articles.description: Ukraine's president voices frustration with US and says it is not pushing Russia hard enough in peace talks to end the war.

articles.headline: Chinese military tests civilian vessel landing tactics during Fujian province drills
articles.title: Chinese Military tests new Taiwan landing tactics in coastal drills
articles.summary: The Chinese military conducted amphibious landing drills in Dacheng Bay, Fujian province, utilising civilian vessels to improvise a floating bridge for troop transport. Satellite images reviewed by geospatial data company ingeniSPACE captured the exercises, which a senior security official confirmed on November 27, 2026, were designed to practice rapid island seizures and support potential Taiwan strait operations.
articles.description: The exercise in Dacheng Bay was first spotted on November 1, according to a report by geospatial data company ingeniSPACE reviewed by Reuters

articles.headline: Saudi coalition airstrikes kill eleven people in Yemen following refinery attack
articles.title: Saudi strike kills 11 in Yemen, reports Houthi media
articles.summary: Saudi-led coalition airstrikes killed eleven people, predominantly children, in the Taiz governorate of Yemen on November 27, 2026, according to Houthi media. The strikes followed a Houthi attack on the Jazan oil refinery in southern Saudi Arabia that killed one Nepalese worker. The renewed conflict has killed over 2,300 people since July, according to the United Nations.
articles.description: The latest incidents came a day after a deadly Houthi attack on a Saudi oil refinery, and add to a growing tally of violence since Yemen's civil war reignited over the summer

articles.headline: NATO jets scrambled after drone enters Latvian airspace
articles.title: NATO jets scrambled after drone enters Latvian airspace
articles.summary: North Atlantic Treaty Organization fighter jets and a national interceptor drone were deployed overnight in Latvia following a brief airspace incursion near the Russian border. The Latvian Army reported that the unmanned aircraft crossed into national territory from Thursday to Friday without identifying its origin. Baltic states have repeatedly faced border incursions and crashes since the invasion of Ukraine began in February 2022.
articles.description: This year, two drones were shot down over Latvia by NATO fighter jets, which protect the skies of Baltic states

articles.headline: Ukraine offers Black Sea ceasefire to protect agricultural exports
articles.title: Kyiv offers Black Sea ceasefire to protect grain exports
articles.summary: Ukraine presented a Black Sea ceasefire proposal during the Food from Ukraine conference to ensure uninterrupted agricultural exports and restore freedom of navigation amid escalating attacks on shipping. Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha stated that Kyiv is awaiting a response from Moscow, which previously sought to include oil transportation in the deal. The diplomatic initiative comes as international concern grows over commercial shipping security and global food supplies.
articles.description: The proposal comes as President Zelenskyy criticises Trump’s ‘friendship’ with Putin.

articles.headline: Mecca pact allies condemn Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
articles.title: Mecca pact allies condemn ‘heinous’ Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
articles.summary: Government and defence officials from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye strongly denounced persistent Houthi attacks on Saudi cities and infrastructure during a meeting in Islamabad. The Strategic Political and Defence Committee reaffirmed its collective commitment to safeguarding Saudi security under the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement signed on August 7. The discussions followed continued drone and missile strikes that have killed at least 26 people in the kingdom since September 23.
articles.description: Officials from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye pledge to protect the kingdom's security during talks in Islamabad.

articles.headline: Kenyan cult leader convicted of manslaughter over follower deaths
articles.title: Kenyan doomsday cult leader convicted over further 123 deaths
articles.summary: A Kenyan court convicted doomsday cult leader Paul Mackenzie of manslaughter for the deaths of 123 followers who starved themselves to death in Shakahola forest. Mackenzie and 29 co-accused were found guilty on Friday, while 60 other defendants were acquitted by the court. The self-styled pastor was previously sentenced to 200 years in prison for murdering 191 children in connection with the same mass fasting incident.
articles.description: Paul Mackenzie is found guilty of killing his followers, weeks after being jailed for the mass murder of children.

articles.headline: Ukrainian forces launch Operation Bear Trap to liberate Kharkiv territory
articles.title: ‘Bear trap’: Ukraine hails new operation as Russian casualties mount
articles.summary: Ukrainian forces executed Operation Bear Trap in the northern Kharkiv region, liberating two hundred square kilometres and fourteen settlements after commanders ordered tactical moves to counter a potential Russian encirclement. The operation utilized deceptive maneuvers and remote mining to repel enemy forces. Meanwhile, United States negotiators continued pushing land-for-peace proposals that Ukrainian leadership resisted as Russian casualties reached record highs.
articles.description: Russian assaults met with stout defence along the front as Western powers discuss ceasefire proposals.

articles.headline: Ministry of Home Affairs issues digital citizenship certificates for naturalised citizens
articles.title: All Indians to get digital citizenship certificates, hard copies only on request: MHA
articles.summary: The Union Ministry of Home Affairs amended the Citizenship Rules, 2009, mandating that individuals acquiring Indian citizenship via registration or naturalisation receive digital certificates. According to a notification published on November 27, 2026, physical copies will now be provided exclusively upon explicit applicant request and issued by an Under Secretary or authorised central government officer.
articles.description: The Ministry, in a notice, said digital citizenship certificates shall be issued by an Under Secretary of the Centre or any other officer authorised by it

articles.headline: District authorities rescue twenty-five bonded labourers in Hanumakonda district
articles.title: 25 workers, including nine children, rescued from bonded labour in Hanumakonda
articles.summary: District authorities rescued twenty-five workers, including nine children, from bonded labour at two brick and cement ring manufacturing units in Kamalapur village on November 26, 2026. Acting on District Collector Chahat Bajpai's directives, inspection teams uncovered severe exploitation, physical abuse, and forced debt bondage lasting up to fourteen years. Release certificates were subsequently issued to the survivors.
articles.description: Officials say some workers were so isolated from the outside world that they struggled to recall their names, ages and even the current date, year or day of the week during preliminary interaction

articles.headline: Supreme Court of Canada largely upholds Quebec provincial religious symbols ban
articles.title: Canada's top court largely upholds Quebec ban on religious symbols for public servants
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of Canada upheld Quebec's Bill 21 on November 27, 2026, which bans public sector workers from wearing religious symbols. While confirming the law's overall validity, the court ruled that prohibiting elected officials from wearing face coverings for religious reasons infringes on democratic rights. Prime Minister Mark Carney stated the government will study the implications of the ruling.
articles.description: The law faced legal challenges from a range of groups, including female Muslim, Sikh and Catholic teachers, who argued it violated their fundamental rights.

articles.headline: West Bengal police analyse data of voters deleted in revision
articles.title: West Bengal Police begin analysing data of voters deleted in SIR
articles.summary: West Bengal police initiated an investigation into voter deletions from electoral rolls during the special intensive revision process, ordering senior officials to analyse data and submit reports by November 30. Local police stations began conducting house-to-house document verification and setting up camps in government schools. While state officials described the initiative as routine, opposition parties condemned the police visits as intimidation tactics.
articles.description: West Bengal police teams have begun house-to-house visits to check the documents of deleted voters, and a report is due by November 30; Opposition parties have raised an alarm, while the Chief Electoral Officer’s office denies any knowledge

articles.headline: RBI cuts daily cash reserve ratio maintenance requirement to 90%
articles.title: RBI cuts daily CRR maintenance to 90%, to unlock over ₹40,000 crore
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India lowered the minimum daily maintenance requirement for the cash reserve ratio from 99% to 90%, releasing over 40000 crore rupees into the banking system. Effective from December 1, 2026, the policy change provides scheduled banks with greater flexibility for managing daily cash balances while meeting overall fortnightly requirements, reversing a tightening introduced in October.
articles.description: The latest relaxation is expected to improve banks’ liquidity flexibility and support credit deployment.

articles.headline: Hackers breach United States Air Force cloud platform Cloud One
articles.title: Hackers breach U.S. Air Force flagship Cloud One computing platform
articles.summary: Unknown hackers have breached the United States Air Force cloud computing platform known as Cloud One, according to five sources familiar with the matter. Discovered during upgrade work, the intrusion has paused migration efforts and blocked software updates. Investigators from Cyber Command have been called in to assess potential damage to the tactical and logistics data.
articles.description: The intrusion at Cloud One was discovered within the past month or so ⁠during work to upgrade the system, two people familiar with the matter said

articles.headline: India and United States trade deal close to culmination
articles.title: India-U.S. trade deal is close to culmination: Goyal
articles.summary: Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal announced that the proposed bilateral trade agreement between India and the United States is nearing finalisation as negotiators resolve past obstacles. Speaking virtually at an industry summit, Goyal noted that the progress follows a United States Trade Representative report proposing tariffs with potential caps for trade partners. India aims to further expand its preferential market access amid ongoing global trade uncertainties.
articles.description: The Commerce and Industry Minister said the “process and pathway” for finalising the pact is now taking shape, after a USTR report proposed 25% tariffs on Indian imports, capped at 17% if a deal is agreed

articles.headline: Canada Supreme Court upholds Quebec secularism law on religious symbols
articles.title: Canada’s top court largely upholds Quebec’s religious symbols ban
articles.summary: Canada Supreme Court largely upheld Quebec Bill 21, maintaining a ban on public school teachers, police officers and other public employees wearing religious symbols at work. The ruling concluded that Quebec lawfully used the notwithstanding clause to shield the legislation from certain Charter challenges. Civil rights groups and advocacy organizations criticized the decision, arguing that the law imposes severe discrimination and restricts professional opportunities for religious minorities.
articles.description: Quebec’s ban on teachers and police wearing religious symbols such as hijabs and turbans on the job remains in place.

articles.headline: Republicans criticize Donald Trump for reinstating Nvidia CEO
articles.title: ‘Playing with fire’: Trump faces GOP backlash over Nvidia CEO’s return
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump faced sharp criticism from his own party after he personally intervened to secure the reinstatement of Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang following his resignation. Several Republican senators expressed alarm that Huang's relationship with an individual suspected of working for China poses a national security vulnerability. Huang is scheduled to testify before congressional committees next week regarding the controversy.
articles.description: Former Trump officials warn his push to reinstate NVIDIA's CEO could be the final straw for Republicans.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh Cabinet approves investment proposals worth 36,000 crore rupees
articles.title: AP Cabinet clears investment proposals worth ₹36,000 crore, approves Kia’s second plant
articles.summary: The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet, led by Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Friday, cleared investment proposals totaling approximately 36,000 crore rupees from six companies. Key approvals include Kia's second automobile manufacturing plant in Sri Sathya Sai district, Adani's Integrated Titanium Complex in Srikakulam, and infrastructure developments in Amaravati, aiming to accelerate regional industrial growth and create new employment opportunities.
articles.description: The meeting also approves MSME Right to Business Bill intended to reduce delays in setting up industries and facilitate ease of doing business, major Amaravati infrastructure projects and power sector proposals

articles.headline: India welcomes climate fund pledge while warning of adaptation shortfalls
articles.title: COP31: India welcomes $50 million climate fund pledge, says adaptation needs far greater
articles.summary: Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav stated that while India welcomed a fifty million dollar pledge at COP31, the funds remain inadequate for developing nations. Speaking to PTI, Yadav expressed disappointment over the removal of a one hundred twenty billion dollar target and the failure to adopt the Antalya Pact, noting that India collaborated closely with the G77 and Like-Minded Developing Countries to advocate for equitable financial support.
articles.description: He said India would continue to push for enhanced financial support, transparency in delivery and implementation of existing commitments, particularly for the poorest and most climate-vulnerable countries.

articles.headline: Congress criticizes government over unshared draft bills ahead of Parliament sitting
articles.title: Bills for Parliament sittings not shared with MPs: Congress after Cabinet clears delimitation bill
articles.summary: The Congress party asserted on Friday that draft legislations for the upcoming parliamentary debate on November 30 have not been shared with members of parliament. General secretary Jairam Ramesh criticized the ruling administration following a Union Cabinet decision clearing a delimitation-linked Constitution Amendment Bill to facilitate the early implementation of the women's quota law.
articles.description: Jairam Ramesh, in a post on X, said “games continue to be played by the PM-HM jodi”

articles.headline: United Nations agencies warn global hunger will worsen in sixteen hotspots
articles.title: Famine expect to rise due to global conflict, El Nino, warns UN
articles.summary: Hunger is projected to intensify significantly across sixteen global hotspots over the coming six months, according to a report released on Friday by the Food and Agriculture Organization and the World Food Programme. Officials attributed the severe food insecurity crisis primarily to armed conflict and extreme climate events, noting that declining humanitarian funding is hindering response efforts.
articles.description: El Nino is a major driver behind three of the four newly identified hotspots, mainly in different parts of Africa.

articles.headline: Judges recommend prosecutors end corruption case against Netanyahu
articles.title: Judges recommend prosecutors end corruption case against Netanyahu
articles.description: Israeli judges have ruled there is little prospect Benjamin Netanyahu will be convicted of corruption.

articles.headline: United States announces new tariff regime targeting fourteen major trading partners
articles.title: Trump embraced Xi, then slapped new tariffs on China: What’s his game plan?
articles.summary: The administration of United States President Donald Trump announced plans to impose new tariffs on fourteen major trading partners, including China, citing unfair government subsidies and suppressed wages. Beijing criticized the unilateral measures and warned that it reserves the right to retaliate with steeper tariffs as bilateral trade tensions continue to escalate between the two nations.
articles.description: US president's new tariff regime targets China hardest, just weeks before Trump and Xi meet again in Miami.

articles.headline: Volkswagen argues rivals follow identical import model in tax dispute
articles.title: Volkswagen drags rivals Mercedes, BMW into $1.2 billion India tax fight
articles.summary: Volkswagen has told an Indian court that rival carmakers Mercedes-Benz, BMW and Kia follow the same parts import model, as it seeks to quash a record 1.2 billion dollar tax demand. Indian authorities previously accused the German manufacturer of fraud by importing car components at lower tariffs. The Mumbai court is scheduled to rule on November 30.
articles.description: Volkswagen has denied the allegations, ‌describing the case as a matter of “life and death” that could “wipe out” all of its investments in India, where it has just a 2% market share

articles.headline: Kuki civilians killed by militants buried in Manipur after two months
articles.title: Seven Kuki civilians killed by militants laid to rest in Manipur’s Churachandpur after two months
articles.summary: The mortal remains of seven Kuki civilians killed by suspected militants in September were laid to rest on November 27 at a cemetery in Churachandpur. Family members and civil society representatives gathered at the Anglo Kuki War Memorial for the funeral rites. The burial comes amid ongoing ethnic conflict in Manipur that has claimed hundreds of lives since May 2023.
articles.description: “The bodies were covered with traditional tribal shawls as a mark of respect and buried,” the officials said

articles.headline: Saudi air strikes kill eleven civilians in Yemen Taiz governorate
articles.title: Saudi strike kills ’11 civilians’ in Yemen’s Taiz: Houthi media
articles.summary: Saudi air strikes have killed 11 civilians, mostly children, in the city of al-Turbah within Yemen's Taiz governorate, according to media affiliated with the Houthi armed group. Rescue teams retrieved eight bodies while three people remain missing. The World Health Organization reported that thousands have been killed or injured as Yemen faces severe food insecurity.
articles.description: Hostilities between Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi-backed coalition continue to push Yemen into a humanitarian crisis.

articles.headline: Iran denies responsibility for drone attack killing Italians in Kuwait
articles.title: Italians killed in Kuwait: Why is Iran denying responsibility?
articles.summary: Two Italian technicians were killed in a drone attack on a military site in Kuwait on Thursday, prompting both Kuwait and Italy to blame Iran. Tehran denied any involvement, claiming the incident was a false-flag operation designed to escalate regional hostilities. The victims were maintaining detection antennae for air-defence systems when falling shrapnel struck them.
articles.description: Iran has openly claimed its strikes on Gulf states throughout the war. So why is it denying an attack on Kuwait?

articles.headline: Russia's unconventional warfare against Europe intensifies but fails to deter Ukraine support
articles.title: Russia’s hybrid war on Europe evolving, but failing: IISS
articles.summary: Sabotage attacks and infrastructure targeting by Moscow rose by sixteen percent over twelve months leading to September 2026, according to the International Institute for Strategic Studies. Despite increased unconventional operations involving arson and explosives, analysts reported that the campaign failed to weaken Western military backing for Kyiv, with European defence spending growing significantly alongside expanded NATO surveillance.
articles.description: Growing attacks have damaged European infrastructure, but have not reduced support for Ukraine, analysis says.

articles.headline: Dmk sets two conditions for supporting the Delimitation Bill
articles.title: DMK sets conditions to support Delimitation Bill
articles.summary: Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam president M.K. Stalin stated on November 27, 2026, that his party will demand Tamil Nadu's Lok Sabha seat share remain unchanged and that state proportional strengths based on the 1971 Census be frozen for 25 years. This support from 22 Lok Sabha members is vital for the Narendra Modi government to secure the necessary two-third majority for passing the legislation.
articles.description: Tamil Nadu’s share in Lok Sabha should not be reduced and the existing proportional strength of all States as determined on the basis of the 1971 Census must remain frozen for another 25 years, are Mr. Stalin’s two demands for supporting the Delimitation bill

articles.headline: Tenant farmer dies by suicide following crop failure in Adilabad district
articles.title: Drought’s bitter harvest of debt
articles.summary: Neelagiri Ashanna, a forty-three-year-old tenant farmer, died by suicide on November fourteen in Thalamadugu village after failing to repay a debt exceeding ten lakh rupees due to crop failure. His death leaves behind his wife Neelagiri Laxmi and two children, compounding family struggles amidst financial strain and failing health in Telangana.
articles.description: As El Niño conditions deepen Telangana’s agricultural distress, failed kharif crops have left farmers saddled with mounting debts, wiped-out investments and little means of recovery. With loan repayments looming and rural livelihoods under threat, Abhinay Deshpande reports on the human toll of the crisis, the growing desperation among farming families and the gaps in support, as experts warn that worsening water scarcity could prolong the distress well beyond this season

articles.headline: Amnesty International accuses Israel of systematically destroying reproductive life in Gaza
articles.title: Israeli attacks on women and girls meant ‘to destroy life’ in Gaza: Amnesty
articles.summary: Amnesty International alleged that Israeli military operations have sought to prevent births by targeting women, children, and maternal healthcare facilities since October 2023. Secretary General Agnes Callamard stated that the campaign violates the Genocide Convention through killings and forced displacement. Gaza's Health Ministry reported that nearly seventy-five thousand people have died, including over twenty-two thousand women and girls.
articles.description: Israel seeking 'to prevent births' and destroy Palestinians in Gaza by targeting women and girls, rights group says.

articles.headline: Government plans amended delimitation bill for special parliamentary session
articles.title: Why Delimitation Bill failed to pass in Parliament in April 2026
articles.summary: The Union government scheduled a special parliamentary session for November 30, 2026, to introduce an amended Delimitation Bill proposing a uniform fifty percent increase in Lok Sabha seats and a twenty five year freeze on state shares. An earlier version failed in April 2026 due to opposition concerns over linking women reservation to the 2011 Census and federal impacts on southern and eastern states.
articles.description: Why the Delimitation Bill failed in Parliament in April 2026 and how the political arithmetic changed since then; here’s what to know

articles.headline: Kerala records thirty four percent monsoon deficit raising drought concerns
articles.title: 34% monsoon deficit, bleak August outlook set alarm bells ringing in Kerala
articles.summary: Kerala faced a thirty four percent rainfall deficit during the first two months of the southwest monsoon, receiving 853.8 mm against the normal 1301.7 mm by July 31, 2026. India Meteorological Department Director Neetha K. Gopal warned of a potential drought year as August and September forecasts remain bleak, compounded by the expected peak of El Niño and neutral Indian Ocean Dipole conditions.
articles.description: By the end of July, Kerala received just 853.8 mm of rain, well below the normal 1,301.7 mm. This raises concerns of a potential drought, particularly if the monsoon remains weak in August and September. An impending El Niño threaten to further diminish rainfall prospects.

articles.headline: Former Chief Justice B.R. Gavai alleges disregard for merit in judicial appointments
articles.title: Ex-CJI Gavai writes to President Murmu, alleges ‘complete disregard’ for merit and inclusivity in judicial appointments
articles.summary: Former Chief Justice of India B.R. Gavai wrote to President Droupadi Murmu on November 27, 2026, alleging that recent judicial appointments by the Supreme Court Collegium headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant ignore merit and inclusivity. Justice Gavai claimed candidates from a single community are favoured while marginalised sections are excluded, citing controversial high court judge transfers.
articles.description: Former CJI says recent Collegium recommendations to constitutional courts favour ‘one particular section’, to the exclusion of marginalised communities

articles.headline: Centre proposes special parliamentary session to run from November 30 to December 3
articles.title: Amended Delimitation Bill likely to be tabled in special Parliament sitting from November 30
articles.summary: Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju announced that the Lok Sabha will convene on November 30 and the Rajya Sabha on December 2, with both houses concluding on December 3, 2026. According to the minister, the special sitting aims to transact essential government business while the Monsoon Session remains unprorogued, keeping alive speculation about constitutional amendments linked to the Women’s Reservation Bill.
articles.description: Centre announces special sitting of Parliament from November 30, 2026, over 100 days since both Houses were adjourned without prorogation; government trying to pass the Bill after ‘operation lotus’, says Congress

articles.headline: Canada Supreme Court issues landmark ruling on Quebec secularism law
articles.title: Canada’s top court rules on Quebec secularism law in landmark case
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of Canada delivered a pivotal ruling on November 27, 2026, addressing Quebec legislation that prohibits certain public sector employees from wearing religious symbols. The controversial statute, passed in 2019, heavily utilizes the constitutional notwithstanding clause to restrict religious expressions. Legal experts note the national implications for balancing provincial autonomy, secularism, and fundamental freedoms across the country.
articles.description: The law has been the subject of intense legal debate since it was first passed by Quebec's government in 2019

articles.headline: Gaza children suffer from severe stunting amid war and blockade
articles.title: ‘Will I get taller?’: Gaza’s children suffer stunting amid war, blockade
articles.summary: Prolonged conflict and blockade in Gaza have severely restricted access to diverse food and medical treatment, resulting in alarming rates of stunting and malnutrition among young children. According to a UNICEF survey conducted between May 31 and June 15, 2026, twelve percent of children under five were stunted, while doctors at Nasser Hospital report a sharp rise in growth disorder cases requiring unavailable hormonal therapies.
articles.description: One in eight children is stunted. Many have bones that have not matured the way they should. Treatment is elusive.

articles.headline: IORA nations must enhance collaboration: EAM Jaishankar
articles.title: IORA nations must enhance collaboration: EAM Jaishankar
articles.description: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar says the 23-member grouping must strengthen its collective voice amid geopolitical changes, as India chairs the Indian Ocean Rim Association

articles.headline: Congress condemns upcoming parliamentary session as a delimitation move
articles.title: Parliament's special sitting not for women’s quota but delimitation, will be resisted with all might: Congress
articles.summary: The Indian National Congress stated on November 27, 2026, that the upcoming special parliamentary sitting called by Prime Minister Narendra Modi focuses on constituency delimitation rather than women's reservations. Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh criticized the plan on X, alleging it empowers Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to manipulate boundaries for political gain, and vowed firm resistance against the amendment bill.
articles.description: The Opposition party said the government is convening a session, slated to begin on November 30, on the delimitation bill, which it will firmly oppose

articles.headline: South Asian study highlights lack of legal protection against marital rape
articles.title: Millions of wives in South Asia unprotected from marital rape - study
articles.summary: Millions of women across eight South Asian countries remain vulnerable to intimate partner violence due to colonial-era laws that exempt marital rape from criminal penalties, according to a report by the women rights coalition Samaj. While nations like the Maldives and Nepal have criminalized the act, countries including India, Bangladesh, and Sri Lanka retain the exception, prompting ongoing legal challenges and fierce opposition from conservative groups.
articles.description: More than 100 countries have outlawed marital rape, but a large part of South Asia has not.

articles.headline: Donald Trump asks Vladimir Putin to halt military aggression
articles.title: Donald Trump urges Vladimir Putin to end ‘military aggression’ in Europe
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump stated on November 26, 2026, that he requested Russian leader Vladimir Putin to withdraw military aggression in Europe to facilitate a quick peace agreement with Ukraine. The remarks follow Trump's meetings in China and discussions with North Atlantic Treaty Organization chief Mark Rutte, amid rising European security concerns regarding Russian provocations.
articles.description: Donald Trump said he had requested Vladimir Putin when they met in China last week, adding that he thought it would help lead to a deal to end Moscow's grinding war in Ukraine

articles.headline: Senior officials from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye meet over Mecca defence pact
articles.title: Can the Mecca pact turn its collective defence promise into real support?
articles.summary: Top defence and foreign officials from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye gathered in Islamabad on Friday to advance their Mecca Joint Defence Agreement amid ongoing Houthi attacks. While Pakistan has pledged defensive air and ground support for the kingdom, officials have ruled out offensive operations inside Yemen, highlighting a delicate diplomatic balance between regional military alliance commitments and ongoing mediation efforts with Iran.
articles.description: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye meet in Islamabad as Houthi attacks on the kingdom continue and Iran talks stay open.

articles.headline: Teenager in Rajasthan uses child helpline to halt forced wedding
articles.title: In Rajasthan, the girls who refuse to be spoken for
articles.summary: A sixteen-year-old student in Sikar successfully prevented her arranged marriage by repeatedly contacting the national child helpline via borrowed phones when her family scheduled the ceremony without her consent. District Child Protection Officer Gargi Sharma stated that authorities obtained a court injunction within seventy-two hours of the first alert, stopping the wedding while keeping the student's identity anonymous.
articles.description: Rajasthan ranks sixth among India’s States with the highest prevalence of child marriage, according to the latest National Family Health Survey (2023-24). Poverty, the lack of education, and entrenched customs such as atta-satta, reinforced by a skewed sex ratio, continue to fuel the practice, particularly in tribal and rural areas. Now, a growing number of girls, empowered by education and greater access to social media, are saying no, reports Ashok Kumar. Meanwhile, the United Nations has declared November 27 as the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage

articles.headline: European Union leaders defer budget negotiations after failing to bridge spending divisions
articles.title: EU leaders fail to bridge budget splits as talks stall
articles.summary: European Union leaders deferred negotiations on their 2028 through 2034 budget after a twelve-hour summit in Brussels on Thursday ended in deep division. Member states argued over spending priorities, aid for Ukraine, and a proposed reduction of up to 230 billion euros. The European Council announced that a new two-day summit starting on December 17 would revive the stalled budget talks.
articles.description: Aid for Ukraine was among the disputes as EU members hope to conclude talks by the end of the year.

articles.headline: Israel criticised for utilizing south Lebanon Christian villages in strategy
articles.title: Israel uses south Lebanon Christian villages to try to divide and conquer
articles.summary: Israeli military spokesperson Ella Waweya posted a video from a classroom in Dibil, drawing heavy condemnation from Lebanese officials. Experts state that Israel permits Christian villages in southern Lebanon to remain during the ongoing conflict as part of a divide-and-conquer strategy. Meanwhile, municipal leaders like Ain Ebl president Ayoub Khreish report living under strict military occupation and severe movement restrictions.
articles.description: Israel is trying to fragment Lebanon by separating its Christian residents in south Lebanon from the rest.

articles.headline: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva appoints Luiz Carlos Trabuco Finance Minister
articles.title: Brazil’s Lula appoints private banker as Finance Minister
articles.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva appointed private banking executive Luiz Carlos Trabuco as Finance Minister for his upcoming term. The selection of the Bradesco bank chairman aims to reassure the business community following market instability after the October election. Lula will begin his fourth non-consecutive term in January, having secured acceptance from Trabuco during a meeting.
articles.description: Lula’s shock election win in October sent stock markets tumbling while the national currency, the real, weakened significantly

articles.headline: New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon loses his parliamentary majority
articles.title: New Zealand PM Luxon loses majority, centrists now kingmakers
articles.summary: New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon lost his parliamentary majority after final election results showed his coalition fell one seat short. Centrist party leader Qiulae Wong emerged as the decisive kingmaker following the November seventh poll. Both major political figures held meetings with Wong, though the process to determine the nation's next government could take several weeks.
articles.description: If Christopher Luxon doesn’t strike a deal with centrist newcomers Opportunity, the country could be headed for another election

articles.headline: U.S. President Donald Trump states Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang poses no security threat
articles.title: President Donald Trump insists Nvidia CEO not a security threat
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump declared that Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang is not a security threat based on information he reviewed. Huang previously resigned following revelations regarding an affair with a business executive linked to intelligence, though the board later reinstated him. Trump defended his administration's intervention in the company decision during remarks at his Mar-a-Lago estate.
articles.description: Jensen Huang sudden resignation saw the stock price of Nvidia plummet, before a shock decision by the board to reinstate him saw a partial rebound

articles.headline: Severe Thanksgiving storms leave nearly a million without power across US
articles.title: Thanksgiving storms leave nearly a million without power across the US
articles.summary: Powerful storms and strong winds disrupted Thanksgiving celebrations on Thursday by knocking out electricity for nearly one million customers, primarily along the East Coast. FlightAware reported over 2,000 flight delays and 400 cancellations nationwide. The National Weather Service issued wind advisories across multiple states, while heavy snowfall impacted the Midwest and coastal areas experienced severe flooding.
articles.description: Severe weather across the US causes outages and flight delays as families and friends gather for the annual holiday.

articles.headline: Binance lifts withdrawal suspension following massive crypto hack
articles.title: Binance lifts withdrawal suspension after $6.3 billion crypto heist
articles.summary: According to the company, cryptocurrency platform Binance completed its withdrawal recovery work and ended its suspension following a record theft last month. The organization noted that a small number of networks remain temporarily paused for maintenance and planned upgrades separate from the resolved security incident, allowing the vast majority of users to resume normal account transactions.
articles.description: Binance ​said on ‌Thursday its ​withdrawal recovery ⁠work is complete

articles.headline: Donald Trump discusses regional security and Iran during phone calls
articles.title: Trump downplays Russia, China support for Iran during talks with US troops
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump asserted on November 26, 2026, that Iran possesses missiles capable of reaching Europe while minimizing the significance of military support from Russia and China. Speaking to deployed service members for the Thanksgiving holiday, Trump emphasized the ongoing necessity of Middle East peace and warned that military action remains an option against Iranian targets.
articles.description: Trump praises US troops for their role in the war on Iran and says he has spoken to Netanyahu in recent days.

articles.headline: Delegates at the UN climate conference in Antalya fail to reach consensus
articles.title: Why is COP31 perceived to be a failure? | Explained
articles.summary: Negotiations at the 31st UN climate conference concluded on November 20, 2026, in Antalya, Turkiye, without agreement on the Antalya Pact. According to reports, a deadlock over phasing out fossil fuels delayed proceedings by 48 hours. The political stalemate centred on a cover text proposed by conference president and Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum.
articles.description: Parties agreed to arrangements for the Adaptation Fund to serve the Paris Agreement exclusively once the first share of proceeds under Article 6.4 (the Paris Agreement’s carbon-market mechanism) turns into revenue, though this fund is practically underfunded

articles.headline: India and UAE agree to accelerate joint defense equipment production
articles.title: India, UAE to accelerate joint development and production of next generation defence equipment
articles.summary: India and the United Arab Emirates agreed to boost co-development and co-production partnerships in next-generation military equipment during the fourteenth meeting of their Joint Defence Cooperation Committee in Abu Dhabi. Co-chaired by Indian Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh and UAE Under Secretary Lieutenant General Ibrahim Nasser M. Al Alawi, the talks advanced bilateral defense ties.
articles.description: Meeting provided strategic direction to initiatives under the India-UAE Strategic Defence Partnership Framework, signed during PM’s May visit to the UAE

articles.headline: Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia chief executive officer
articles.title: Jensen Huang needs a new playbook for his second innings at Nvidia
articles.summary: Co-founder Jensen Huang resumed his role at Nvidia in California on November 23, 2026, following intensive lobbying by tech billionaires. Huang apologized to employees after a scandal-driven exit wiped out a quarter of the company value. His reinstatement immediately boosted market capitalization by nearly a trillion dollars as company stock surged.
articles.description: Returning to Nvidia’s Santa Clara headquarters in California on Monday (November 23, 2026), and standing on the ground floor of the atrium, Jensen Huang apologised to employees and vowed to be a better CEO

articles.headline: Ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina plans a December return to Bangladesh
articles.title: Sheikh Hasina's planned return puts Bangladesh on edge - and India in a bind
articles.summary: Ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina announced plans to return to Bangladesh on December sixteenth, prompting defiance from authorities who promised immediate arrest and execution of her death sentence. Hasina fled to Delhi in August 2024 following a student-led uprising. Her banned Awami League party has continued demonstrations and clashes, while the Indian foreign ministry stated the extradition request remains under examination.
articles.description: The ousted prime minister's December homecoming plan deepens Dhaka-Delhi tensions and risks fresh unrest.

articles.headline: Inside Ukraine’s power crisis amid its war with Russia
articles.title: Inside Ukraine’s power crisis amid its war with Russia
articles.description: Electricity and water shortages have become part of daily life in Ukraine’s capital.

articles.headline: Argentine legislature passes bill barring Central Bank from funding government spending
articles.title: Argentina bars Central Bank from printing money to fund government spending
articles.summary: The Argentinian Chamber of Deputies approved a measure prohibiting the Central Bank from printing money for government expenses on Thursday, aiming to curb inflation. Supported by President Javier Milei, the legislation marks a shift in monetary policy following years of fiscal instability. Meanwhile, the Senate advanced a separate bill to suspend primary elections ahead of the October vote.
articles.description: The South American country's Senate also advances proposal to suspend primary elections ahead of 2027 presidential race.

articles.headline: Drone attack in Kuwait kills two Italian technicians working on defense system
articles.title: Two Italians killed in drone attack in Kuwait
articles.summary: Two Italian technicians from Rheinmetall were killed on Thursday when drones struck Kuwaiti military installations, marking a fatal escalation in regional tensions. Kuwait and Italy attributed the attack to Iran, though Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi denied Tehran's involvement. The incident follows heightened regional conflict involving United States and Iranian forces over the Strait of Hormuz.
articles.description: ‘Around 2:00 p.m. today, several Iranian-made drones targeted Kuwaiti military installations, including an air-defence detection station where two Italian technicians from Rheinmetall were working,’ Italian FM Antonio Tajani said

articles.headline: Israeli settlers damage Palestinian homes in West Bank village attack
articles.title: Israeli settlers damage Palestinian family’s homes in West Bank attack
articles.summary: Israeli settlers used a bulldozer to smash the concrete foundations of two two-storey houses belonging to the Tubasi family in the West Bank village of Jaloud on Thursday. Lawyer Ghiath Nasser attributed the escalation to a lack of law enforcement. The incident follows a surge in West Bank settler attacks documented by the United Nations since the start of the year.
articles.description: The Tubasi family was forced out months ago and has been denied a return by settlers despite an Israeli court order.

articles.headline: Zelensky questions 'strange' Trump-Putin friendship in BBC interview
articles.title: Zelensky questions 'strange' Trump-Putin friendship in BBC interview
articles.description: The Ukrainian president tells the BBC that Russia's Vladimir Putin should not be treated as a friend.

articles.headline: Two Italian technicians killed by Iranian strike in Kuwait
articles.title: Two Italians killed in strike in Kuwait, as Iran denies responsibility
articles.summary: Two Italian nationals working as technicians for German firm Rheinmetall died following an explosion caused by a drone attack on a facility in Kuwait, according to Italy's foreign ministry. Kuwait's defence ministry reported the casualties resulted from falling shrapnel after intercepting Iranian drones, while Iran denied responsibility for any offensive operations during the ongoing regional conflict involving U.S. forces.
articles.description: The pair were technicians for German company Rheinmetall, according to Italy's foreign ministry.

articles.headline: Refinery attack in Saudi Arabia kills worker and halts operations
articles.title: Attack on Saudi’s Jazan refinery kills one person, disrupts operations
articles.summary: An aerial projectile struck an oil refinery in Jazan, Saudi Arabia, on Thursday, killing a Nepali worker and injuring others while causing a fire and temporary operational disruptions, according to the Ministry of Energy. The Saudi-led military coalition blamed the Iranian-backed Houthi movement for the strike and responded by destroying a missile launch platform in Hodeidah, Yemen.
articles.description: The attack killed a Nepali national, injured several people and sparked a fire, Saudi Energy Ministry says.

articles.headline: Winter storms displace thousands of Palestinians in Gaza tents
articles.title: Why are winter rains forcing Palestinians in Gaza to flee again?
articles.summary: Heavy November rains flooded roughly 70,000 tents across Gaza within twelve hours, affecting over 226,000 people and forcing hundreds to relocate again, according to United Nations figures. The storms and subsequent infrastructure failures caused multiple fatalities while worsening health risks, as shelter supplies remained stalled at borders due to Israeli restrictions.
articles.description: Israeli restrictions on humanitarian aid, damaged buildings and flooded tents leave displaced Palestinians vulnerable.

articles.headline: Federal judge blocks administration restrictions on birthright citizenship
articles.title: Judge strikes down Trump’s latest restrictions on US birthright citizenship
articles.summary: United States District Court Judge Christopher Cooper ruled on Wednesday to block the administration's policy denying birthright citizenship to certain children born to non-citizen parents. The decision marks another legal setback for executive orders attempting to restrict constitutional citizenship guarantees previously upheld by the Supreme Court in landmark rulings.
articles.description: After a Supreme Court ruling against it, the Trump administration had tried a narrower set of restrictions.

articles.headline: What will Trump’s latest tariffs mean for the world?
articles.title: What will Trump’s latest tariffs mean for the world?
articles.description: New measures come after previous trade tariffs ruled illegal.

articles.headline: Kushner explains the ‘good thing’ about Gaza’s destruction
articles.title: Kushner explains the ‘good thing’ about Gaza’s destruction
articles.description: Jared Kushner says the “good thing” about Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza is that it can be built into “something new”.

articles.headline: Trump demands investigation into US economic growth data released prior to midterms
articles.title: Trump calls GDP data released before midterms ‘fake’, demands investigation
articles.summary: Former United States President Donald Trump demanded a federal investigation into revised third-quarter gross domestic product figures released by the Department of Commerce, alleging without evidence that the initial data were intentionally manipulated before the November 3 elections. The Bureau of Economic Analysis revised annualized growth up to 4.3 percent from 3.4 percent. Officials routinely update statistics as complete source data becomes available.
articles.description: President says it was a deliberate decision to release 'fake' growth numbers before US midterm elections.

articles.headline: EU leaders debate long-term budget and financial aid for Ukraine
articles.title: EU leaders struggle to agree on long-term budget, $49bn Ukraine loan
articles.summary: European Union leaders gathered in Brussels for an extraordinary summit to negotiate a nearly $1.76 trillion budget proposal for 2028 to 2034 alongside a $49 billion loan for Ukraine. Divisions emerged as some officials advocated for fiscal restraint while others prioritized defense and funding. Securing unanimous approval remains uncertain amid upcoming national elections across several member states.
articles.description: The bloc is holding an extraordinary summit in Brussels to discuss its budget proposal for 2028 to 2034.

articles.headline: Saudi-led coalition launches airstrikes on Houthi-held Sanaa
articles.title: Yemen's Houthi-held capital hit after group targets Riyadh
articles.summary: The Saudi-led coalition conducted retaliatory airstrikes against Houthi-held territory in Yemen, including the capital city of Sanaa, after intercepting ballistic missiles targeting Riyadh. The military exchanges follow a recent escalation in Yemen's revived civil war, which resumed in July following the breakdown of a multi-year truce, causing extensive damage and rising casualties across the region.
articles.description: The exchanges between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen have become near-daily in the country's revived civil war

articles.headline: Supreme Court rules PMLA property attachment benches need judicial members
articles.title: PMLA Bench adjudicating property attachment must have at least one judicial member: Supreme Court
articles.summary: India's Supreme Court ruled that benches adjudicating property attachments under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act must include at least one judicial member. Chief Justice Surya Kant delivered the judgment, emphasizing that legal expertise is required to evaluate civil rights before the state can confiscate assets suspected of constituting proceeds from criminal activities.
articles.description: The PMLA permits the State to reach into a citizen’s estate even before guilt is proved, the Supreme Court notes

articles.headline: Israeli airstrikes in Gaza kill nine people including Khaled Abu Nada
articles.title: Israel kills nine in Gaza, including Hamas-appointed deputy Education Minister, officials say
articles.summary: Israeli airstrikes and gunfire killed at least nine Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, including Hamas-appointed deputy education minister Khaled Abu Nada. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirmed the targeted killing as part of ongoing military operations against Hamas officials. Palestinian and Israeli tallies indicate that thousands have died since a ceasefire was established in October 2025.
articles.description: Medics said an Israeli airstrike hit an apartment in Deir Al-Balah in central Gaza Strip, killing ‌Khaled Abu Nada, the Deputy Gaza Education Minister, and his wife.

articles.headline: Nvidia halts AI server shipments to four Southeast Asian nations
articles.title: Nvidia stops shipping AI servers to four Southeast Asian nations
articles.summary: U.S. tech company Nvidia instructed manufacturing partners to stop shipping computer servers containing artificial intelligence chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, according to the Financial Times.
