The reported halt on November 26, 2026, follows tightened U.S. export controls aimed at cracking down on chip smuggling and the grey market renting computing power to Chinese entities, significantly impacting regional data centre operations.
articles.description: The Financial Times report said Nvidia had instructed manufacturing partners to stop shipping computer servers to buyers in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia

articles.headline: Kremlin accuses Ukraine of trying to widen conflict to seas
articles.title: Kremlin accuses Ukraine of trying to widen conflict zone to Mediterranean and Baltic seas
articles.summary: The Kremlin claimed on November 26, 2026, that Ukraine is attempting to expand its war into the Mediterranean and Baltic seas through terrorist activities, calling the actions very dangerous. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov responded to a joint U.S. and NATO statement urging restraint, following recent Ukrainian drone strikes that hit a Russian naval corvette in Libya and a cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland.
articles.description: Ukraine sank a Russian naval corvette in a Libyan port using maritime drones on Sunday, a day after ​it carried out a ‌drone strike on a Russian military-linked cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland

articles.headline: President Murmu calls pending court cases a major justice challenge
articles.title: Pendency a challenge to justice delivery, says President
articles.summary: Indian President Droupadi Murmu stated on November 26, 2026, that the high volume of pending court cases creates a major challenge for the nation's justice delivery system and hinders timely verdicts. Speaking at Supreme Court Constitution Day celebrations, she noted judicial efforts involving technology and special courts, while Chief Justice Surya Kant emphasised ongoing initiatives to ensure broader access for citizens.
articles.description: At the Constitution Day celebrations organised by the Supreme Court, President Murmu listed measures used to improve timely delivery of justice

articles.headline: Myanmar president rejects international court genocide orders
articles.title: Myanmar says it will not fully comply with ICJ genocide orders
articles.summary: Myanmar's military-backed president Min Aung Hlaing stated on November 26, 2026, that his administration will not fully comply with UN International Court of Justice measures. The court previously ruled that security forces committed genocide against the Rohingya minority during 2017 operations in Rakhine state. The crackdown displaced over 730,000 people to Bangladesh, according to records.
articles.description: The ruling by ‌the ⁠ICJ, the first instance of the UN court holding a ⁠state responsible for genocide, is final but the court has very limited options to enforce it

articles.headline: Ncp-sp announces support for delimitation bills despite opposition bloc friction
articles.title: NCP-SP announces support to delimitation, Congress calls it ‘unfortunate’
articles.summary: The Nationalist Congress Party-Sharadchandra Pawar announced on November 27, 2026, that it will support upcoming delimitation bills in Parliament. The decision caused friction within the opposition Indian National Developmental, Inclusive Alliance, prompting criticism from the Congress party and Shiv Sena. The Union Cabinet approved the legislation, which provides a proportionate increase in seats and implements the Women's Reservation law.
articles.description: NCP-SP leader Jitendra Awhad said that while the party decided to support the Centre’s move, which has been opposed by the INDIA bloc, it would attend the bloc’s meeting on November 28

articles.headline: Bombay High Court allows Tata Sons board meeting to proceed
articles.title: Bombay High Court gives go-ahead for Tata Sons board meeting on November 30
articles.summary: The Bombay High Court declined urgent relief requested by two Tata Trusts seeking to defer a Tata Sons board meeting or block N. Chandrasekaran from voting. Justice Abhay Ahuja ruled the November 30 meeting may proceed, though any outcomes remain subject to final court orders. The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and RD Tata Trust previously filed suits challenging Chandrasekaran's reappointment as executive chairman.
articles.description: The High Court says any outcome of the meeting would be subject to its final orders, declines any urgent relief on pleas challenging Chandrasekaran’s reappointment as executive chairman

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu legislator arrested following sexual harassment allegations by officer
articles.title: Kallakurichi TVK MLA Arul Vignesh arrested on charges of harassing IAS officer
articles.summary: Police arrested Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam legislator C. Arul Vignesh in Kallakurichi on Friday evening following allegations of sexual harassment made by a woman Indian Administrative Service officer. According to police sources, the arrest was led by Investigating Officer Shristi Singh after the Madras High Court directed authorities to pursue the formal complaint filed under the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act.
articles.description: The TVK MLA was subsequently brought to the Circuit House in Kallakurichi on the Salem-Ulundurpet highway for questioning, where a large posse of police personnel has been deployed

articles.headline: Two Italians killed by drone strike debris in Kuwait facility
articles.title: Two Italians killed by ‘drone strike debris’ in Kuwait
articles.summary: Two Italian technicians working at an air-defence surveillance station in Kuwait died from injuries sustained after being hit by falling debris during an Iranian drone interception. Kuwait's Ministry of Defence reported that two other workers, a Kuwaiti and a Pakistani national, were wounded in the incident at a vital site, while Iranian state media quoted military officials denying any offensive operations in the region.
articles.description: Iran has strongly denied any involvement in the fatal incident.

articles.headline: Taiwan holds local elections as Chinese military pressure and warnings escalate
articles.title: Taiwan votes in local elections as China sends warplanes, lambastes Taipei candidate
articles.summary: Taiwan held elections for mayors and county chiefs across twenty-two cities and counties on November 28, 2026. The vote occurred while Chinese state media targeted ruling party candidate Puma Shen and Taiwan's Defence Ministry reported thirty-three aircraft encircling the island. Campaigning focused on local infrastructure and municipal leadership ahead of upcoming presidential and parliamentary races.
articles.description: The main race to watch is for the Taipei mayorship, where Chiang ‌has faced a stiff challenge from Shen, an academic-turned-lawmaker and an expert on China’s information warfare

articles.headline: European Union leaders appoint Pablo Hernandez de Cos as next European Central Bank chief
articles.title: Spanish economist to become new European Central Bank chief
articles.summary: European Union leaders have appointed Pablo Hernandez de Cos as the next head of the Frankfurt-based European Central Bank, succeeding Christine Lagarde in February. The fifty-five-year-old Spaniard, currently heading the Bank for International Settlements, will become the first person from his country to lead the institution. Diplomats praise his pragmatism as he assumes the role during a challenging period for the eurozone economy.
articles.description: Economist Pablo Hernandez de Cos was announced after a meeting of eurozone leaders.

articles.headline: Military helicopter crash in remote Peru kills eight personnel during rescue mission
articles.title: Eight killed in Peruvian military helicopter crash
articles.summary: Eight military personnel died in a helicopter crash near Sanabamba in Peru during an army patrol evacuation mission. According to the Peruvian ministry of defence, the pilot Enzo Espinoza Roque survived and was evacuated to Lima for specialized medical treatment. The aircraft went down in the Apurimac, Ene, and Mantaro rivers valley, an area known for drug trafficking and coca cultivation.
articles.description: The pilot was the sole survivor of the crash during a rescue mission in a remote area known for drug trafficking.

articles.headline: U.K. net migration falls to lowest level since 1997
articles.title: U.K. net migration falls to lowest since 1997; Indians largest foreign group entering and leaving the country
articles.summary: Official U.K. government figures released on November 26, 2026, show net migration dropped to 77,000, driven largely by a decline in non-European Union arrivals. Indians constituted the largest foreign nationality group both immigrating and emigrating. The dramatic decrease follows stricter policies implemented after record highs during the administration of Boris Johnson.
articles.description: Some 44,000 Indians arrived in the U.K. for work-related reasons, 77,000 to study, and 5,000 for other reasons. Some 28,000 Indians on work visas left the U.K. and 55,000 on study visas departed

articles.headline: Russian President Vladimir Putin unveils nuclear submarine and announces fleet expansion
articles.title: Putin unveils new nuclear submarine
articles.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin unveiled the new nuclear-powered Perm submarine at the Sevmash shipyard in Severodvinsk on November 27, 2026. Putin stated that Russia will add five more submarines to the naval fleet by 2030, including three Yasen-M class vessels. Nuclear submarines provide a vital retaliatory strike capability through covert underwater operations and global cruise missile reach.
articles.description: Nuclear-powered submarines are a key part of Russia's nuclear deterrent because their ability to operate covertly underwater ensures a retaliatory strike capability in the event of an attack

articles.headline: Turkish authorities dismantle pro-opposition news channel Halk TV as arrests continue
articles.title: Turkish officials 'destroyed' pro-opposition TV channel, owner tells BBC
articles.summary: Turkish authorities have taken control of Halk TV and arrested nine individuals linked to the pro-opposition news channel on charges including money laundering and spreading misleading information. London-based owner Cafer Mahiroglu told the BBC that the allegations are false and that the government is seeking complete control over domestic media following previous crackdowns on independent outlets.
articles.description: The headquarters of Halk TV were raided last month, the latest in a series of crackdowns on news sources deemed critical of the government.

articles.headline: Two dead after Iranian drone attack on Kuwait
articles.title: Two dead after Iranian drone attack on Kuwait
articles.description: Kuwait’s army says two Italian workers were killed and four others were injured in an Iranian drone attack.

articles.headline: UK and EU to publish post-Brexit trade and emissions treaties
articles.title: New UK-EU treaty has 10-year termination clause
articles.summary: The British government and the European Union plan to release two post-Brexit treaties covering food exports and carbon trading on Thursday. The food export agreement includes a ten-year termination clause requiring infrastructure rebuilding costs if ended. European affairs minister Hamish Falconer stated the measures will eliminate paperwork and reduce business expenses, although political figures have expressed differing views on the arrangement.
articles.description: Text of the treaties was published this afternoon, alongside legislation designed to enact the bulk of the deal.

articles.headline: New Zealand reaches 330 for eight at lunch against India on day two
articles.title: IND vs NZ second Test: India stumbles to 59 for 3; Akash Deep takes five wickets in Kiwis’ 356
articles.summary: New Zealand advanced to 330 for eight at lunch on the second day of the second Test at Hagley Oval, with Tom Blundell remaining unbeaten on 80 runs. Akash Deep took four wickets for India, maintaining his strong performance despite a dropped catch that cost him a five-wicket haul. The hosts added 84 runs to their overnight total during the first session, bolstered by resilient lower-order partnerships.
articles.description: Akash Deep was the standout bowler for India, returning impressive figures of 5 for 99, while Brar (2/78) and Anshul Kamboj (2/79) enabled to dismiss New Zealand for 356

articles.headline: Severe US East Coast storms ease as power restoration and parade preparations begin
articles.title: Parts of US clean up after Thanksgiving storm lashes East Coast
articles.summary: Heavy rain and flooding began easing along the United States East Coast as power was gradually restored to hundreds of thousands of customers after holiday storms disrupted travel and caused widespread outages. In New York City, preparations resumed for the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade following a rare weather-related postponement, while the National Weather Service warned of lingering precipitation.
articles.description: Power is being slowly restored to hundreds of thousands of customers following a round of heavy wind, rain and snow.

articles.headline: Bulgarians demand action by French after Marseille match violence
articles.title: Bulgarians demand action by French after Marseille match violence
articles.description: Bulgarians protested at the French embassy after violence at a Europa League match hospitalised six Levski Sofia fans.

articles.headline: US Democrats weigh funding bill strategy to restrict military operations in Iran
articles.title: Can Trump continue with Iran war despite funding restrictions?
articles.summary: As federal funding approaches an expiration date on December 11, Democratic lawmakers are considering leveraging the upcoming budget package to pressure President Donald Trump by restricting offensive operations in the ongoing war on Iran. According to experts, while the measure could constrain executive spending, a potential presidential veto and existing Pentagon resources mean it may not immediately halt the conflict.
articles.description: A Congress budget bill could serve as a pressure tactic on Trump to end the war but could also trigger a shutdown.

articles.headline: India hosts first Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Civilisational Dialogue Forum in Delhi
articles.title: What is the Indraprastha Communique issued after SCO Civilizational Forum in New Delhi? | Explained
articles.summary: India hosted the inaugural Civilisational Dialogue Forum of the 10-nation Shanghai Cooperation Organisation in New Delhi from November 20 to 22. Organised by the Ministry of Culture and the Ministry of External Affairs at Purana Qila, the three-day summit concluded with the adoption of the Indraprastha Communiqué. The initiative was proposed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi to strengthen people-to-people ties and promote shared cultural heritage.
articles.description: The dialogue, which was organized by the Ministry of Culture and the Ministry of External Affairs, was proposed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the SCO leaders’ Summit in Tianjin last year and adopted by the SCO Council

articles.headline: Serbia schedules early presidential election for December 27 following former leader's departure
articles.title: Serbia sets Presidential election for December 27 after students won Parliamentary vote
articles.summary: Serbia's Parliament Speaker Aleksandar Cupic announced an early presidential vote for December 27 following the September resignation of former President Aleksandar Vucic. The upcoming election follows a student movement's victory over Mr. Vucic's party in an October 25 parliamentary ballot, concluding fourteen years of virtually unchallenged rule and prompting a surge in official detentions.
articles.description: The Presidential vote will be held after a student movement defeated Mr. Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive Party in an early Parliamentary ballot on October 25

articles.headline: Australia drops veteran spinner Nathan Lyon for test series against New Zealand
articles.title: Nathan Lyon’s 13-year reign as Australia’s top-choice spinner ends
articles.summary: Australia ended Nathan Lyon's 13-year reign as first-choice spinner by dropping the 39-year-old veteran from the 13-man squad for the upcoming test series against New Zealand. Chief selector George Bailey announced that spinner Corey Rocchiccioli and batter Jack Clayton received their first test call-ups. The opening match of the four-test series begins on December 9 in Perth.
articles.description: The 39-year-old off spinner was dropped for the four-Test cricket series against New Zealand

articles.headline: Thousands of Puerto Ricans protest in San Juan over high electricity rates
articles.title: Thousands of Puerto Ricans join ‘Day of National Outrage’ protest
articles.summary: Thousands of Puerto Ricans demonstrated in San Juan on Friday during a Day of National Outrage organised by about 30 groups. Protesters expressed deep frustration over record-high electricity rates, unreliable power services, and a surging cost of living under Governor Jenniffer Gonzalez. Organisers estimated that 8,000 people participated in the march, which forced the closure of a main highway.
articles.description: Anger and frustration erupt over record-high electricity rates, surging cost of living and deteriorating basic services.

articles.headline: Canadian prosecutors seek 25-year prison term for Kenneth Law
articles.title: 'Poison seller' Kenneth Law apologises in court to the families of his victims
articles.summary: Canadian prosecutors are recommending a 25-year prison sentence for Kenneth Law, who pleaded guilty to aiding the suicide deaths of 14 people in Ontario. Crown Attorney Kathleen Doherty described Law as a predator who sold toxic chemicals online for financial gain. Defence lawyers argued for a 12-year sentence, stating Law held a misguided belief that he was helping victims who were already struggling with mental health issues.
articles.description: The Canadian man, who pleaded guilty to 14 counts of aiding and abetting suicide earlier this year, said he was remorseful for his actions.

articles.headline: Bollywood musical Eetha inspires renewed focus on life of Tamasha star Vithabai Narayangaonkar
articles.title: The Indian 'Tamasha queen' whose fans paid for a show that never happened
articles.summary: The life of Vithabai Narayangaonkar, an acclaimed traditional folk theatre artist from Maharashtra, has inspired a Bollywood musical titled Eetha directed by Laxman Utekar. Vithabai toured extensively and gained widespread fame during the golden age of Tamasha. However, family members and scholars note that despite her artistic success, she suffered severe financial struggles and died in debt in January 2002.
articles.description: A new Bollywood flim spotlights the remarkable life of dancer and singer Vithabhai Narayangaonkar.

articles.headline: Swedish clinic offers ADHD and autism diagnosis reassessments to remove career barriers
articles.title: A clinic is reassessing people with ADHD and autism diagnoses - but critics fear it could deepen stigma
articles.summary: A government-funded psychiatric clinic in Sweden has launched a dedicated reassessment service for autism and ADHD diagnoses to help individuals overcome career barriers such as restrictions on joining the police force. While some young adults welcome the opportunity to update their medical records, critics and non-profits warn that the approach could deepen stigma and leave individuals without necessary lifelong support.
articles.description: While many people find a diagnosis for ADHD or autism affirming, a government-funded clinic in Sweden is re-assessing people who feel it does not reflect them.

articles.headline: At least eight migrants found dead on rescue boat near Spain's Canary Islands
articles.title: At least eight found dead on migrant boat off Spain’s Canary Islands
articles.summary: The Spanish maritime rescue service announced that at least eight migrants died aboard a boat carrying about 100 people near the Canary Islands. Six survivors were airlifted to hospital in serious condition following the rescue 39 nautical miles south of El Hierro. The incident occurs amid a surge in Atlantic arrivals ahead of Spain's general elections, where immigration remains a prominent political issue.
articles.description: Six people airlifted to hospital in serious condition, Spanish rescue service says.

articles.headline: China calls border situation stable following military talks with India
articles.title: Situation in India-China border areas remains ‘generally stable’, says China
articles.summary: The Chinese Defence Ministry stated that bilateral border regions remain generally stable after concluding high-level military discussions with India. Senior Colonel Chen Xi confirmed that both nations communicate through diplomatic and military channels to maintain peace. Meanwhile, recent Corps Commander-level talks focused on establishing engagement protocols along the frontier in Arunachal Pradesh before winter conditions set in.
articles.description: On November 24, 2026, India and China concluded a second round of Corps Commander-level talks aimed at easing tensions along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in Arunachal Pradesh

articles.headline: Taiwan holds referendum on reviving nuclear power amid rising energy demands
articles.title: Will Taiwan vote to revive nuclear power – and why does that matter for AI?
articles.summary: Voters in Taiwan are deciding whether to abolish the nuclear-free homeland policy and restart atomic energy to support the growing semiconductor industry and address energy security concerns. The referendum coincides with local elections and follows previous shutdowns, increasing regional tensions, and soaring power demand from artificial intelligence processing. The ruling Democratic Progressive Party faces pressure to shift its stance as the island imports most of its energy.
articles.description: Voters will decide on Saturday whether to scrap the country's 'nuclear-free homeland' policy.

articles.headline: United States proposes new trade tariffs against fourteen partners
articles.title: Are Trump’s tariffs aimed at securing US-friendly trade deals?
articles.summary: The administration of United States President Donald Trump proposed new trade tariffs ranging from 20 percent to 40 percent against 14 key trading partners, including China and India. Announced by the United States Trade Representative on Wednesday, the measures respond to alleged unfair trading practices and industrial overcapacity while serving as leverage in ongoing trade negotiations.
articles.description: New US policy threatens further tariff hikes on China, India, Vietnam if trade negotiations fall through.

articles.headline: Cheaper generic HIV prevention injection arrives in Africa
articles.title: Hope for millions as cheaper HIV prevention jab reaches Africa
articles.summary: Zambia received the first global shipment of a generic version of lenacapavir on Wednesday, with deliveries to Uganda expected soon. Administered twice a year, the injection costs approximately $40 annually per person. The Global Fund stated the rollout aims to expand access across low- and middle-income countries where sub-Saharan Africa bears the highest disease burden.
articles.description: Lenacapavir, administered as an injection twice a year, is nearly 100% effective at preventing HIV infection.

articles.headline: Makkah alliance countries review regional security and condemn Houthi attacks
articles.title: Makkah alliance countries review regional security situation, condemn Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
articles.summary: Top officials of the Makkah Defence Alliance met in Islamabad to review regional security and condemn attacks by Yemen's Houthi militia on Saudi Arabia. Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar confirmed commitment to the trilateral pact. The meeting addressed practical implementation of collective defence provisions, intelligence sharing, and regional de-escalation efforts following recent escalations involving Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkiye.
articles.description: ‘The committee reviewed the evolving regional security situation and reaffirmed the determination of the three countries to continue working collectively towards peace, security, and stability,’ said Ishaq Dar

articles.headline: Supreme Court seeks response from Centre and protest organisers on demonstration rules
articles.title: Plea seeks guidelines to govern protests; Supreme Court issues notice to Centre, CJP leaders
articles.summary: The Supreme Court agreed to examine a petition filed by a lawyers body requesting standard operating procedures for public demonstrations. The Bench issued notices to the central government and political leaders following concerns regarding unauthorised protests held in Delhi earlier in the year. The petition emphasises balancing democratic dissent with public order and the protection of normal civic life.
articles.description: Supreme Court to examine plea for uniform protest guidelines; Centre, CJP leaders issued notice as demands SOPs to regulate demonstrations

articles.headline: Myanmar refuses to comply with parts of ICJ genocide ruling
articles.title: Myanmar refuses to comply with parts of ICJ genocide ruling
articles.summary: Leader Min Aung Hlaing announced that Myanmar will reject inappropriate requirements from the International Court of Justice ruling that found the country guilty of genocide. The landmark decision followed a 2017 military crackdown in Rakhine State that killed thousands of Rohingya Muslims and forced more than 700,000 to flee to Bangladesh.
articles.description: A landmark ruling by the International Court of Justice (ICJ) convicted Myanmar of genocide against its Rohingya minority.

articles.headline: Hamas says Israel targeted chief's son in Gaza strike
articles.title: Hamas says Israel tried to kill chief’s son in Gaza
articles.summary: Hamas stated that an Israeli strike in Gaza City targeted the adult son of political bureau chief Khalil al-Hayya, who reportedly survived. Separate incidents across the Palestinian territory resulted in additional casualties according to Gaza's civil defence agency and local medical facilities. The Israeli military stated it was reviewing the reported incidents amid an ongoing truce that has seen persistent violence since October 2025.
articles.description: ‘Izz al-Din al-Hayya, the youngest surviving son of Hamas political bureau chief Khalil al-Hayya, along with his family and the family of his late brother Azzam, survived an Israeli assassination attempt,’ a security source in Gaza told AFP

articles.headline: Israeli air strikes in Gaza kill eight Palestinians including Hamas official
articles.title: Hamas political official and wife among eight Palestinians killed in Israeli strikes on Gaza
articles.summary: Three Israeli air strikes across the Gaza Strip on Thursday killed eight Palestinians, including Hamas political official Khaled Abu Nada and his wife in Deir al-Balah. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirmed the death on social media, stating that approximately 80 Hamas officials have been killed over the past month as military operations continue.
articles.description: The killings are the latest from a series of near daily attacks by Israel against what it says are Hamas targets.

articles.headline: Ukraine drone attack kills five in Russian-occupied Zaporizhia
articles.title: Ukraine drone attack kills five in Russian-occupied Zaporizhia
articles.summary: At least five individuals died and three sustained injuries during a Ukrainian drone strike targeting a parking facility in Vesioloye within Russian-occupied Zaporizhia, according to Moscow-installed governor Yevgeny Balitsky. Meanwhile, Russian ballistic missiles struck Kyiv, hitting a shopping center and damaging military-industrial installations. The ongoing conflict has severely degraded Ukraine's energy infrastructure since the full-scale invasion commenced in February 2022.
articles.description: Russian forces launch ballistic missile attack on Ukrainian capital Kyiv, hitting a shopping centre and other buildings.

articles.headline: ‘Activists of rhythm’: Fighting Spain’s far-right through art
articles.title: ‘Activists of rhythm’: Fighting Spain’s far-right through art
articles.description: Madrid’s La Parceria and Espacio Afro cultural centres are using the arts to fight racism and boost migrant voices.

articles.headline: State attorneys general attempt to block Character.AI data sale
articles.title: 42 state AGs are trying to stop Character.AI from selling users’ chats
articles.summary: A bipartisan group consisting of forty-two state attorneys general is working to prevent chatbot developer Character.AI from auctioning off private chat records belonging to more than twenty-one million accounts during its Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings. Officials raised concerns that the proposed sale of data originating from over two million minors lacks adequate privacy protections, user deletion options, or restrictions on subsequent buyers.
articles.description: A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is trying to prevent Character.AI from selling off user data as it navigates Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings. In a deluge of nearly identical press releases, the various AGs accuse the company of planning to auction off "the private chat histories of more than 21 million U.S. accounts - […]

articles.headline: Kolkata Municipal Corporation delimitation bill sparks gerrymandering allegations
articles.title: In Kolkata, the BJP redraws power lines
articles.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party government in West Bengal passed a bill in the State Assembly on August 12, increasing the number of wards in the Kolkata Municipal Corporation from 144 to 209. Opposition members accused the ruling party of gerrymandering to gain an unfair advantage in upcoming local body elections. The delimitation exercise, which alters historical ward boundaries like the former ward number 58, has been challenged in the Supreme Court of India.
articles.description: The BJP government in West Bengal has taken up a delimitation exercise of civic bodies of the twin cities of Kolkata and Howrah, increasing the number of wards in both municipal corporations. Opposition parties have claimed there has been gerrymandering. Elections will impact over seven million people. Shrabana Chatterjee and Shiv Sahay Singh examine the delimitation exercise and the related legal challenges

articles.headline: US regulators approve SpaceX plan to deploy one million data satellites
articles.title: Musk's plan to send a million SpaceX data satellites into space approved
articles.summary: The Federal Communications Commission granted SpaceX permission to launch one million satellites into low-Earth orbit for space-based artificial intelligence data processing. FCC Chairman Brendan Carr endorsed the Starmind project as a technological advancement, while company owner Elon Musk expressed appreciation on social media. The initiative aims to alleviate terrestrial energy demands, though experts have raised concerns regarding space debris and orbital congestion.
articles.description: The Starmind constellation aims to be the most cost and energy-efficient way to meet the growing demand for AI computing power.

articles.headline: Highway fire near Cairo leaves thirty-one people dead
articles.title: Deadly fire erupts near Cairo killing dozens of people
articles.summary: A massive highway blaze in the Warraq neighborhood north of Cairo resulted in thirty-one fatalities and twenty-one injuries. State-owned media indicated the incident occurred when a high-voltage cable fell near a fuel tanker, causing the driver to lose control and overturn, which sprayed surrounding vehicles with petrol. Egypt's health ministry reported that the wounded individuals are receiving medical treatment at nearby hospitals.
articles.description: At least 31 people have died in a large fire on a busy highway in Cairo, after a fuel tanker overturned, says Egypt's health ministry.

articles.headline: Israeli strikes kill senior education official and others in Gaza
articles.title: Israeli attacks on Gaza kill senior education official, seven other people
articles.summary: Israeli air strikes across the Gaza Strip resulted in at least eight deaths, including Ministry of Education undersecretary Khaled Abu Nada and his wife in Deir el-Balah, according to local health officials. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz stated that Abu Nada was a Hamas figure. Gaza Health Ministry figures indicate that more than 1,600 Palestinians have died from attacks since a ceasefire took effect in October.
articles.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirms killing of Khaled Abu Nada, undersecretary of Education Ministry.

articles.headline: Omar Abdullah denies road construction on Amarnath route and accuses rivals
articles.title: Not a single foot of blacktopping done on Amarnath route, PDP-BJP stoking Hindu-Muslim discord: Omar Abdullah
articles.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah stated on November 27, 2026, that no road blacktopping occurred on the Amarnath route near Sheshnag lake. He accused the Bharatiya Janata Party and the Peoples Democratic Party of stoking Hindu-Muslim discord. A forest department report confirmed routine maintenance by the Border Roads Organisation, while opposition leaders demanded an on-site inspection of the area.
articles.description: ‘The BJP and those carrying the symbol of pen and inkpot are again trying to foment Hindu-Muslim discord over the Amarnath route,’ said Omar Abdullah

articles.headline: Capsized fuel tanker carrying diesel to be towed to Cartagena port
articles.title: Capsized tanker carrying 7,000 tonnes of diesel to be towed away from Ibiza
articles.summary: A Malta registered tanker carrying up to 7000 tonnes of diesel that capsized off Ibiza on Thursday will be towed to the Spanish port of Cartagena. Spanish transport ministry officials confirmed that all seventeen crew members were rescued, though the chief engineer later died, and inspections indicate that the vessel fuel tanks remain intact while an investigation continues.
articles.description: There are fears of a major oil spillage off Ibiza but the ship's fuel tanks are so far intact.

articles.headline: Elon Musk announces every US child will receive two SpaceX shares
articles.title: Elon Musk says every child in U.S. will get two SpaceX shares
articles.summary: SpaceX chief executive officer Elon Musk announced that every child in the United States will receive two shares of company stock, one issued by SpaceX and one matched personally by him. The initiative follows a prior contribution of Class A common stock to active Trump Accounts by the aerospace manufacturer, though specific lockup terms remain unconfirmed.
articles.description: SpaceX did ​not immediately respond ‌to a request for comment on whether Mr. Musk’s SpaceX share donations would be linked to Trump Accounts or ‌come with any kind of ​lockup period

articles.headline: UN Gaza rapporteur Francesca Albanese denied entry into Costa Rica
articles.title: UN Gaza rapporteur Francesca Albanese denied entry into Costa Rica
articles.description: Costa Rica has barred UN special rapporteur Francesca Albanese, citing unfounded ‘links to terrorist acts’.

articles.headline: Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina plans return amid escalating political tensions
articles.title: Sheikh Hasina’s return gambit tests Bangladesh’s political fault lines
articles.summary: Former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina announced plans to end over two years of exile in India and return to Bangladesh on December 16, testing political fault lines. The interim administration and Bangladesh Nationalist Party officials stated she could only return as a convicted fugitive through extradition, while her Awami League party called for nationwide lockdowns.
articles.description: The ousted leader’s December 16 return plan has energised the Awami League leaders and cadre, tested Tarique Rahman’s government and complicated Dhaka’s efforts to reset ties with New Delhi

articles.headline: Iraq federal government takes control of Kurdish oil refineries
articles.title: Is Iraq facing renewed instability?
articles.summary: The Iraqi federal government has announced control over oil refineries in the semi autonomous Kurdish region amid claims of losing millions of dollars to crude oil smugglers. Around twenty percent of the nation's oil reserves are located in this region. Thousands of local residents have protested against the move, fearing a significant loss of autonomy and potential military confrontation.
articles.description: PM asserts state control over resources in semi-autonomous Kurdish region

articles.headline: Indian Navy receives final Project 17A stealth frigate from GRSE
articles.title: Navy Project 17A programme completed as GRSE hands over final stealth frigate Vindhyagir
articles.summary: The Indian Navy accepted Vindhyagiri, the final Nilgiri-class stealth frigate, from Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers in Kolkata. This delivery concludes the Project 17A shipbuilding programme, with all seven vessels handed over in 23 months. Designed by the Navy's Warship Design Bureau, the warships feature advanced weapon systems, 75 percent indigenous content, and support numerous micro, small and medium enterprises.
articles.description: Vindhyagiri (Yard 3024) is the third and final Project 17A frigate built by GRSE

articles.headline: South African court overturns 2022 impeachment report against President Cyril Ramaphosa
articles.title: Cyril Ramaphosa wins court bid to overturn impeachment report
articles.summary: A South African high court ruled in favour of President Cyril Ramaphosa, setting aside a 2022 parliamentary panel report that alleged misconduct regarding a 2020 farmhouse theft. The court found the panel exceeded its remit and made legal errors. The ruling removes findings that previously threatened his political career and prompted ongoing legal battles.
articles.description: The 74-year-old leader was accused of hiding from police and tax authorities a 2020 break-in and theft of $580,000, which was stashed in furniture at his luxury Phala Phala farmhouse in the northern Limpopo province

articles.headline: DR Congo Ebola cases surpass 12,000 amid escalating eastern conflict
articles.title: DR Congo Ebola cases surpass 12,000 as fighting disrupts response in east
articles.summary: Confirmed Ebola infections in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceeded 12,000, driven by conflict, delayed detection, and strained health services across eight provinces. According to government data and humanitarian workers, intensifying fighting in Ituri province between the Congolese army and the Convention for the Popular Revolution forced emergency evacuations and disrupted containment operations, heightening risks for millions.
articles.description: Authorities struggle to contain country's worst Ebola outbreak, as fighting in east displaces health workers, civilians.

articles.headline: India and China hold high-level talks on border management
articles.title: India, China hold high-level talks in Arunachal sector on border management, LAC issues: MEA
articles.summary: The Indian and Chinese armies conducted high-level discussions this month in the Arunachal Pradesh sector to address border management and Line of Actual Control issues, the Ministry of External Affairs stated on November 25, 2026. Led by Lt. Gen Girish Kalia for India, the talks aim to maintain peace following previous regional tensions.
articles.description: MEA spokesperson Randhir also addressed a report claiming China-sourced satellite data may have aided Pakistan in tracking Indian troop movements and monitoring installations during Operation Sindoor

articles.headline: Civil rights groups claim police involvement in voter verification is illegal
articles.title: Civil rights group claim that involvement of police in SIR exercise illegal
articles.summary: Civil rights groups and political leaders in West Bengal claimed on November 27, 2026, that police involvement in the State's deleted voter verification process is illegal. Letters were sent to Chief Minister Suvendu Adhkari and the Election Commission of India urging the withdrawal of police forces. Former Chief Electoral Officer Jawhar Sircar stated the police have no right to participate.
articles.description: Congress leader, Mamata-Trinamool MP writes to poll body seeking validity of police usage in voter verification

articles.headline: Karnataka government issues show cause notice to IOCL terminal over measurements
articles.title: Karnataka government serves show-cause notice to IOCL terminal in Bengaluru over ethanol measurement discrepancies
articles.summary: The Karnataka government issued a show cause notice on November 27, 2026, to Indian Oil Corporation Limited at its Bengaluru terminal following inspections by the Department of Legal Metrology. Officials found significant measurement discrepancies in ethanol and motor gasoline dispensed through mass flow meters. The oil marketing company has been directed to submit an explanation within seven days.
articles.description: The action follows inspections initiated by the Department of Legal Metrology, Karnataka, at the terminals of oil marketing companies, taking the checks of fuel samples for ethanol blend one step further

articles.headline: Civil society groups urge Karnataka chief minister to scrutinise electoral deletions
articles.title: Civil society groups urge Karnataka Chief Minister to scrutinise SIR deletions ahead of local polls
articles.summary: Members of various civil society groups under the Anti-SIR alliance submitted a memorandum on November 27, 2026, to Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar. The alliance demanded the rejection of the final electoral roll published after the Special Intensive Revision due to numerous errors. They urged the restoration of the 2025 electoral roll ahead of upcoming local body elections.
articles.description: The alliance said the final electoral roll was riddled with errors and demanded that the 2025 electoral roll be restored, subjected to public scrutiny and revised in a voter-friendly manner before being used for local body elections.

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu chief minister reviews rainfall deficit and directs relief measures
articles.title: Vijay reviews rainfall situation in T.N., directs steps to ensure drinking water, fodder supply
articles.summary: Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay held a review meeting in Chennai on November 27, 2026, addressing the impact of rainfall deficit and preparedness for the summer. Officials reported a twenty percent decrease in normal rainfall. Vijay ordered immediate crop damage surveys, compensation for farmers, and allocated thirteen point twenty six crore rupees from the State Disaster Relief Fund for fodder.

articles.headline: Low postdoc funding drives Indian scientific brain drain overseas
articles.title: Low funding for postdoc roles fuelling brain drain, govt. funds only 2,500 positions
articles.summary: Indian-origin scientists are driving technological advancements at institutions such as MIT, Stanford, and Caltech due to systemic limitations in India's domestic research ecosystem. Young researchers in India face severe administrative hurdles, delayed scholarships, and rigid funding deadlines that contrast sharply with the multi-year grants and flexible environments available in the United States, according to an analysis published on September 11, 2026.
articles.description: India spends about $13 a year per person on research; China spends $250, the U.S. over $2,100. There are just 262 full-time-equivalent researchers per million people in the country

articles.headline: CRPF deployed to secure Madurai temple and hill area
articles.title: CRPF arrives in Madurai to secure Thirupparankundram area
articles.summary: Central Reserve Police Force personnel arrived in Madurai on Friday night to secure the Sri Subramania Swamy Temple and surrounding hill. The deployment followed a Supreme Court order issued by Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi to ensure the Karthigai deepam ritual proceeds safely on November 28, 2026, while suspending the temple board and appointing receivers.

articles.headline: Coimbatore court convicts two men for minor's murder
articles.title: Coimbatore court convicts two accused in Sulur sexual assault and murder case
articles.summary: A special POCSO court in Coimbatore convicted K. Karthi and R. Mohan on Friday for the sexual assault and murder of a ten-year-old girl in Sulur in May. Judge K. Hariharan posted the hearing on the sentence to December 4, 2026, awaiting a Probation Officer report following a trial involving sixty-eight witnesses.

articles.headline: War and drought severely threaten agricultural livelihoods across Sudan
articles.title: War and drought threaten livelihoods of Sudan’s farmers
articles.summary: Decades-old farming communities in Sudan face unprecedented harvest failures due to a crippling water crisis driven by below-average rainfall and war-induced infrastructure destruction. Organizations like the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization and the International Committee of the Red Cross reported that electricity shortages, fuel scarcity, and damaged power stations have severely disrupted irrigation systems and threatened millions.
articles.description: Attacks on electricity infrastructure and drought are threatening Sudan's harvests and leaving millions without water.

articles.headline: Mother of slain Bihar youth begins fast unto death
articles.title: Killed Bihar youth’s mother sits on fast-unto-death protest, MP Pappu Yadav meets her, demands CBI probe
articles.summary: Asha Devi, mother of a youth killed in an alleged police encounter in Bihar, began a fast unto death on November 27, 2026, protesting unmet government promises. Independent Member of Parliament Rajesh Ranjan visited the village to support the grieving family and demanded a Central Bureau of Investigation probe into the incident.
articles.description: ‘The government had assured us of a government job to a family member, financial help and arrest of those found guilty in the case but even after five months of the incident, no one takes care of us,’ said Asha Devi

articles.headline: Sunny Joseph meets Mallikarjun Kharge amid factional feuds in Keralam
articles.title: Sunny Joseph meets Kharge as factional feud continues to convulse Congress in Keralam
articles.summary: Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee president Sunny Joseph met All India Congress Committee president Mallikarjun Kharge in New Delhi on Friday to discuss ongoing organisational affairs. Amid factional feuding within the party in Keralam, the discussions focused on addressing an organisational void and planning leadership restructuring. Mr. Joseph also announced plans to meet Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi.
articles.description: KPCC president says his meeting with the AICC president has set the ball rolling on organisational restructuring in the State. Sunny Joseph likely to seek AICC approval for an extended KPCC meeting to discuss organisational issues

articles.headline: Former ISRO chief stresses environmental safety in technological advancement
articles.title: Former ISRO chief stresses environmental safety in technological advancement
articles.summary: Former Indian Space Research Organisation Chairman A.S. Kiran Kumar emphasized the importance of environmental safety during the Earth 2026 convention in Mysuru. He noted that scientific innovations must support sustainable development and highlighted India's achievements in space research. The four-day event runs at the JSS College of Pharmacy, bringing together researchers to discuss environmental health and toxicology.
articles.description: International toxicology convention in Mysuru brings scientists and researchers together to discuss emerging health and environmental risks

articles.headline: Supreme Court quashes premature release of former MP Anand Mohan in murder case
articles.title: Supreme Court quashes premature release of former MP Anand Mohan in murder case
articles.summary: The Supreme Court quashed the premature release of former MP Anand Mohan, who was serving a life sentence for the 1994 murder of district magistrate G. Krishnaiah. Setting aside the Bihar government remission policy, the Bench directed Mohan to surrender within one month and mandated that the victim's wife be heard in future remission attempts.
articles.description: The apex court says Article 21 is not a “one-sided guarantee, equally encompasses victims, society at large

articles.headline: India records record 378 million tonnes of foodgrain production for 2025-26
articles.title: India produced record 378.53 million tonnes of foodgrains in 2025-26: Agriculture Minister
articles.summary: Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan released final crop estimates showing India produced a record 378.53 million tonnes of foodgrains in 2025-26, exceeding the previous year by 20.8 million tonnes. Rice production reached 155.15 million tonnes, maintaining India's position as the largest global producer ahead of China, while wheat output stood at 122.06 million tonnes.
articles.description: Shivraj Singh Chouhan also released the first advance estimates for the 2026–27 crop year, stating that output is expected to remain on track for the upcoming season despite El Niño and inadequate rainfall

articles.headline: Fuel tanker crash on Cairo Ring Road causes deadly fire
articles.title: Fuel tanker crash ignites massive fire on highway surrounding Cairo, killing at least 31 people
articles.summary: At least thirty people died and twenty-five others sustained injuries when a fuel tanker crash ignited a massive blaze on the Ring Road encircling Cairo on Wednesday, November 25, 2026. The Egyptian Health Ministry reported that the incident occurred in the densely populated Waraq area of Giza, charring numerous vehicles and prompting an ongoing investigation by the Public Prosecutor's office.
articles.description: The blaze on Ring Road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 25 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, the Public Prosecutor’s office said in a statement

articles.headline: India defeats Malaysia to reach Women's Asian Champions Trophy final
articles.title: WACT: India outclasses Malaysia, storms into the final; meets China
articles.summary: India defeated Malaysia 6-2 at the International Sports Complex to advance to the Women's Asian Champions Trophy final. Deepika scored twice from penalty corners, while Mumtaz Khan, Navneet Kaur, Sunelita Toppo, and Ishika also contributed goals for the victorious team. India will face China in the final match after China defeated Japan 1-0 in the other semifinal encounter.

articles.headline: CBI secures extradition of Chhattisgarh liquor scam suspect from UAE
articles.title: Chhattisgarh liquor scam syndicate ‘moneyman’ extradited from UAE, says CBI
articles.summary: The Central Bureau of Investigation announced the deportation of Vikas Agrawal from the United Arab Emirates for his alleged role in a Chhattisgarh liquor syndicate. Investigators allege Agrawal served as the central financial coordinator for a scam that caused a state loss exceeding 1280 crore rupees between 2019 and 2022. Authorities located Agrawal through an Interpol Red Notice before returning him to Mumbai.
articles.description: The liquor ‘scam’ in the State, according to the ED, was orchestrated between 2019 and 2022 when Chhattisgarh was governed by the Bhupesh Baghel-led Congress dispensation

articles.headline: Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy warns of severe water crisis
articles.title: Govt. committed to protecting environment and safeguarding resources for future generations: Revanth Reddy
articles.summary: Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy stated on Friday that the State faces a serious water crisis due to El Nino-induced drought, with potential rainfall shortages lasting eight months. Speaking at a Climate Change Conclave curtain-raiser, Reddy urged collective action, suggesting farmers forego a crop if needed. He also highlighted government environmental initiatives, including electric vehicle adoption, Musi River rejuvenation, and strict anti-drug efforts.
articles.description: Chief Minister says State facing a serious situation, with projections indicating that there might be no rainfall for the next eight months; calls for a collective effort to tackle climate change and challenges posed by the El Niño phenomenon

articles.headline: India and the Netherlands upgrade bilateral ties to strategic partnership
articles.title: India, Netherlands upgrade ties; sign 17 MoUs on water, renewable energy, and semiconductors
articles.summary: During Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit on May 16 and 17, 2026, India and the Netherlands elevated their relations to a Strategic Partnership. Both nations signed 17 agreements covering water, agriculture, health, renewable energy, and critical minerals. According to Dutch media, Prime Minister Rob Jetten also raised sensitive topics including press freedoms, which the Ministry of External Affairs rejected.
articles.description: MEA pushes back on Dutch concerns over press freedom and minority rights in India. Agreements signed include a semiconductor fabrication project between TATA Electronics and Dutch company ASML

articles.headline: Gaza Ministry of Health declares epidemic alert following sharp surge in meningitis cases
articles.title: Gaza meningitis cases surge as collapsing infrastructure fuels health fears
articles.summary: The Gaza Ministry of Health declared an epidemic alert after reporting 272 meningitis cases in October, driven by collapsing infrastructure, severe overcrowding in displacement camps, and poor sanitation. Paediatricians at Rantisi Children Hospital noted a high volume of admissions for bacterial and viral infections, while international organizations reported critical shortages of laboratory supplies and medicines.
articles.description: Meningitis is raising alarm in Gaza, where overcrowding, damaged sanitation are putting children at risk.

articles.headline: US technology companies provide key infrastructure for Israeli military operations
articles.title: How Silicon Valley became central to Israel’s war on Palestinians
articles.summary: Major United States technology corporations including Amazon, Microsoft, Google, and Palantir supply advanced cloud computing, artificial intelligence, and facial recognition infrastructure to support Israeli military operations in Gaza and the West Bank. According to rights groups, leaked documents and UN reports, this technology facilitates intelligence gathering, communications interception, and automated targeting systems, leading to deep integration between US firms and former members of Israel's military cyberwarfare units.
articles.description: From surveillance systems to AI targeting, US tech giants are deeply embedded in Israel's war machine.

articles.headline: International Criminal Court judges face US sanctions over war crimes investigations
articles.title: ICC judge Kimberly Prost tries war crimes. She’s a target of US sanctions
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump's administration has imposed financial penalties, asset freezes, and visa restrictions on International Criminal Court judges, including Canadian jurist Kimberly Prost, and other officials. These sanctions stem from court investigations into alleged war crimes committed by US personnel and Israeli leadership in Gaza. The measures have disrupted the daily lives of judges, complicated international banking transactions, and threatened the operational capacity of the judicial institution.
articles.description: Apps not working. Bank transfers not going through. And a court fighting for international law must skirt US firms.

articles.headline: Supreme Court declines to mandate unified portal for unclaimed deposits
articles.title: Supreme Court refuses to mandate unified portal for tracing unclaimed deposits; cites regulatory reforms
articles.summary: The Supreme Court declined a plea seeking a unified portal for tracing unclaimed bank deposits and investments, citing existing sector-specific reforms. Justices Vikram Nath and R. Mahadevan disposed of the PIL filed by journalist Sucheta Dalal, noting that mechanisms like the UDGAM portal and recent legislative changes have addressed primary concerns. Authorities reported returning approximately 6,453 crore rupees in unclaimed assets through nationwide campaigns.
articles.description: Sucheta Dalal’s petition highlighted the accumulation of unclaimed deposits and investments with financial institutions and the procedural difficulties faced by nominees and legal heirs in recovering them

articles.headline: Imprisoned Iranian women face death sentences following anti-government protests
articles.title: Desperate appeals from women on death row in Iran after protests
articles.summary: Iranian twin sisters Taraneh and Romina Rahimi are among several women facing execution or lengthy prison terms following anti-government protests in January 2026. According to relatives and human rights groups, the defendants endured severe physical abuse and forced confessions during interrogation. The Iranian embassy in London categorically rejected allegations of torture and stated that legal penalties were issued for violent offenses.
articles.description: Female protesters and dissidents are being sentenced to death in numbers not seen for decades, a rights group says.

articles.headline: Mexico files formal complaint against US over DEA tip line
articles.title: Mexico files complaint with US over DEA tip line on alleged drug dealers
articles.summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum announced that Mexico filed a formal complaint with the United States regarding a Drug Enforcement Administration tip line targeting suspected drug traffickers and officials. Foreign Minister Juan Ramon de la Fuente contacted the US ambassador in Mexico City. The dispute highlights bilateral tensions over sovereignty and security cooperation, following recent US pressure concerning cartel links among Mexican politicians.
articles.description: Tensions rise over DEA tip line, with Mexico emphasising respect for its sovereignty amidst growing bilateral discord.

articles.headline: Spanish rescuers treat migrants as hundreds arrive in Canary Islands
articles.title: Spanish rescuers treat migrants as hundreds arrive in Canary Islands
articles.description: Spain's Military Emergencies Unit has been sent to treat migrants brought ashore on the island of El Hierro

articles.headline: Mauricio Pochettino becomes eighth regular head coach of Manchester United
articles.title: Can Pochettino resuscitate a dysfunctional Manchester United?
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino has been appointed as the new head coach of Manchester United, becoming the eighth regular manager since Alex Ferguson departed in May 2013. Following the dismissal of Michael Carrick, the Argentine manager takes charge of a struggling squad with the objective of restoring domestic and continental success. Pochettino stated in his inaugural press conference that the historic club must return to its former competitive status.
articles.description: The 54-year-old will have to master significant challenges on and off the pitch to deliver the glory the Red Devils were once accustomed to. But his career trajectory as head coach offers hope

articles.headline: Origins and evolution of body mass index as obesity measure
articles.title: How waistlines, organ function tell a better story of obesity than BMI does
articles.summary: The body mass index originated in 1832 when Belgian astronomer Adolphe Quetelet sought to understand human populations using height and weight measurements. Originally known as the Quetelet Index, the ratio was renamed in 1972 by United States physiologist Ancel Keys after determining it best represented body fat, though it cannot distinguish between muscle mass and excess fat.
articles.description: In 2025, The Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology established a commission of 58 experts from different countries to set obesity-related guidelines. A new study in Nature has tested whether the commission’s recommendations can actually distinguish between people at different levels of risk, with data from 8.4 lakh adults

articles.headline: Gukesh draws against Sindarov in the World Chess Championship
articles.title: World Chess Championships: Gukesh serves a timely reminder with his class & resilience
articles.summary: Grandmaster D. Gukesh demonstrated notable class and resilience during the third game of the World Chess Championship against Javokhir Sindarov in Cologny. Playing with black pieces, Gukesh managed the clock effectively throughout the sixty-move match, forcing a fighting draw that highlighted his extensive preparation and classical chess proficiency.
articles.description: The Grandmaster from Chennai and his team of coach and ‘seconds’ should be particularly happy about the third game where with black pieces he blitzed his moves away and surprised Sindarov

articles.headline: Spain Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez expresses confidence ahead of snap election
articles.title: Spain’s Pedro Sanchez bets on left-wing voting surge to defy election polls
articles.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez expressed confidence on Friday that he will secure a left-wing majority in the upcoming general election despite adverse polling data suggesting a right-wing advantage. Speaking to radio station SER, Sanchez emphasized that internal data points to a win for his Socialist Party through mobilised voters. Parties concluded campaigning ahead of Saturday's mandatory day of reflection before Sunday's crucial vote.
articles.description: Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez makes last bid to beat right-wing parties before Spanish vote on Sunday.

articles.headline: SIMA urges five-year import duty exemption to counter cotton shortfall
articles.title: Cotton output shortfall: SIMA seeks five-year import duty waiver
articles.summary: The Southern India Mills’ Association has requested a five-year import duty waiver on cotton to address an expanding deficit between local production and consumption. Cotton production for the current season starting October 1 is projected at 248.66 lakh bales, falling short of the textile industry requirement of 350 to 360 lakh bales. According to former Cotton Association of India president Atul Ganatra, imports could reach nearly 90 lakh bales.

articles.headline: Nepal initiates process to declare 213 missing Indian nationals presumed dead
articles.title: Nepal flash floods: Kathmandu begins process to declare 213 missing Indians presumed dead
articles.summary: The government of Nepal has started the official procedure to declare 213 Indian nationals missing since the August 26 flash floods presumed dead. According to the Indian Embassy in Nepal, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority published the list on November 25, 2026, inviting public objections until December 2 before finalising death certificates. The devastating floods in the Trishuli-Bhote Koshi river system killed at least 1,453 people.
articles.description: Inviting objections or concerns, the Embassy said concerned family members could contact it via eoikathmandufloodsupport@gmail.com or +9779851316807

articles.headline: Karnataka plans super speciality and cancer hospitals in every district
articles.title: Super speciality, cancer hospitals in each district soon: Minister
articles.summary: Karnataka Minister for Medical Education and Skill Development Sharan Prakash Patil stated that the State government plans to establish a super speciality hospital, cancer hospital, and trauma centre in every district. Speaking in Mysuru on Friday, the Minister noted that 12 super-speciality hospitals are already established and announced that cancer facilities in Mysuru, Mandya, and Tumakuru will open within three months.

articles.headline: Doctors call for Hyderabad health database amid high air pollution
articles.title: Hyderabad’s air pollution puts focus on hospitals; doctors call for city-level health database
articles.summary: Medical professionals and public health experts in Hyderabad urged hospitals to collaborate on a city-level health database to track pollution impacts beyond respiratory illnesses. Speaking at Cyberabad Moves on Friday, doctors noted that daily exposure to poor air quality, which recently exceeded an Air Quality Index of 300, contributes to cardiovascular problems, strokes, and heightened risks for commuting children.
articles.description: Hospitals want to share anonymised data on respiratory illnesses, strokes and cardiovascular conditions, while doctors propose using daily AQI readings to alert vulnerable patients

articles.headline: Sooranad school principal transferred following student suicide in Kollam
articles.title: Plus Two student’s death in Kollam: school Principal transferred to Kozhikode
articles.summary: The principal of Sooranad Government Higher Secondary School was transferred to Kozhikode district on Friday following the suicide of Plus Two student Niranjan. Relatives and classmates alleged that school authorities humiliated the student and his parents after a school excursion. The tragedy sparked protests outside the school before authorities intervened with assurances of a fair investigation.
articles.description: Move follows widespread allegations from students and relatives regarding the Principal’s misconduct toward the deceased student

articles.headline: Rohit Sharma returns as Mumbai Indians captain for the 2027 Indian Premier League season
articles.title: IPL 2027: Rohit Sharma back in the saddle for Mumbai Indians
articles.summary: Veteran batsman Rohit Sharma will reclaim the captaincy of the franchise ahead of the 2027 tournament following a three-year hiatus. Sharma replaces Hardik Pandya, who transferred to the Punjab Kings in a deal involving Arshdeep Singh. Having led Mumbai to five previous titles, Sharma returns to leadership after the team struggled under subsequent management during recent seasons.
articles.description: The Hindu understands that Jasprit Bumrah, Suryakumar Yadav and Tilak Varma were also in contention for the captaincy. The franchise, however, opted for the man whose leadership brought it its five championships

articles.headline: President Droupadi Murmu says Keralam can become an international Panchakarma centre
articles.title: Keralam can become an international centre for Panchakarma treatment, says President
articles.summary: President Droupadi Murmu stated on November 27, 2026, during the Golden Jubilee of Vaidyaratnam Ayurveda College in Thrissur, that Keralam can become an international hub for Panchakarma treatment. She emphasized documenting Ashtavaidya texts as a national priority and suggested joint research with the Ministry of Ayush and WHO. State officials, including Governor Om Prakash Mathur, attended the event.
articles.description: President Droupadi Murmu addresses valedictory of Golden Jubilee of Vaidyaratnam Ayurveda College

articles.headline: Belagavi Police register financial fraud case against six individuals over ponzi scheme
articles.title: Police book six in Belagavi for collecting ₹133 crore promising high returns
articles.summary: The Belagavi Police registered a fraud case against six people from Nippani, including Nanda Patil and her son Prasad Patil, for allegedly running a ponzi scheme through Nanda Traders and Lunars Education and Training Solutions. The firms collected over 133 crore rupees from individuals in Karnataka and Maharashtra by promising high returns. Authorities stated the funds were used to purchase properties.
articles.description: A large number of people, most of them from Nasik in Maharashtra, have deposited money with two Nippani firms for 36% returns

articles.headline: Elon Musk gets the greenlight from the US to launch one million satellites
articles.title: Elon Musk gets the greenlight from the US to launch one million satellites
articles.description: Elon Musk wants to move AI data centres into space, where near-constant sunlight could help power them.

articles.headline: Telangana Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka seeks viability gap funding for power projects
articles.title: Telangana seeks VGF for setting up pumped storage power projects by Genco
articles.summary: Telangana Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka requested viability gap funding from the Centre for pumped storage power projects during a conference in New Delhi on November 27, 2026. He asked for speedy approval of pending project reports and raised concerns about fluctuating inter-State transmission charges that negatively impact the State's financial planning.
articles.description: Deputy CM Bhatti Vikramarka urges Union Minister of Power at State Power Ministers’ conference to extent inter-state transmission charges waiver till March 2030 for renewable energy

articles.headline: J&K leaders condemn police summons issued to Maulana Rehmatullah Qasimi
articles.title: J&K leaders condemn police action against Maulana Rehmatullah over Vande Mataram issue; Mirwaiz alleges house arrest
articles.summary: Kashmir chief cleric Mirwaiz Umar Farooq and Peoples Democratic Party president Mehbooba Mufti condemned the police for summoning prominent cleric Maulana Rehmatullah Qasimi on November 27, 2026, after he opposed the playing of Vande Mataram at a Waqf event. The Mirwaiz also claimed he was placed under house arrest and prevented from delivering a Friday sermon at Jamia Masjid in Srinagar.
articles.description: It was shameful that a scholar of Moulana Sahab’s stature and age was being subjected to such treatment simply because he dared to question and condemn the playing of Vande Mataram at a Waqf event, says Mehbooba Mufti

articles.headline: Formula One drivers face intense challenges during championship-winning campaigns
articles.title: Rearview: holding a mirror to Norris’ title defence
articles.summary: Elite athletes frequently unlock their full potential after securing a significant breakthrough victory or a career-defining title. In Formula One, capturing a championship requires enduring a grueling year-long campaign filled with competitive ups and downs. Max Verstappen demonstrated this resilience during his 2021 battle with Lewis Hamilton before ultimately establishing his dominance on the racing grid.
articles.description: How has the McLaren driver fared after winning the 2025 F1 World championship? Does he emerge from the 2026 season with his reputation diminished or enhanced?

articles.headline: Syria debates citizenship rights for children of foreign fighters
articles.title: Syria debates citizenship rights for children of foreign fighters
articles.description: Syria may amend its nationality law to grant citizenship to children of Syrian mothers and foreign fighters.

articles.headline: Severe Thanksgiving storms leave roads flooded and trees fallen
articles.title: Severe Thanksgiving storms leave roads flooded and trees fallen
articles.description: Hundreds of thousands of people were without power after severe weather hit both coasts of the United States during the Thanksgiving holiday.

articles.headline: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra urges MSMEs to accelerate artificial intelligence adoption
articles.title: RBI Governor pegs AI’s potential economic value to MSMEs at $685 billion, urges faster adoption
articles.summary: Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra stated on Friday at the SME Finance and Investment Summit in Mumbai that artificial intelligence adoption could generate between $490 billion and $685 billion in economic value for Indian micro, small and medium enterprises. He urged small businesses to accelerate technology integration to overcome productivity challenges, noting that only about 15% of small enterprises currently utilize the technology.
articles.description: “This is entirely doable,” the Governor said, encouraging enterprises to begin with practical applications such as digital accounting, inventory management, quality control and customer engagement before expanding their use of AI.

articles.headline: Tripura begins voting for sixteen urban local bodies under tight security
articles.title: Urban local body elections in Tripura held amid sporadic incidents; rigging alleged
articles.summary: Polling for sixteen urban local bodies in Tripura began at seven in the morning on November 27, 2026, under tight security. State Election Commission Secretary Anurag Sen reported that voting has been peaceful, with over ten thousand security personnel deployed to manage the election across Agartala Municipal Corporation and other regions.
articles.description: Altogether, 5.56 lakh voters are eligible to exercise their franchise to decide the fate of 733 candidates contesting 268 seats across the 16 civic bodies

articles.headline: Brazil denounces proposed United States tariffs on aircraft and sugar
articles.title: Brazil blasts ‘unacceptable’ new US tariff proposals
articles.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's administration has condemned unilateral tariff proposals announced by the United States trade representative targeting Brazilian manufactured aircraft and sugar imports. Brazil stated it is weighing reciprocal measures while remaining open to negotiated solutions through bilateral talks. The proposed duties, which could take effect in January, form part of a broader package impacting multiple trading partners following disputes over trade practices.
articles.description: President Lula’s office says Brazil will not yield to threats and aims for a negotiated resolution.

articles.headline: Pinarayi Vijayan accuses Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan of trivialising phone-tapping allegations
articles.title: Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan accuses Keralam CM of trivialising issues of illegal phone tapping
articles.summary: Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan criticized Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on November 27, 2026, for trivializing claims of illegal phone tapping and surveillance. Mr. Vijayan demanded a comprehensive investigation after the Chief Minister stated at a Constitution Day function that his phone was being monitored and that he deliberately fed false information during calls.
articles.description: Even while making serious allegations that the phones of Opposition leaders and even members of his own Cabinet are being tapped, the Chief Minister is attempting to trivialise the issue instead of announcing a serious inquiry, says Pinarayi

articles.headline: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un inspects nuclear facilities and urges expansion
articles.title: North Korea's Kim vows to build more nuclear weapons after ignoring Trump's overture
articles.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un inspected nuclear materials production facilities and called for the accelerated manufacturing of more nuclear weapons. Reported on November 26, 2026, by the Korean Central News Agency, the visit follows Kim ignoring recent diplomatic overtures from United States President Donald Trump. Kim stated that bolstering the nuclear arsenal is necessary to counter escalating security threats from the United States and South Korea.
articles.description: North Korea didn't say where the nuclear materials production factories that Kim Jong Un visited this week are located; U.S President Trump reiterated his eagerness to restore diplomacy with Mr. Kim as he visited China last week for the APEC summit

articles.headline: Eisenkot accuses Netanyahu's Likud party of stalling coalition talks
articles.title: Israel’s Eisenkot accuses Netanyahu’s party of stalling coalition talks
articles.summary: Gadi Eisenkot has accused the Likud party of caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of deliberately stalling coalition negotiations to trigger new elections. President-appointed Eisenkot faces a December deadline to form a government, but his centrist Yashar party holds only 36 seats, falling significantly short of the necessary majority in parliament.
articles.description: Yashar party chief says Likud wants to drag Israel into another election under the outgoing government.

articles.headline: Norse Atlantic files for bankruptcy and halts all ticket sales
articles.title: Norse Atlantic files for bankruptcy, halts flights and ticket sales
articles.summary: Norwegian budget airline Norse Atlantic has filed for bankruptcy for its main operating unit and suspended all flights following a critical financial crisis. Chief Executive Officer Eivind Roald stated that skyrocketing jet fuel prices, driven by the war in Iran, made operations unsustainable. Customers have been advised to seek refunds through bankruptcy proceedings.
articles.description: Passengers advised to seek refunds via bankruptcy process, though guarantees are not assured, warns Norse Atlantic.

articles.headline: Indian states project massive spending on unconditional cash transfer schemes
articles.title: The fiscal cost of cash-transfer schemes
articles.summary: Twelve Indian states expect to spend nearly 1.68 trillion rupees on unconditional cash transfers for women during 2025 and 2026, representing about 0.5 percent of the national gross domestic product. Critics argue that such social policies lack crucial ex ante appraisals, potentially worsening fiscal deficits and creating trade-offs with essential public investments like education.
articles.description: A social policy is often based on expected electoral gain, and is implemented without any ex ante appraisal; since cash transfers and subsidies are perpetual in nature and politically hard to reverse, such continuous commitment of financial resources demands prior evaluation and real-time monitoring to address potential shortcomings

articles.headline: Trump endorses Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Azidi's oil crackdown
articles.title: Trump backs Iraqi PM’s oil smuggling crackdown
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump has expressed full support for Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Azidi's recent efforts to combat oil smuggling, curb corruption, and assert federal control over state weapons. The campaign has sparked direct confrontation with Kurdish authorities and Iran-aligned militias, raising significant regional tensions regarding constitutional and territorial rights in Iraq.
articles.description: Baghdad closes border crossings as Kurdish authorities warn of constitutional violations and call for meeting.

articles.headline: United States prepares to announce tariffs on global trading partners
articles.title: US announces new tariffs on host of countries including India
articles.summary: The United States is preparing to introduce new import taxes affecting at least fourteen jurisdictions, including China, the European Union, and Japan.
