The upcoming announcement follows a Section 301 investigation launched after the Supreme Court invalidated previous trade measures implemented by President Donald Trump. While the administration argues the tariffs will protect American manufacturing, critics contend the policy risks increasing consumer prices and escalating international trade tensions.
articles.description: The new levies would hit many of America's trading partners, including India.

articles.headline: Jerusalem Daily: Kushner calls Gaza rebuilding ‘act of kindness’
articles.title: Jerusalem Daily: Kushner calls Gaza rebuilding ‘act of kindness’
articles.description: As Gaza remains under Israeli bombardment, US envoy Jared Kushner calls its reconstruction a ‘huge act of kindness'.

articles.headline: Supreme Court issues notice to Delhi Police on bail pleas by activists
articles.title: Supreme Court issues notice on bail pleas by Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam in 2020 Delhi riots case
articles.summary: The Supreme Court issued notice on November 25, 2026, regarding interim bail petitions filed by activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam related to the 2020 Delhi riots. Both individuals have spent over six years in custody under the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act while awaiting trial for the violence that erupted during protests against the Citizenship Amendment Act.
articles.description: The court declined to take up their pleas for interim relief; CJI to set up three-judge Bench to decide whether prolonged incarceration and delay in trial can override stringent bail curbs under UAPA

articles.headline: Brazil criticizes French President Emmanuel Macron over meat comments
articles.title: Brazil pushes back on Macron calling its meat 'doped'
articles.summary: The Brazilian government expressed regret over remarks by French President Emmanuel Macron, who recently described Brazilian meat as doped during a meeting with farming unions. Brazil defended its rigorous sanitary control systems and condemned the European Union restrictions, noting that agricultural exports to European markets totaled $1.84bn in 2025.
articles.description: France's president made the comment while speaking to French farming representatives, months after the EU banned Brazil beef and poultry products.

articles.headline: Environmental authority reports elevated fine dust levels across parts of Sri Lanka
articles.title: Is stubble burning in Punjab affecting Sri Lanka’s air quality?
articles.summary: Sri Lanka Central Environmental Authority recorded raised levels of fine dust particles across the Northern Province and multiple districts including Anuradhapura and Colombo. Officials attributed the poor air quality primarily to regional winds blowing from outside the island. This phenomenon coincides with seasonal agricultural residue burning by farmers in Punjab and Haryana to clear their fields for upcoming wheat crops.
articles.description: Pollution from northern India and the wider region travels over the Bay of Bengal to Sri Lanka during the northeast monsoon, and crop burning is part of that mix

articles.headline: Student-backed movement in Serbia nominates Radomir Saicic for presidency
articles.title: Serbia’s student-led movement nominates chemistry professor for presidency
articles.summary: Serbia’s student-backed political movement has selected Belgrade University chemistry professor Radomir Saicic as its presidential candidate for the upcoming December 27 polls. Saicic, who is 65 years old and a member of the Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts, aims to prioritize the rule of law and combat corruption. The election follows a parliamentary ballot victory by the Student List after Aleksandar Vucic ended his presidential term.
articles.description: Radomir Saicic, who teaches at Belgrade University, was among the first university professors to join the movement.

articles.headline: Supreme Court sets aside High Court order for inquiry into Rahul Gandhi
articles.title: SC sets aside Allahabad HC order on CBI, ED enquiries into disproportionate assets complaint against Rahul Gandhi
articles.summary: The Supreme Court set aside Allahabad High Court orders directing the Central Bureau of Investigation and the Enforcement Directorate to probe a disproportionate assets complaint against Lok Sabha Opposition Leader Rahul Gandhi. A three-judge bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant ruled that Gandhi must be impleaded as a party and heard from the threshold, criticizing the previous in-chamber proceedings.
articles.description: Three-judge bench led by CJI India Surya Kant directs the Opposition leader be impleaded as a party, while relegating the case back to the High Court to be heard from the very threshold in open court by a fresh Bench of judges

articles.headline: Supreme Court clarifies students opting for three languages may continue
articles.title: Students who opted for three languages can continue with them, says Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Supreme Court observed on November 25, 2026, that students currently opting for three languages may continue their choice without mandatory switching. The remarks responded to a Central Board of Secondary Education plea modifying evaluation rules. While Classes 7 through 9 have transitional relaxations, authorities debate implementation schedules and student incentives for learning additional languages.
articles.description: Class 7 students, along with Classes 8 and 9, had been granted a transitional relaxation from the CBSE Board exam in the third language when they reached Class 10

articles.headline: MeitY plans national computing capacity expansion for AI inference
articles.title: MeitY plans to expand national computing capacity for AI inference
articles.summary: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology in India is expanding domestic computing infrastructure to meet rising demands for artificial intelligence inference. Secretary S. Krishnan stated that initial support focused on model training, while broader inference needs now require dedicated facilities like those developing in Pune and Bengaluru. The government will prioritize internal needs and research institutions before potentially offering surplus capacity to innovators.
articles.description: The proposed expansion would meet the government’s own computing needs, as well as those of research institutions, academic institutions and innovators

articles.headline: Funeral prayers held for 31 victims of Egypt tanker crash
articles.title: Funeral prayers held for 31 victims of Egypt tanker crash
articles.description: Funeral prayers were held at Cairo’s Al-Azhar Mosque on Friday for 31 people killed when a car collided with a tanker

articles.headline: PMI chief says governments must regulate artificial intelligence proactively
articles.title: AI regulation must precede job losses and economic disruption, says PMI chief
articles.summary: Governments in the United States, Europe, and India are lagging behind artificial intelligence adoption by waiting for economic disruption before establishing regulations, according to Project Management Institute President Johannes Heinlein. Speaking in an interview, Heinlein emphasized that a coordinated coalition of government, industry, and academia is vital to manage workforce transitions and prevent strategic corporate errors during rapid technological advancements.
articles.description: A coordinated coalition of government, industry, and academia is critical to managing the transition. Hope India will act as a leading indicator rather than waiting for job losses and stalled investments to force policy action, says PMI President, Johannes Heinlein

articles.headline: D. Gukesh and Javokhir Sindarov draw second World Chess Championship game
articles.title: World Chess Championship: Gukesh, Sindarov sign peace treaty in quick time
articles.summary: Grandmasters D. Gukesh and Javokhir Sindarov agreed to a draw in the second game of the World Chess Championship in Geneva on Wednesday. Utilizing the London System opening, the twenty-year-old competitors reached a threefold repetition after thirty moves. The result leaves the youngest World title match in history tied at one point each after two rounds.
articles.description: It is all-square in the youngest World title match in history; it is D. Gukesh 1, Javokhir Sindarov 1

articles.headline: Costa Rica bans United Nations rapporteur Francesca Albanese over security concerns
articles.title: Why is Israel celebrating Costa Rica’s ban on Francesca Albanese?
articles.summary: Costa Rican immigration authorities barred United Nations independent rapporteur Francesca Albanese from entering the country upon her arrival at Juan Santamaria International Airport on Thursday. Immigration director-general Omer Badilla stated she was refused entry due to an international alert regarding ties to terrorist acts. The decision drew strong condemnation from regional legal groups and university officials, while Israel welcomed the ban.
articles.description: Costa Rica is under pressure over its decision to bar the UN expert who has documented Israel's genocidal war on Gaza.

articles.headline: Kim Jong Un urges wider deployment of tactical nuclear weapons
articles.title: Kim Jong Un says North Korea should widen deployment of tactical nukes
articles.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un called for expanded deployment of tactical nuclear weapons across multiple domains during an inspection reported by state media KCNA on Thursday. Kim stated that North Korea's nuclear status is inviolable and warned that any denial is an open declaration of war amid ongoing border tensions with South Korea.
articles.description: North Korean leader warns attempts to deny country's nuclear status will be seen as "an open declaration of war".

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu Governor seeks report from Chief Minister over lamp lighting dispute
articles.title: Thirupparankundram ‘deepathoon’ row: Tamil Nadu Governor seeks CM Vijay’s report
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar requested a comprehensive report from Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay concerning compliance with a Supreme Court order. The directive mandated lighting the Karthigai Deepam lamp atop the Thirupparankundram hillock. Authorities instead lit the ceremonial lamp only at the traditional Deepa Mandapam after temple trustees allegedly failed to authorise a lamp-lighting team, prompting the constitutional intervention.
articles.description: The move comes in the wake of the ceremonial lamp being lit only at the traditional spot — the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchchipillaiyar Temple — on November 24, defying the Supreme Court’s direction.

articles.headline: Student sent to juvenile home for counselling after bringing gun to school
articles.title: Student sent for mental health care after bringing gun to school in Keralam’s Palakkad
articles.summary: A student who brought a gun to Parudur Higher Secondary School in Pallippuram was transferred to the Government Juvenile Home in Kozhikode for counselling until December 5, as ordered by the Juvenile Justice Board. The student's statement was recorded with parents present, while the bullet removed from an injured student during a Wednesday surgery at Kottakkal was sent to a forensic laboratory for examination following the incident.
articles.description: Police have warned against spreading unverified claims about the gun on social media

articles.headline: Ukrainian forces strike Russian military base and damage aircraft
articles.title: Ukraine says five jets damaged in attack on Russia’s Savasleyka airbase
articles.summary: Ukrainian forces attacked the Savasleyka airbase in the Nizhny Novgorod region on Wednesday, damaging five aircraft including MiG-31 jets and Su-34 fighter-bombers, according to the Ukrainian General Staff. The long-range strike aims to cripple Moscow military capabilities amid ongoing conflict and severe Russian attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure.
articles.description: The Ukrainian General Staff says its forces struck an airbase in the Nizhny Novgorod region east of Moscow.

articles.headline: Student organisations warn school merger scheme could close thousands of institutions
articles.title: ADB-backed scheme may lead to closure of 45,326 govt. schools, says AIDSO
articles.summary: The All India Democratic Students Organisation and the Save Public Education Committee claimed that Karnataka Public Schools Magnet Scheme could close over forty five thousand government schools. Supported by Asian Development Bank funding, the plan involves merging surrounding institutions into new complexes. Student representatives expressed concern over corporate involvement, vocational education changes, and potential restrictions on higher education access.
articles.description: All India Democratic Students Organisation and the Save Public Education Committee are opposing the Karnataka Public Schools magnet scheme

articles.headline: Kashmiri leaders condemn police action against Islamic scholar over Vande Mataram
articles.title: Jammu and Kashmir leaders condemn police summons to religious scholar who opposed Vande Mataram at Waqf event
articles.summary: Political leaders Mehbooba Mufti and Aga Ruhullah Mehdi criticised authorities for summoning Maulana Rehmatullah Qasmi following his opposition to singing Vande Mataram during a Waqf Board event in Srinagar. Opposition figures demanded explanations from the Jammu and Kashmir Police regarding the legality of the inquiry, alleging an ongoing campaign to intimidate religious figures and suppress dissenting voices across the region.
articles.description: Peoples Democratic Party president Mehbooba Mufti said the BJP's agenda to saffronise the Islamic scholars and bring religious voices under its political control is unmistakable

articles.headline: Georgian police detain sixteen people following clashes at European match
articles.title: Why did Georgian police clash with Turkish football fans over Palestine?
articles.summary: Georgian police detained at least 16 individuals after fan clashes temporarily suspended a Europa League match between Turkiye’s Besiktas and Israel’s Hapoel Be’er Sheva in Batumi on Thursday. The fixture was moved to Georgia by UEFA for security reasons. Turkish officials condemned the use of police force against supporters, while Georgian Interior Minister Sulkhan Tamazashvili stated that law enforcement intervened due to aggressive fan behavior during the march.
articles.description: Georgia's Interior Ministry says 16 people were detained and three employees injured during clashes.

articles.headline: Telugu Desam Party president attributes panchayat election success to public confidence
articles.title: Panchayat poll results reflect people’s mandate in favour of coalition: Palla
articles.summary: Telugu Desam Party State president Palla Srinivasa Rao stated that initial Gram Panchayat election results reflect strong public support for the governing coalition. Speaking in Mangalagiri, he credited Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and government welfare programmes for the electoral gains. He also criticised opposition Yuvajana Sramika Rythu Congress Party leaders, urging them to respect the mandate delivered through the recent ballot paper voting process.
articles.description: TDP State president says YSRCP-backed candidates secured only 26% of seats in the first phase; credits welfare schemes and development programmes for coalition’s performance

articles.headline: Denmark foreign minister visits Bengaluru to explore technology cooperation and talent
articles.title: Denmark Foreign Minister discusses technological ties, tapping Indian talent during Bengaluru visit
articles.summary: Denmark Minister for Foreign Affairs Lars Lokke Rasmussen visited Bengaluru to strengthen bilateral technology ties and attract skilled Indian professionals. During his tour, he visited several facilities including the Indian Space Research Organisation and launched a new report on accessing Indian tech talent. The diplomat emphasised that collaboration in sectors like space technology and artificial intelligence can help address domestic labour shortages in Denmark.
articles.description: While exploring the innovations in space-tech, quantum technology and defence-tech in the city, the Minister highlighted the potential for Denmark to attract Indian tech talent

articles.headline: Gadi Eisenkot navigates coalition talks with Benjamin Netanyahu
articles.title: Eisenkot navigates tricky waters as he tests power-sharing with Netanyahu
articles.summary: Following the Israeli elections, opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot faces a complex political dilemma regarding a potential unity government with caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. While Eisenkot attempts to form a coalition without sufficient seats alone, prospective alliances risk alienating his change bloc supporters. Meanwhile, Netanyahu's negotiating position has strengthened following corruption trial developments, threatening political careers and long-standing reform promises.
articles.description: Some of his allies are calling for such an arrangement, but it would represent a betrayal of his pre-election promise.

articles.headline: ASHA workers strike in Bengaluru over pay and benefits
articles.title: ASHAs’ strike: A test of the Congress government’s sensitivity
articles.summary: An indefinite strike by Accredited Social Health Activists in Bengaluru entered its eleventh day on November 27, creating a political test for the Congress government. Workers demand their monthly honorarium increase from 8,000 to 15,000 rupees and better service benefits, following an unimplemented 2025 announcement by then Chief Minister Siddaramaiah. Dismissive remarks from ministers have escalated tensions, handing the opposition Bharatiya Janata Party an advantage.
articles.description: ASHAs’ status as volunteers has kept their remuneration and social security below what regular government employees receive

articles.headline: IN-SPACe report highlights India's heavy reliance on imported satellite components
articles.title: India’s satellite supply chain ‘highly dependent on imports’, says space body
articles.summary: India's satellite manufacturing supply chain remains highly dependent on imports for critical components, according to an Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre report released on November 25, 2026. Chairman Pawan Goenka noted that electronics and specialized materials account for nearly 60% of costs. The autonomous body emphasized that addressing gaps in testing and procurement could help India become a global space exporter.
articles.description: India’s space economy is currently valued at nearly $9 billion and is set to grow to $40-45 billion in less than a decade

articles.headline: Bombay High Court pauses road project pending mangrove loss report
articles.title: Bombay High Court puts road project on hold till State files report on mangrove loss, compensatory measures
articles.summary: The Bombay High Court has halted a road project proposed by the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority until the Maharashtra government submits a comprehensive report regarding mangrove destruction and compensatory afforestation measures. During the hearing on November 27, 2026, the Bench consisting of Chief Justice Mahesh C. Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna directed authorities to provide survival rates and tree cover data before the case resumes on November 30.
articles.description: The Bombay High Court directed the State to submit figures documenting tree cover, losses, and five-year survival rates before any orders are passed

articles.headline: Sentence served, still detained: Palestinian families waiting for reunions
articles.title: Sentence served, still detained: Palestinian families waiting for reunions
articles.description: Palestinian families say their loved ones remain in Israeli prisons despite having completed their sentences.

articles.headline: ISIL blamed for multiple suicide attacks in Syria
articles.title: ISIL blamed for multiple suicide attacks in Syria
articles.description: ISIL suicide attack kills two in an assault on a security post in northeastern Syria.

articles.headline: ISIL suicide attack kills two security personnel in Syria
articles.title: Two Syrian security personnel killed in ISIL suicide attack
articles.summary: An ISIL suicide attack killed two security personnel and wounded five others in Hasakah, Syria, after four gunmen targeted an Internal Security Forces checkpoint on Wednesday. All four assailants died during the incident, which local authorities and Deputy Governor Ahmed al-Hilali vowed to investigate thoroughly to ensure regional stability.
articles.description: Syrian forces say the attack in northeastern Syria's city of Hasakah involved four assailants who were all killed.

articles.headline: Thailand presses Myanmar and China over mining pollution affecting rivers
articles.title: Arsenic in the water: Thailand presses Myanmar over mining pollution
articles.summary: Thailand is urging Myanmar to address unregulated rare-earth and gold mining after high arsenic levels forced the suspension of tap water supplies in 14 villages in the Mae Sai district earlier this month. Following talks in Bangkok this week, Thai and Myanmar officials agreed to joint water sampling on the Kok and Sai rivers. Meanwhile, Bangkok has sought China's backing for a six-month mining suspension and plans to ban chemical exports.
articles.description: Tap water supplies to 14 villages in Mae Sai district near the Myanmar border were suspended earlier this month after arsenic levels were found to be nearly 30 times government limits

articles.headline: Ashutosh Ranka seeks damages from Jitendra Singh over funding remarks
articles.title: CJP’s Ashutosh Ranka seeks ₹3 crore in damages from Jitendra Singh over Pakistan funding remarks
articles.summary: The Cockroach Janta Party legal cell has served a defamation notice to Union Minister Jitendra Singh, demanding an apology and three crore rupees in damages over remarks made at a Bengaluru press conference on November 3, 2026. The notice states that Singh falsely alleged party co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka received funds from Pakistani politicians. Ranka rejected the claims as baseless and stated his professional engagements are fully compliant with Indian tax laws.
articles.description: CJP’s Ashutosh Ranka says he will file a defamation case with the Delhi Police; notice demands retraction, unconditional apology and evidence to substantiate the Minister’s allegations

articles.headline: Al-Qaeda and IS branches adapt strategies and community outreach in Africa and the Middle East
articles.title: Has global jihadism failed, or is it simply changing shape?
articles.summary: Jihadist groups are shifting tactics by engaging in local community outreach, such as aid distribution by al-Shabab in Somalia, and forging alliances closer to home instead of pursuing global attacks. According to reports, this strategic evolution follows significant defeats and the high-profile rise of former militant leaders like Syria's president Ahmed al-Sharaa. Internal debates persist between hardliners and pragmatists regarding compromises.
articles.description: Jihadist groups appear to be focusing on local issues rather than global terror. Does it signify a real change?

articles.headline: European football matches face security concerns following violent fan clashes
articles.title: European football violence causes concern with far-right claim in UEFA game
articles.summary: Violent clashes during two European football matches have prompted condemnation from French and Bulgarian leaders regarding stadium security. A UEFA Europa League match between Marseille and Levski Sofia at the Stade Velodrome on Wednesday involved brawls, metal pipes, and a reported Nazi salute, leaving multiple fans injured. A separate match between Besiktas and Hapoel Be'er Sheva in Batumi was temporarily suspended after fights broke out in the stands.
articles.description: Claims of Nazi salutes at UEFA Europa League game in Marseille headline night of further violence in European football.

articles.headline: Indian rupee drops 60 paise against United States dollar
articles.title: Rupee nosedives 60 paise to settle at 92.98 against U.S. dollar
articles.summary: The Indian rupee depreciated by 60 paise to provisionally settle at 92.98 against the United States dollar on November 27, 2026. According to forex analysts, the domestic currency retreated due to rising crude oil prices driven by geopolitical tensions and a sharp decline in domestic equity markets, despite continuous support from foreign institutional investments during the month.
articles.description: In the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 92.44 and touched the day's low of 93.01 before settling at 92.98 (provisional) against the greenback, logging a steep loss of 60 paise from its previous close.

articles.headline: IBM ends United States visa and green card sponsorship for consulting roles
articles.title: IBM ends U.S. visa, green card sponsorship for most roles in consulting unit
articles.summary: International Business Machines Corporation is discontinuing United States visa and green card sponsorship for the majority of positions within its consulting division. The decision follows mounting regulatory pressure and fees on foreign work visas enacted by the government. Affected employees were reportedly given the choice to relocate abroad or depart by December 31, 2026, receiving three months of severance if they decline relocation.
articles.description: ‘IBM Consulting participates in U.S. high-skilled visa programmes to address skill shortages,’ the company said in a statement

articles.headline: Biju Janata Dal says Odisha interests remain priority ahead of delimitation sessions
articles.title: Odisha’s interest must be protected: BJD on delimitation bill
articles.summary: The Biju Janata Dal stated on November 27, 2026, that it would determine its stance on the amended delimitation bill in the Rajya Sabha only after receiving complete information. Manas Mangaraj, leader of the Biju Janata Dal parliamentary party, noted that no specifics had been provided yet for upcoming special sessions in Parliament, while MP Santrupta Mishra emphasized that Odisha representation must be protected.
articles.description: The regional party says the party will come up with a formal stand once details of bill to be discussed in Parliament is made available

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu begins ration card data clean-up following Union government nudge
articles.title: Nudged by Centre, Tamil Nadu begins ration card data clean-up
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu government has started removing ineligible beneficiaries from Priority Household and Antyodaya Anna Yojana ration cards following lists provided by the federal Department of Food and Public Distribution. A recent study highlighted a high inclusion error rate in Tamil Nadu at thirty eight point seven percent. Authorities removed over three lakh beneficiaries by July thirty-one, while the State continues incurring a fourteen thousand crore rupee food subsidy bill.
articles.description: Following a study, the Centre has sent two lists of ineligible beneficiaries to the State

articles.headline: Indian stock markets snap two-day rally as Sensex plunges 989 points
articles.title: Stock markets snap two-day rally; Sensex tanks 989 points amid profit booking
articles.summary: Benchmark equity indices ended their two-day rally on November 27, 2026, driven by profit-taking in blue-chip information technology stocks and rising crude oil prices. The BSE Sensex fell 989.33 points to settle at 83,339.26, while the NSE Nifty declined 277.30 points to 25,607.20. Global factors, including rising Brent crude and a stronger Asian market performance, influenced the domestic trading session.
articles.description: The 30-share BSE Sensex tanked 989.33 points, or 1.17%, to settle at 83,339.26

articles.headline: Bangladesh state minister calls deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina bilateral thorn
articles.title: Hasina has become a ‘thorn’ in Bangladesh-India ties: Minister Humaiun Kobir
articles.summary: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir stated in Dhaka on November 27, 2026, that ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina is damaging relations between Bangladesh and India. According to the report, Ms. Hasina faces a death sentence in Bangladesh over a 2024 crackdown and plans to return on December 16, though Mr. Kobir insisted she will only be handed over via extradition.
articles.description: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir says New Delhi is beginning to realise the strain the former Prime Minister’s presence in India is causing to bilateral relations

articles.headline: Houthi group targets Saudi Arabian ports and capital amid escalating regional strikes
articles.title: Houthis target Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea ports as strikes escalate
articles.summary: Yemen’s Houthi group struck Saudi Arabia’s Jizan port and targeted Riyadh and Jeddah on Wednesday, prompting air defence interceptions, as fighting intensified near Taiz. A Saudi-led coalition reported hundreds of air strikes against the group, while the Houthis claimed numerous attacks on civilian sites across Yemen, raising concerns over the humanitarian impact on the vital Hodeidah port.
articles.description: Explosion reported in Sanaa after Saudi air defenses intercept ballistic missiles targeting Riyadh.

articles.headline: Hong Kong residential complex renovation fire leaves 168 people dead
articles.title: A renovation was meant to improve these Hong Kong homes - it ended in a blaze that killed 168
articles.summary: A fast-moving fire at the Wang Fuk Court apartment complex in Hong Kong resulted in 168 fatalities on November 26, 2025. An independent committee report attributed the tragedy to human errors, disabled fire alarms, and flammable scaffolding materials used during mandatory building renovations. Surviving relatives shared accounts of personal loss and subsequent psychological trauma following the unprecedented disaster.
articles.description: A year after one of Hong Kong's deadliest fires, families left behind are still waiting for justice.

articles.headline: Former Kenyan governor jailed for 25 years for murder
articles.title: Ex-Kenyan governor jailed for 25 years over pregnant girlfriend's murder
articles.summary: The High Court sentenced former Migori County governor Zacharia Okoth Obado to 25 years in prison for the 2018 murder of Sharon Belyne Otieno, who was pregnant with his child. Judge Cecilia Githua delivered the sentence alongside terms for two former co-accused aides. The conviction follows a trial involving 42 witnesses, highlighting issues of violence against women and holding senior political figures accountable in Kenya.
articles.description: The pregnant student was murdered after leaving a hotel with a journalist she had contacted to discuss her affair with the governor.

articles.headline: Arvind Kejriwal urges support in Punjab as opposition criticises rally
articles.title: All election guarantees fulfilled, says Arvind Kejriwal; Opposition slams AAP of misusing public resources
articles.summary: On November 26, 2026, Aam Aadmi Party national convener Arvind Kejriwal addressed a rally in Moga, Punjab, urging women to support the party ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. He stated that all election guarantees, including free electricity and health insurance cards worth 10 lakh rupees, had been fulfilled. Meanwhile, opposition leaders Partap Singh Bajwa and Kewal Singh Dhillon accused the government of misusing public resources and failing to address financial mismanagement.
articles.description: The Opposition parties accuse AAP of misusing Punjab’s public resources to organise a party event while the State grapples with a mounting financial crisis

articles.headline: Why Benjamin Netanyahu’s corruption trial could be unravelling
articles.title: Why Benjamin Netanyahu’s corruption trial could be unravelling
articles.description: Could Netanyahu escape his most serious corruption charges? Al Jazeera's Lina-Serene explains.

articles.headline: Kashmiri chief cleric placed under house arrest following Vande Mataram dispute
articles.title: Mirwaiz says he was put under house arrest over Vande Mataram issue, decries action against Maulana Qasimi
articles.summary: Kashmir chief cleric Mirwaiz Umar Farooq stated he was placed under house arrest and another prominent religious figure was summoned by police over their opposition to playing Vande Mataram at a Jammu and Kashmir Waqf Board function. The cleric criticized the ruling regime for using pressure tactics regarding religious matters. Meanwhile, Grand Mufti Nasir-ul-Islam declared that reciting the song is unacceptable under Islamic law.
articles.description: It has become a precedent that every time I raise people’s issues and concerns, I am not allowed to go to Jama Masjid on that Friday, says the chief cleric

articles.headline: Uganda announces plans to withdraw its troops from Lubero in DR Congo
articles.title: Uganda to withdraw troops from DR Congo town amid diplomatic row
articles.summary: Ugandan authorities announced the planned withdrawal of military forces from Lubero town in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo within two weeks, handing security back to Congolese forces. The decision coincides with escalating diplomatic tensions between the neighboring countries following controversial social media remarks by a top Ugandan military commander regarding regional rebel movements.
articles.description: The Ugandan army is helping the Congolese military fight an Islamist militant group in the east of the country.

articles.headline: Shiromani Akali Dal and Bharatiya Janata Party reunite ahead of upcoming Punjab assembly election
articles.title: Punjab polls: SAD, BJP reunification puts both parties back in the reckoning
articles.summary: The Shiromani Akali Dal and the Bharatiya Janata Party announced their reunification ahead of the upcoming 2027 Punjab Assembly election. Political observers noted that the alliance repositions both parties in the reckoning, as the state's political landscape increasingly points toward a competitive four-cornered electoral contest leading up to the polls scheduled for early next year.
articles.description: Had they contested separately, the SAD and the BJP would likely have split the Opposition space, leaving the AAP and the Congress as the principal rivals; united, they have become serious contenders

articles.headline: Amicus report highlights significant waste management deficiencies across Keralam
articles.title: NGT-appointed amicus report flags gaps in Keralam’s solid, liquid waste management
articles.summary: A report filed by an amicus curiae appointed by the National Green Tribunal revealed multiple gaps in solid and liquid waste management across Keralam. The observation note stated that approximately four-fifths of sanitary waste remains untreated and highlighted concerns over inert waste being used for land filling without proper safety safeguards.
articles.description: The report stated that about four-fifths of sanitary waste is not scientifically treated. Only 42.1 tonnes per day of the total sanitary waste of 203.66 tonnes generated daily is treated. Even when all projects are complete, the capacity will be 113.25 tonnes per day

articles.headline: Keralam faces widening rainfall deficit as southwest monsoon enters final lap
articles.title: Keralam may witness early summer-like conditions this year as rain deficit set to widen further
articles.summary: Keralam is experiencing a deficient southwest monsoon season with rainfall already measuring twenty-two percent below normal levels. The India Meteorological Department forecasts little prospect for rainfall revival in September due to suppressing atmospheric conditions, raising concerns over water and power availability, particularly in Wayanad and Idukki districts.

articles.headline: Australia imposes counterterrorism sanctions on two men linked to Iran
articles.title: Australia sanctions suspects in Iran-linked anti-Semitic attacks
articles.summary: Australia imposed counterterrorism financing sanctions targeting Zohair Hassib and Kazem Hamad for allegedly orchestrating anti-Semitic arson attacks against a Sydney restaurant and a Melbourne synagogue in 2024 on behalf of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. Foreign Minister Penny Wong stated the measures restrict the suspects from accessing funds to carry out further attacks.
articles.description: Sanctions aim to restrict funds for two men alleged to have planned attacks for IRGC.

articles.headline: Severe storms leave hundreds of thousands without power across US coasts
articles.title: Hundreds of thousands still without power after storms hit US on Thanksgiving
articles.summary: Severe storms struck both coasts of the United States on Thursday during the Thanksgiving holiday, leaving hundreds of thousands of people without power and causing widespread flight delays and cancellations. According to monitoring site Poweroutage.us, Pennsylvania experienced the highest number of power cuts. United States President Donald Trump said he would consider releasing emergency funds to assist affected eastern areas.
articles.description: Pennsylvania and neighbouring states remain badly affected on Friday after both coasts were lashed with wind and rain.

articles.headline: European football matches disrupted by fan violence and police clashes
articles.title: Clashes mar European games as Macron condemns violence
articles.summary: Violent fan altercations disrupted several European football fixtures on November 26, 2026, prompting French President Emmanuel Macron to condemn stadium unrest at Marseille. Supporters clashed during matches involving Marseille and Levski Sofia, Besiktas and Hapoel Be'er-Sheva in Georgia, and Sunderland against Jagiellonia Bialystok. Multiple injuries were reported during the incidents, leading to international condemnation from government officials and sports authorities across the affected nations.
articles.description: Violent clashes mar a number of European football matches on Thursday night, with French president Emmanuel Macron condemning trouble at Marseille's home game against Levski Sofia.

articles.headline: Monsoon set to begin on June 4 but expected to remain sluggish
articles.title: Monsoon may remain subdued after vigorous onset in Kerala
articles.summary: The southwest monsoon is scheduled to begin on June 4, 2026, in Kerala after missing earlier predicted onset dates. India Meteorological Department Director Neetha K. Gopal stated that the monsoon current will likely remain sluggish in June following a vigorous onset. Unusually warm ocean waters in the tropical Pacific, linked to developing El Niño conditions, are forecast to aggravate the bleak season.
articles.description: The southwest monsoon is set to reach the Kerala coast on June 4. IMD issues orange alert for Alappuzha, Kottayam, Ernakulam, and Thrissur on Wednesday, warning of intense rainfall

articles.headline: Pakistan hosts trilateral defence talks with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye
articles.title: Pakistan set to host talks with Saudi Arabia, Turkey under trilateral defence pact
articles.summary: Senior diplomats and military officials from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye convened in Islamabad on November 27, 2026, under a mutual defence pact that treats aggression against one member as an attack on all three. The discussions address regional security developments, including Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, while Islamabad simultaneously promotes diplomatic efforts between Washington and Tehran.
articles.description: The talks in Islamabad will focus on West Asia and the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, two security officials said, with Pakistan’s Defence and Foreign Ministers and army chief attending

articles.headline: US approves SpaceX plan to deploy one million orbital data centres
articles.title: Why does Elon Musk want to put a million satellite data centres in space?
articles.summary: The United States Federal Communications Commission authorised a SpaceX plan named Starmind on Wednesday to deploy one million orbital compute modules in low-latency space. Federal Communications Commission Chairman Brendan Carr said the initiative reinforces economic leadership and technological innovation. However, the American Astronomical Society expressed deep concern that the proposed satellite constellation would significantly undermine astronomical research.
articles.description: The US FCC authorised the plan on Wednesday, calling it a first in the history of the country.

articles.headline: Keralam records seventh-lowest southwest monsoon season with rainfall deficit
articles.title: Keralam witnesses 7th-lowest southwest monsoon season
articles.summary: Keralam concluded its southwest monsoon season on September 30 with a significant 28 percent rainfall deficit, receiving 1,446.5 millimetres of rain against the normal 2,018.6 millimetres. According to India Meteorological Department data, this marks the seventh-lowest seasonal rainfall recorded since 1901. Districts including Idukki and Wayanad experienced severe impacts, receiving around 50 percent less precipitation than normal and facing drought conditions.
articles.description: According to India Meteorological Department data, nearly 70% of the State remained significantly rain-deficient at the end of the season on September 30. Northeast monsoon, which normally sets in by mid-October, may be below normal during the opening month

articles.headline: Fuel tanker crash on Cairo highway causes massive fire killing thirty-one
articles.title: Thirty-one killed in massive fire as fuel tanker crashes on Cairo highway
articles.summary: Thirty-one people died and twenty-one others suffered injuries after a fuel tanker crashed and burst into flames on a busy highway in the Warraq neighbourhood of Cairo on Wednesday evening, according to the health ministry. Officials stated the vehicle overturned following a fallen power cable. The regional public prosecutor initiated an investigation into the deadly accident.
articles.description: Another 21 are injured after the tanker reportedly overturns on a busy ring road in the Egyptian capital.

articles.headline: Tehran residents battle severe year-round air pollution alongside military threats
articles.title: ‘I cannot go to work’: Iranians contend with pollution as well as US war
articles.summary: Residents in Tehran and other major Iranian cities face persistent year-round air pollution alongside military tensions with the United States. Fine particulate matter concentrations frequently trigger health warnings from the Meteorological Organization, leading to school closures and remote work options. Ministry of Health figures indicate that winter hospital visits for respiratory and heart conditions increase by as much as 50 percent.
articles.description: Hospital admissions for respiratory ailments have soared as the winter smog sets in.

articles.headline: Indian police rescue foreign nationals from cyberfraud and trafficking ring
articles.title: India busts cyberfraud and trafficking network rescuing 164 foreigners
articles.summary: Law enforcement officials in Noida rescued 92 Indonesian and 72 Malaysian nationals who were allegedly duped into forced cybercrime activities after arriving in India on promises of IT jobs. Authorities seized hundreds of electronic devices, arrested one Malaysian suspect, and launched an investigation amid a sharp nationwide surge in digital investment scams.
articles.description: Lured by IT job promises, the victims were allegedly forced into cybercrime, police say.

articles.headline: US congressional Democrats call for immediate end to military conflict in Iran
articles.title: Democrats want to end Trump’s Iran war. But how different are they?
articles.summary: Following midterm electoral victories, Democratic leaders in the United States have demanded a swift conclusion to the ongoing war involving Iran, which has driven up global energy prices. While party figures distance themselves from Republican policies, analysts note a long history of bipartisan hostility and economic pressure directed toward Tehran by successive administrations.
articles.description: Decades of bipartisan pressure on Tehran raises questions about how far Democrats are willing to change US policy.

articles.headline: Global tech stocks decline further amid ongoing concerns over artificial intelligence investment
articles.title: US stocks fall further as fears over AI intensify
articles.summary: Major technology firms experienced sharp share price drops on Wednesday, with losses affecting Nvidia, Anthropic, Amazon, and Meta. The downturn reflects persistent investor anxiety regarding the sustainability of artificial intelligence spending and recent political developments in the United States. Despite the market volatility, investment bank Goldman Sachs projects that artificial intelligence spending will surpass one trillion dollars in 2026.
articles.description: All three main US indexes were down in early trading, with the tech-dominated Nasdaq down almost 4%.

articles.headline: Gaza municipalities warn winter rains threaten displaced Palestinian shelter camps
articles.title: Winter rains threaten 1,000 Gaza shelter sites, councils warn
articles.summary: Gaza municipal leaders warned on Wednesday that upcoming winter storms threaten roughly one thousand displacement camps due to damaged drainage systems and missing repair supplies. The Union of Gaza Strip Municipalities stated that recent November rains already flooded about seventy thousand tents. Meanwhile, European Commission representatives urged Israel to permit waiting humanitarian aid trucks carrying tents to enter the enclave.
articles.description: About 200,000 tents need replacing, Gaza’s municipalities say, as the EU urges Israel to reopen all crossings.

articles.headline: Guinea-Bissau military leaders delay civilian rule return until 2028
articles.title: Guinea-Bissau's military leaders delay return to civilian rule until 2028
articles.summary: Military rulers in Guinea-Bissau have postponed presidential and parliamentary elections from December to 26 November 2028, delaying the handover to civilian governance. Transitional President Gen Horta N'Tam stated that inadequate technical, material, and financial conditions forced the delay. The announcement follows the November 2025 coup that ousted former President Umaro Sissoco Embaló amid disputed election results and ongoing political instability since 1974.
articles.description: The announcement comes a year after a military coup with its leaders promising a return to civilian rule within 12 months.

articles.headline: Indian officials upbeat about 2036 Olympic Games host bid
articles.title: India upbeat about first Olympic Games after ‘very good’ 2036 presentation
articles.summary: Indian Olympic Association officials expressed confidence in their bid to host the 2036 Olympic Games after presenting Ahmedabad as the candidate city to the International Olympic Committee. Chief Executive Raghuram Iyer described the online presentation as very successful. Ahmedabad will also host the 2030 Commonwealth Games, while a final decision on the 2036 host city is expected after the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics or in early 2029.
articles.description: India makes Ahmedabad pitch for 2036 Games as it bids to host first Olympics, but Qatar and South Africa strong rivals.

articles.headline: Punjab chief minister launches scheme to distribute ration cards
articles.title: Punjab CM launches Smart Ration Card Scheme to benefit 10 lakh beneficiaries
articles.summary: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann launched the Smart Ration Card Scheme to extend food-security benefits to ten lakh beneficiaries across the state. Distributed alongside Aam Aadmi Party national convenor Arvind Kejriwal in Moga, eligible households will receive Meri Rasoi kits and free wheat under the National Food Security Act following a transparent digital selection process.
articles.description: The Chief Minister assured the beneficiaries of five kg of free wheat per family member per month after the completion of e-KYC

articles.headline: Costa Rica blocks entry of United Nations rapporteur Francesca Albanese
articles.title: Costa Rica bars entry to UN rapporteur over ‘links to terrorist acts’
articles.summary: Costa Rican immigration authorities denied entry to United Nations special rapporteur Francesca Albanese at the airport serving San Jose. According to the immigration director general, the decision followed an international alert regarding terrorist links. The official stated the action protected national security as she arrived to receive an honorary degree from the University of Costa Rica.
articles.description: Francesca Albanese arrived at the airport serving the capital, San Jose, to receive an honorary degree from the University of Costa Rica, a public university

articles.headline: Supreme Court dismisses plea to remove political summit videos
articles.title: Supreme Court rejects plea to remove video of Italian politician’s ‘Vote Chor’ slogan at Bharat Summit 2026
articles.summary: The Supreme Court dismissed a petition seeking the removal of videos showing Italian politician Giacomo Filibeck raising a controversial slogan at the Bharat Summit 2026 in Hyderabad. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh rejected the plea after petitioner counsel Syed Rizwan Ahmed argued that the foreign official interfered in domestic political issues.
articles.description: After the Bench said it was dismissing the petition, the petitioner’s counsel urged that the authorities be asked to treat the same as a representation

articles.headline: Madras High Court refuses to reject election petition against chief minister
articles.title: Madras High Court refuses to reject election petition challenging CM Vijay’s victory from Perambur
articles.summary: The Madras High Court dismissed an application by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to reject an election petition challenging his victory in the Perambur Assembly constituency. Justice V. Lakshminarayanan ruled that the petitioner established a valid cause of action for a full trial regarding alleged property misrepresentations in the 2026 election affidavit, which the Chief Minister denied.
articles.description: Justice V. Lakshminarayanan dismisses an application filed by the Chief Minister to reject the election petition filed by a voter, S. Dinesh

articles.headline: WhatsApp introduces in-app travel eSIM purchase for international users
articles.title: WhatsApp to let users buy travel eSIMs in app; Jio, Verizon among partners
articles.summary: Meta-owned messaging platform WhatsApp announced on November 26, 2026, that users will soon be able to purchase and install data eSIMs directly within the application for international travel. Partnering with telecommunications companies such as Jio and Verizon, the feature aims to eliminate roaming charges and airport kiosk visits, allowing travellers to maintain their existing phone numbers seamlessly abroad.
articles.description: WhatsApp Head Kunal Shah described the effort as the company's early explorations around eSIMs in a post on X

articles.headline: Border Security Force personnel shoot dead Pakistani intruder in Punjab
articles.title: Pakistan intruder shot dead by BSF troops along IB in Punjab
articles.summary: Border Security Force troops shot and killed a Pakistani intruder along the International Border in Punjab after he ignored warnings to halt. According to officials, the incident occurred near the Pahadpur border post along the Ujh River in Pathankot as the individual continued advancing toward the border boundary.
articles.description: The intruder was challenged and asked to stop, but he continued moving towards the International Border (IB) and was shot by the BSF troops, says officials

articles.headline: Swiss cybersecurity office reports five cyber attacks using AI agents
articles.title: AI agents used in five cyber attacks in Switzerland, government says
articles.summary: According to the Federal Office for Cybersecurity, five recent cyber attacks in Switzerland utilized artificial intelligence agents to target companies and critical infrastructure operators, successfully compromising systems in four cases. The targeted entities included providers of electricity, water, and telecommunications. Officials did not identify the perpetrators but advised organizations to implement protective measures and regular cyber tests.
articles.description: In four ⁠of the five cases, the attacks were ​successful and systems ‌were compromised, BACS said

articles.headline: Costa Rica denies entry to UN rapporteur Francesca Albanese
articles.title: Costa Rica denies entry to UN’s Albanese over ‘links to terrorist acts’
articles.summary: Costa Rican immigration authorities barred United Nations Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese from entering the country at Juan Santamaria International Airport due to national security concerns. Omer Badilla, director-general of the immigration authority, stated she was the subject of an international alert regarding terrorist acts. Albanese condemned the detention as a disgrace while travelling to receive an honorary doctorate.
articles.description: Authorities said the UN special rapporteur was blocked from entering the country due to 'national security' risks.

articles.headline: Early life sugar restriction reduces cancer incidence and aging pace
articles.title: Sugar restriction during first 1000 days of life reduces cancer incidence, pace of ageing: study
articles.summary: Reducing sugar exposure during the first 1,000 days of life substantially lowers cancer risk decades later and slows biological aging. A United Kingdom study published in PNAS analyzed 64,761 adults and found that individuals who experienced sugar rationing had up to 69 percent lower cancer incidence, 2.2 fewer years of biological aging, and persistent healthy eating habits.
articles.description: Researchers uncovered two pathways for this: people unexposed to sugar early ate smaller quantities, and maintained healthier, more diverse diets five decades later; they also exhibited a longer leukocyte telomere, the protective DNA–protein cap at the ends of chromosomes inside a white blood cell length

articles.headline: Benjamin Netanyahu calls for immediate end to corruption trial
articles.title: Netanyahu says corruption trial ‘must end’ as court suggests dropping case
articles.summary: Caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu demanded the immediate conclusion of his ongoing corruption trial after judges in Jerusalem expressed significant doubt regarding the bribery charges against him. During a court hearing on Wednesday, judges indicated low chances of conviction in Case 4000. Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara stated she would consider the recommendations as political opponents negotiate coalition pacts.
articles.description: The judges' recommendations came as Israel's longest-serving prime minister fights for his political survival.

articles.headline: Deadly floods leave parts of Ecuador under water
articles.title: Deadly floods leave parts of Ecuador under water
articles.description: Deadly floods have submerged homes, businesses and roads across Ecuador.

articles.headline: AirAsia delays employee salary payments to conserve cash reserves
articles.title: AirAsia delays staff salary payments to end of month, internal email shows
articles.summary: AirAsia informed employees via an internal email that salary payments will be postponed to the end of each month from November through March. Chief People Officer Muhammad Khurram Zia cited challenging operating conditions and soaring jet fuel costs linked to the Iran war. Meanwhile, AirAsia Philippines announced workforce reductions following mounting financial pressures and sliding quarterly cash balances.
articles.description: Salary payments during the five-month period would be made on the 30th of each month ‌or the last day of February, the notice said

articles.headline: Aam Aadmi Party marks 14th foundation day with political reflections
articles.title: We changed politics, but much remains to be done: Kejriwal on AAP’s 14th foundation day
articles.summary: Aam Aadmi Party chief Arvind Kejriwal stated that the party defied scepticism and won public trust across India during its fourteen-year journey. Marking the milestone on November 27, 2026, the former Delhi Chief Minister emphasized that the organization formed governments in Delhi and Punjab while focusing on education and healthcare. Senior leader Manish Sisodia added that the party aims to demonstrate honest governance.
articles.description: AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal marked the party’s 14th Foundation Day on November 26, 2026, saying the party has withstood skepticism about its survival and grown from Delhi to win trust across India, with governments in Delhi and Punjab and support from Jammu and Kashmir to Goa and Gujarat, while promising more work on education, healthcare, and anti-corruption

articles.headline: New Zealand election final results leave conservative coalition short of majority
articles.title: New Zealand election results set up tricky talks for conservative incumbent
articles.summary: Final results from New Zealand's November 7 election show Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's conservative National Party coalition fell one seat short of a parliamentary majority. Released on Friday, the outcome requires Luxon to seek additional support from minor parties like Qiulae Wong's Opportunity Party to form a stable government, with political analysts anticipating challenging coalition negotiations ahead.
articles.description: Conservative PM Luxon and populist coalition partners face negotiations with centrist kingmaker.

articles.headline: Eurozone inflation climbs to three-year high amid rising energy costs
articles.title: ‘Borrowing to make ends meet’: The rising cost of living in Europe
articles.summary: Eurozone inflation doubled from two percent in December 2025 to four percent in October 2026, driven largely by energy price spikes caused by Middle East conflicts. According to Eurostat, Lithuania, Bulgaria, and Greece recorded the highest inflation rates in the region. Households across Europe face mounting financial pressure, forcing many to tighten household budgets and borrow money to cover essential living expenses.
articles.description: Prices are climbing again across Europe as energy costs surge.

articles.headline: Israeli judges recommend dropping bribery charges against Benjamin Netanyahu
articles.title: Israeli judges recommend dropping most serious charges against Netanyahu
articles.summary: Judges at the Jerusalem District Court suggested that prosecutors drop bribery charges against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during a Wednesday hearing. The panel summoned Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara to state that conviction chances are low in the primary case. Netanyahu praised the development as his political rival Gadi Eisenkot attempts to form a new government administration.
articles.description: The Israeli PM says his trial should end after judges said there was little chance of conviction in one of three cases.

articles.headline: Dozens killed in Egypt vehicle fire
articles.title: Dozens killed in Egypt vehicle fire
articles.description: At least 30 have been ⁠killed and ⁠15 injured when a vehicle carrying ‌petroleum products caught fire in Egypt.

articles.headline: What we know about Trump's Thanksgiving tariffs
articles.title: What we know about Trump's Thanksgiving tariffs
articles.description: Donald Trump is targeting China, the European Union and 12 other jurisdictions in a new round of tariffs.

articles.headline: Severe storm disrupts Thanksgiving holiday celebrations across the United States
articles.title: Major storm batters U.S. on Thanksgiving holiday; 400 flights cancelled
articles.summary: A powerful nor-easter storm battered the central and eastern United States on Thursday, leaving hundreds of thousands without electricity and prompting flight cancellations. Organizers postponed New York's Macy’s parade to Saturday out of safety concerns over high winds. Officials issued travel warnings, declared states of emergency, and requested water conservation in parts of Maryland due to potential infrastructure strains.
articles.description: New York’s famed Macy’s parade was postponed for the first time in its 100-year history

articles.headline: Ukrainian laser downs Russian jet-powered drone in world first
articles.title: Ukrainian laser downs Russian jet-powered drone in world first
articles.description: Ukraine says that its Blysk laser system has intercepted a Russian jet-powered drone in combat for the first time

articles.headline: US Federal Communications Commission approves SpaceX space data centres
articles.title: US grants SpaceX approval for 1 million space data centres
articles.summary: The United States Federal Communications Commission authorised Elon Musk's SpaceX to deploy a constellation of one million space data centres named Starmind. Agency Chairman Brendan Carr stated the decision on Wednesday marks a historical first to support growing artificial intelligence computing demands. Rival companies have previously criticized the ambitious orbital infrastructure deployment plan.
articles.description: Elon Musk hails FCC's approval of SpaceX's Starmind project as 'a great asset to America and the world.'

articles.headline: Trump administration announces new tariffs on fourteen trading partners
articles.title: World reacts to Trump’s new tariffs as US stocks tumble
articles.summary: The United States administration announced new import tariffs targeting fourteen major trading partners, including China and the European Union, citing structural manufacturing overcapacity. The levies follow an investigation led by Trade Representative Jamieson Greer under Section 301. Following the announcement on Wednesday, US stock indices tumbled significantly while bond yields dropped across both America and Europe.
articles.description: The new levies come after an eight-month investigation launched by the United States Trade Representative.

articles.headline: Karnataka regional airports face severe turbulence following UDAN subsidy expiry
articles.title: Up in the air: Karnataka’s regional airports hit turbulence
articles.summary: Karnataka lost its newest facility at Shivamogga Airport after sole operator Star Air halted services following the end of its three-year UDAN subsidy. Across seven regional airports in the state, airlines frequently dropped routes due to poor financial viability. Stakeholders are now working to restore air connectivity to key destinations across the region.
articles.description: It has been a challenging phase for Karnataka’s seven Tier-I and Tier-II airports, as airlines have frequently dropped routes citing poor financial viability post the subsidy period under the ambitious UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Naagrik) scheme. The Hindu examines the growing uncertainty they face...

articles.headline: Janata Dal United backs special parliament session for reservation bills
articles.title: ‘Honest attempt’: JDU backs special Parliament session, urges Opposition to support bills
articles.summary: The Janata Dal United supported the upcoming special session of Parliament called by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, urging the opposition to cooperate in passing the Women Reservation Bill and Delimitation Bill. National spokesperson Rajeev Ranjan Prasad stated that the session is an honest effort to fulfill reservation promises for women ahead of the parliamentary sittings scheduled from November 30.

articles.headline: Thirteen year old murder accused interviewed by lawyers in central Keralam
articles.title: The Age of Crime: Why there is a call to lower juvenile age threshold following rise in crimes by minors in Keralam
articles.summary: A thirteen year old girl accused in a murder case was visited by lawyers at a Child Protection Officer's lounge in central Keralam. The volunteers provided psychological and legal support while discussing a rehabilitation plan. Initially reclusive, the minor grew amiable after speaking with her mother on the telephone for the first time.
articles.description: Back-to-back incidents of heinous crimes involving juveniles have given rise to a public demand for amending the Juvenile Justice Act to lower the age threshold. Child rights campaigners, however, caution against lowering the age limit and say such changes shall be considered only after wide consultations. K.S. Sudhi takes a look at opposing view points.

articles.headline: Indian viewers embrace Pakistani dramas despite official bans and crackdowns
articles.title: ‘You can’t stop it’: Indians embrace Pakistani dramas, defying bans
articles.summary: Indian audiences increasingly consume Pakistani television dramas like Dar-e-Nijaat using virtual private networks despite official government bans following political tensions. Cultural enthusiasts organize private screenings and engage online, generating substantial viewership for Pakistani channels. Stakeholders attribute the enduring popularity to cultural similarities, high production quality, and relatable storytelling across the border.
articles.description: India has tried to keep Pakistani dramas off its screens since May 2025. But Indians can't get enough of these shows.

articles.headline: Japanese Space Agency unveils prototype rover for lunar exploration mission
articles.title: Prototype of Chandrayaan-5/LUPEX rover unveiled
articles.summary: The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency displayed the vehicle at the Chofu Aerospace Centre on November 25, 2026. Scheduled for a 2028 launch, the Chandrayaan-5 initiative is a joint venture between India and Japan to study lunar volatiles at the south pole. The Indian Space Research Organisation will provide the lander and instruments alongside contributions from foreign agencies.
articles.description: The Chandrayaan-5/LuPEX mission is the fifth mission in the Chandrayaan series of lunar missions; JAXA, the Japanese space agency, unveiled the rover in Japan on November 25

articles.headline: Communist Party of India Marxist urges DMK to clarify delimitation stance
articles.title: CPI(M) urges DMK to spell out its position on delimitation
articles.summary: Communist Party of India Marxist State secretary P. Shanmugam urged the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam leadership to explicitly clarify its position on upcoming parliamentary delimitation discussions. Addressing reports of a potential understanding between the Union government and the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam, the party emphasized that the interests of Tamil Nadu and other southern states must remain fully protected.
articles.description: Reports that the Union government has reached an understanding with the DMK on the issue are worrying, CPI(M) State secretary Shanmugam says

articles.headline: 'It's impossible': Spain's young people on housing ahead of Sunday's election
articles.title: 'It's impossible': Spain's young people on housing ahead of Sunday's election
articles.description: Europe correspondent Nick Beake speaks to one couple kept apart by high rents in Valencia.

articles.headline: Ukrainian drone strikes hit industrial facilities in Russia's Samara region
articles.title: Ukraine says it struck two oil refineries in Russia's Samara region
articles.summary: Ukrainian drone attacks struck industrial facilities in Syzran and killed one person in Samara on November 25, 2026, according to local authorities. Governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev reported that air defence downed 145 drones, causing power outages. Unverified social media reports indicated two oil refineries were hit, following Russian President Vladimir Putin's pledge to retaliate for previous strikes.
articles.description: Samara’s regional governor, ​Vyacheslav Fedorishchev, said on social media that local air defence ⁠forces had downed 145 Ukrainian drones overnight, causing power outages

articles.headline: Congress party wins majority of up zila pramukh posts in Rajasthan
articles.title: Congress maintains dominance in Rajasthan panchayat polls with up zila pramukh victories
articles.summary: The opposition Congress party secured deputy chairperson positions in twenty-five of thirty-seven districts across Rajasthan during local body elections. According to election results, the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party won eight districts, while regional groups claimed the remaining seats. Voting outcomes demonstrated the impact of last-minute political realignments and cross-voting throughout the state.
articles.description: The Opposition party won deputy chairperson posts in 25 of 37 districts, while the BJP secured eight and the Bharat Adivasi Party three

articles.headline: Houthi drone and missile attacks test Saudi Arabia security
articles.title: Inside Saudi Arabia, Houthi attacks test kingdom's image of security
articles.summary: An escalation in Houthi military actions following the collapse of a ceasefire in Yemen has brought frequent drone and missile attacks against Saudi Arabian cities. Data from the Armed Conflict Location and Event Data Project identified 274 attacks over five months, including a deadly strike at Riyadh international airport. The campaign threatens the kingdom's efforts to project economic stability and attract international tourism despite rapid structural repairs.
articles.description: Despite the strikes, markets and restaurants in Riyadh remain busy as residents express trust in the government to protect them.

articles.headline: Seventeen year old hospitalized in Keralam due to mercury in skin cream
articles.title: Mercury in cosmetics: What does the Keralam case reveal about health risks of skin-lightening creams | Explained
articles.summary: A seventeen year old girl from Areekode in Malappuram district was hospitalized with Membranous nephropathy after using a skin-lightening cream containing twelve thousand five hundred ppm of mercury. The patient is now recovering following prolonged treatment, prompting police and drug regulatory authorities to crack down on dubious cosmetic products across the region.
articles.description: What does the recent case in Keralam reveal about mercury poisoning from cosmetics? How does exposure affect the kidneys, and what safeguards are in place to regulate unsafe products?

articles.headline: Spanish party leaders clash over housing crisis in final debate
articles.title: Leaders clash in final Spain election debate as housing dominates run-in
articles.summary: Spain's main political leaders confronted each other in a final television debate dominated by the housing crisis ahead of Sunday's election. Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez defended his emergency tenant protections, while conservative challenger Alberto Núñez Feijóo pledged to construct one million homes. Opinion polls indicate Sánchez may lose power, potentially forming a right-wing government with the Vox party, as high living costs and rising rents concern voters across the country.
articles.description: The struggle many face in buying a home has been the biggest issue of a bitter campaign.

articles.headline: Israeli airstrike in Gaza kills senior Hamas official and family
articles.title: Israeli strike kills Hamas official, his wife and children
articles.summary: An Israeli military airstrike in the Beach refugee camp killed Hamas colonel Mohammad Abuelouf alongside his wife and two children on November 25, 2026, according to medics and Gaza's Interior Ministry. The military stated Abuelouf advanced attacks against Israeli forces in violation of a ceasefire. The attack followed another strike that killed internal security head Naeem Abu Nahel.
articles.description: The Israeli military confirmed it had killed Abuelouf, whom it described as a significant figure who "served as ‌a key source of expertise in efforts to restrict the IDF’s counterterrorism operations in the ‌Gaza ⁠Strip"

articles.headline: Spain prepares for snap general election amid rising political tensions
articles.title: Spain’s 2026 election explained in maps and charts
articles.summary: Millions of eligible voters across Spain will participate in a snap general election following the collapse of previous housing relief measures. Polling organizations indicate the centre-right People's Party may win the highest number of seats in the Congress of Deputies, though forming a governing majority likely requires support from the far-right Vox party.
articles.description: Spaniards vote on November 29 in a snap general election. Here is how the system works, the parties and the key issues.

articles.headline: FCC authorizes SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI satellites
articles.title: FCC signs off on SpaceX’s plan to put up to 1 million data center satellites into space
articles.summary: The Federal Communications Commission approved a plan by Elon Musk-owned SpaceX to launch up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites under the Starmind initiative, marking the first agency approval for a full satellite constellation. The decision requires at least one deployment by 2033 and full completion by 2040, though the agency deferred a request regarding graveyard orbits due to insufficient disposal details.
articles.description: In an announcement on Wednesday, the FCC says it authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites as part of the Elon Musk-owned company's "Starmind" initiative. With several others also pursuing the idea of putting AI data centers in space, including Google and Blue Origin, this is the first approval the agency […]

articles.headline: India restricts Pakistani series on streaming platforms following regional tensions
articles.title: On what legal basis has government blocked a Pakistani series on Netflix? | Explained
articles.summary: Following the April 22, 2025 attack in Pahalgam that killed 26 individuals, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting directed Netflix and other streaming services on May 8 to remove Pakistan-origin productions. Industry bodies such as the All Indian Cine Workers Association and the Federation of Western India Cine Employees pressured authorities to enact the ban, citing national security rules under the Information Technology Act.
articles.description: Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo has drawn a warning from the government that Pakistani-origin content cannot be shown on Indian streaming platforms.

articles.headline: Trump’s tariff plan explained: Which countries could be hit and why?
articles.title: Trump’s tariff plan explained: Which countries could be hit and why?
articles.description: The Trump administration is preparing a fresh tariff offensive targeting major trading partners including China, India and the European Union. Here’s what the investigation is about and what it could mean for global trade.

articles.headline: Venezuela to repeal controversial law barring opposition from public office
articles.title: Venezuela to scrap law that bars opposition from public office
articles.summary: National Assembly speaker Jorge Rodríguez announced that Venezuela will repeal the Simón Bolívar Law, which previously banned opposition figures supporting foreign sanctions from holding public office. Rodríguez expects parliamentary approval next week following negotiations between interim President Delcy Rodríguez's government and opposition groups. The legislation was enacted after the disputed July 2024 election involving former President Nicolás Maduro, as authorities pursue a roadmap toward future democratic elections.
articles.description: The legislation has been criticised for enabling political persecution since it was introduced two years ago.

articles.headline: Iraq court rules federal government can take over Kurdish borders and oil fields
articles.title: Iraq’s top court rules government can take over Kurdish borders, oil fields
articles.summary: The Federal Supreme Court in Iraq ruled that federal forces can deploy to international borders in the Kurdish region and oversee oil fields. The decision supports Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi's efforts to curb oil smuggling and centralise state authority. Kurdish authorities condemned the ruling as an assault on constitutional rights, while analysts highlighted potential challenges in implementing these measures against armed factions.
articles.description: The ruling comes a day after Kurdish authorities accused Baghdad of an 'assault' on the region's constitutional rights.

articles.headline: Fitch Ratings states U.S. chip curbs will slow Asia data-centre investment
articles.title: U.S. chip curbs will slow Asia data-centre investment, Fitch says
articles.summary: Fitch Ratings announced that tighter U.S. semiconductor controls will slow Asia-Pacific data-centre investment and pressure operators reliant on Chinese clients and advanced chips. Effective November 19, the new rules require licenses for shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, and Thailand. This policy is expected to reshape the regional artificial intelligence boom, widen divides between physical owners and leveraged providers, and delay project financing.
articles.description: Fitch’s statement comes a day ​after S&P placed Nvidia’s rating on downgrade ⁠watch over governance concerns

articles.headline: FedEx plane overshoots runway at Miami International Airport
articles.title: Major Thanksgiving storm brings flooding, flight delays across US
articles.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration halted inbound flights and closed runways at Miami International Airport in Florida after a FedEx aircraft from Memphis overran a runway on Wednesday evening. Ground stops caused one-hour delays ahead of Thanksgiving, while the Miami-Dade area faced a flood watch due to heavy rain. No injuries were reported, and authorities are currently investigating the incident.
articles.description: Almost one million customers in the US had no power on Thursday evening as storms descended on both US coasts, bringing wind gusts, heavy rain and flooding.

articles.headline: RBI bulletin indicates continued broad-based pressure on food prices in November
articles.title: Broad-based pressure on food prices continues: RBI Bulletin
articles.summary: High-frequency data up to November 19 reveal persistent inflationary pressures on food items across India, according to a Reserve Bank of India report. Prices for cereals, pulses, and edible oils increased, while vegetable prices showed mixed trends. Officials noted that strong credit growth and robust export performance continue to support domestic economic resilience despite challenging global conditions and geopolitical risks.
articles.description: CPI inflation peaked to 6.1 % (y-o-y) in October 2026 from 5.5% in September 2026, slightly above the upper tolerance level of 6%–last observed in October 2024.

articles.headline: New Zealand’s Opportunity Party poised to become election kingmaker
articles.title: New Zealand’s Opportunity Party poised to become election kingmaker
