articles.description: The newly-elected Opportunity party is now in a position to swing New Zealand’s next parliament to the left or right.

articles.headline: Former U.S. Deputy Secretary of State Strobe Talbott dies at 80
articles.title: Strobe Talbott, former Time magazine reporter and Deputy Secretary of State, has died
articles.summary: Strobe Talbott, who served as United States Deputy Secretary of State under president Bill Clinton and led the Brookings Institution, died on November 26, 2026, at age 80. His son Devin Talbott confirmed the death in East Hampton, New York, following a long illness. The former journalist authored numerous books and shaped foreign policy toward Russia and India.
articles.description: While at the British university, after interning for Time in Moscow, the magazine asked Talbott to help translate the leaked memoirs of Nikita Khrushchev

articles.headline: Javokhir Sindarov acknowledges D Gukesh's superior preparation in Geneva
articles.title: World chess championship: Sindarov admits Gukesh out-prepared him in third game
articles.summary: Challenger Javokhir Sindarov stated he was out-prepared by defending champion D Gukesh during the third game of the World Chess Championship in Geneva. Following three consecutive draws in the fourteen-game match, Sindarov managed a tense endgame under severe time pressure, while Gukesh credited his coaching team for the effective opening strategy before the rest day.
articles.description: With the scores tied at 1.5-1.5 after three consecutive draws, Sindarov acknowledged that Gukesh, who was playing with Black pieces in Game 3, had caught him off guard with his preparation in the opening

articles.headline: Volatile organic compounds protect plants and provide environmental stress relief
articles.title: The changing scents of a warming world
articles.summary: Forests and gardens release volatile organic compounds, which are carbon-containing molecules that evaporate easily at normal temperatures. Conifers, sal trees, and curry leaf trees produce these compounds to deter pests, combat pathogens, and provide relief from heat and drought stress. Certain variants also act as chemical warning signals between plants or exhibit antibacterial properties against infections.
articles.description: Be it in a forest or among the flowers in a garden, the air is enriched in volatile organic compounds, whose profiles climate change is beginning to alter

articles.headline: Estonia closing land borders with Russia to keep out spies
articles.title: Estonia closing land borders with Russia to keep out spies
articles.description: Estonia is set to close its land border crossings to Russia by December 1.

articles.headline: Cargo ship sinks off northern Cuba leaving one sailor dead
articles.title: One dead, three missing after cargo ship sinks off Cuba
articles.summary: A Panama-flagged cargo vessel named the Halima sank off the northern coast of Cuba near Cabanas Bay in Artemisa province on November 26, 2026, according to the Cuban Maritime Administration. Operated by the Turkish company Sidra Line, the ship carried sixteen crew members, resulting in one confirmed fatality and three missing sailors as search operations continued.
articles.description: The Halima, operated by Turkish company Sidra Line and carrying 208 containers, sank early on November 26 near Cabanas Bay in Artemisa province

articles.headline: Mumbai police link jewellery store firing to ten crore rupee extortion demand
articles.title: ‘Even Z-Plus cover won’t save you’: Mumbai jewellery store firing linked to ₹10cr extortion demand
articles.summary: Police in Mumbai reported that a shooting at PC Jain Jewellers in Mahim on November 25, 2026, was linked to a ten crore rupee extortion demand. Shop owner Bharat Jain received multiple threatening WhatsApp messages ignoring them as spam. Authorities are analyzing CCTV footage to trace the two helmeted assailants who fled toward Bandra.
articles.description: Two motorcycle-borne individuals wearing helmets fired three rounds at the store of PC Jain Jewellers in Mahim before fleeing towards Bandra. No one was hurt in the firing

articles.headline: Defence ministry reports thirteen soldiers killed in Niger compound attack
articles.title: At least 13 Niger soldiers killed in Sanam armed attack
articles.summary: Thirteen members of Niger's National Guard were killed and twenty wounded during an assault on their compound in Sanam on November 27, 2026. The Defence Ministry stated that numerous heavily armed assailants carried out the raid in the Tillaberi region near the Mali border. Operations to track down the attackers remain ongoing.
articles.description: It remains unclear who carried out the attack on Niger's National Guard in Tillaberi, near the Mali border.

articles.headline: Meta faces safety concerns over its School Partnership Programme
articles.title: Why is Meta’s Project Gryffindor facing backlash? | Explained
articles.summary: According to a report by news outlet NPR, Meta’s internal School Partnership Programme, known as Project Gryffindor, is facing safety concerns and backlash from experts. Introduced in March 2025, the initiative was designed to help educators and parents report teen safety issues and bullying directly to the social media company through a specialized feature that prioritized academic institution reports.
articles.description: Meta’s initiative to bring more school-going teens to Instagram, nicknamed “Project Gryffindor,” is facing flak from experts, reported the NPR outlet

articles.headline: Jerusalem Daily: Israel kills Hamas’s Gaza security chief
articles.title: Jerusalem Daily: Israel kills Hamas’s Gaza security chief
articles.description: Israel assassinated Hamas’s internal security chief in Gaza City, killing him and six others in a strike

articles.headline: Apple removes MiniMax chatbot Talkie from App Store worldwide
articles.title: Apple pulls MiniMax AI chatbot from App Store over child safety concerns
articles.summary: Apple removed the Talkie chatbot app, developed by Shanghai-based MiniMax, from its global App Store following media reports that artificial intelligence characters sent sexualized messages to minors. The application has an 18+ rating but faced criticism for lax age verification safeguards. Child safety advocates highlighted the risks, while the company and Apple did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
articles.description: China cracked down on domestic AI companion apps including Xingye, banning intimate ⁠relationships for minors and ordering platforms to develop strict guardrails

articles.headline: India records lowest net foreign direct investment in over five years during September
articles.title: Net FDI fell to more than 5.5-year low in September 2026, as outflows jumped 40%
articles.summary: Net foreign direct investment into India dropped to negative 4.95 billion dollars in September 2026, marking the lowest level since at least March 2021. Reserve Bank of India data indicates the decline stemmed from a drop in gross inflows to 5.9 billion dollars alongside a surge in outward investments and profit repatriations by foreign companies totaling 10.8 billion dollars.
articles.description: Despite September’s performance, net FDI in the first half of the financial year was more than 20% higher than in the same period last year

articles.headline: New Zealand ruling coalition falls short of majority in official tally
articles.title: New Zealand's ruling coalition falls short of parliamentary majority by one seat
articles.summary: Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's National Party and its coalition partners secured 65 seats, missing a parliamentary majority by one seat according to official results released on Friday. The incumbent administration now requires backing from the centrist Opportunity Party to maintain governance. Disillusioned voters facing economic struggles influenced the electoral outcome, which saw major parties shift seats following overseas and special vote counts.
articles.description: The right-leaning ruling bloc led by the National Party has fallen short of the majority needed to govern.

articles.headline: Ukraine reports five Russian military jets damaged in strike on Savasleyka airfield
articles.title: Five Russian military jets hit in airfield strike, says Ukraine
articles.summary: Kyiv's General Staff stated that three MiG-31 and two Su-34 aircraft were damaged during a drone strike on the Savasleyka airfield located 300 kilometres east of Moscow. Russian officials have not commented on the airfield attack, which follows separate overnight strikes on oil refineries in the Samara region that left one person dead, according to regional governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev.
articles.description: The Savasleyka airfield hosts aircraft used by Russia to launch hypersonic missiles and glide bombs at Ukraine.

articles.headline: Congress accuses government of stalling court hearings on island project
articles.title: Government has ‘clear strategy’ to stall court proceedings against GNI project: Jairam Ramesh
articles.summary: On November 26, 2026, Congress leader Jairam Ramesh accused the federal government of using a clear strategy to delay Calcutta High Court proceedings regarding forest land diversion on the Great Nicobar Island. The hearings were deferred to January 13, 2027, after the administration sought more time to file affidavits. Ramesh criticised the Andaman and Nicobar administration for inviting tenders to demarcate the project area while legal challenges remain ongoing.
articles.description: Congress leader says the project continues to be “bulldozed through”, citing how the Andaman and Nicobar administration has issued a tender inviting bids to demarcate the 166.1 sq km area earmarked for the project

articles.headline: CPI announces three-day protest over political demands
articles.title: CPI announces three-day ‘Jail Bharo Andolan’ from December 1
articles.summary: Communist Party of India general secretary D. Raja announced a three-day Jail Bharo Andolan starting December 1, 2026. Speaking in New Delhi, he demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, the implementation of women's reservations, and a legal guarantee for farmers' minimum support prices. Raja also urged secular democratic forces to unite against the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party.
articles.description: Demands include CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation, implementation of women’s quota, and legal MSP guarantee for farmers

articles.headline: Israeli air strike kills senior Hamas security official in Gaza City
articles.title: Israeli strike kills senior Hamas security official and family in Gaza City
articles.summary: An Israeli air strike in the Gaza Strip killed Mohammed Abu al-Ouf, a senior Hamas internal security official, along with three members of his family at dawn. The military described the target as a terrorist. The attack caused extensive damage in Shati refugee camp, drawing strong condemnation from the Hamas-run interior ministry amid ongoing conflict.
articles.description: Mohammed Abu al-Ouf, head of Hamas's internal security service in northern Gaza, was killed with his wife and two teenage daughters, doctors say.

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu government introduces paternity leave for married male employees
articles.title: Tamil Nadu introduces 15 days of paternity leave for married government employees
articles.summary: Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay announced a 15-day paid paternity leave policy for married male state government employees with fewer than three surviving children. According to an official release issued on Thursday, the leave can be taken before birth or within six months afterward to encourage shared childcare responsibilities. Medical professionals and employee associations welcomed the decision, which complements the existing 365 days of maternity leave.
articles.description: The paternity leave can be availed by male employees either 15 days before the birth of the child or within six months from the date of birth.

articles.headline: Udhayanidhi Stalin urges Tamil Nadu Governor for CBI probe
articles.title: Udhayanidhi Stalin meets Tamil Nadu Governor, seeks CBI inquiry against Kallakurichi MLA
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu opposition leader Udhayanidhi Stalin submitted a memorandum to Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar in Chennai, demanding a Central Bureau of Investigation probe against a ruling-party MLA accused of misbehaving with a woman officer. He also called for a comprehensive report on the law and order situation and stricter child safety measures.
articles.description: Udhayanidhi also called for preserving all digital evidence and transfer the case to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) for an independent and time-bound investigation

articles.headline: Indian stock indices and rupee surge amid foreign capital inflows
articles.title: Stock indices gain 1.85%, rupee surges to 8-month high aided by foreign inflows, low crude prices
articles.summary: Benchmark equity indices on November 25, 2026, recorded a significant gain of 1.85 percent backed by fresh large-cap buying and easing Brent crude oil prices below $90 a barrel. Simultaneously, the Indian rupee surged to an eight-month high against the dollar, reaching 92.23 in the interbank market. Analysts attributed the positive financial momentum to robust foreign portfolio investor inflows and improved domestic market liquidity.
articles.description: Investors' wealth went up by ₹3.49 lakh crore to ₹5,12,48,042.08 crore (USD 5.54 trillion) on November 25

articles.headline: Trump says the US has ‘close to 50%’ of world’s oil
articles.title: Trump says the US has ‘close to 50%’ of world’s oil
articles.description: On a call to soldiers deployed to the Gulf, Donald Trump claimed that the US does not ‘need Middle East oil'.

articles.headline: Department of Science and Technology secretary highlights future data storage technologies
articles.title: DNA could transform data storage, says DST Secretary
articles.summary: During the 39th Foundation Day celebrations of the Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology on Thursday, Department of Science and Technology Secretary Umesh Waghmare stated that DNA could transform data storage methods. He emphasized that interdisciplinary research combining physics, biology, and artificial intelligence drives modern innovation. CCMB Director Vinay K. Nandicoori also noted the institute's ongoing commitment to advancements in health, agriculture, and biodiversity conservation.
articles.description: We are generating nearly a billion terabytes of data every year, and DNA can change the way we store this data,’Umesh Waghmare said

articles.headline: Bangladesh tightens border security and deploys paramilitary forces
articles.title: Bangladesh tightens border security ahead of Hasina's planned return; deploys 108 BGB platoons
articles.summary: Bangladesh deployed 108 platoons of border paramilitary forces across seven districts to maintain order amid rising political tensions and violence surrounding the planned return of exiled former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. Authorities increased surveillance and patrols following incidents of arson and clashes linked to the banned Awami League party ahead of December.
articles.description: The heightened security comes amid fears that Ms. Hasina's supporters could intensify violence and sabotage in the coming days. Awami League, whose activities have been banned, is promoting a lockdown programme for November 29 and 30 through online platforms, adding to concerns over a possible escalation of tensions

articles.headline: Agence France-Presse shuts down content platform following overnight cyberattack
articles.title: Global news agency AFP reports cyberattack, shuts down content platform
articles.summary: The France-based international news agency Agence France-Presse experienced a cyberattack that forced its AFP Forum content platform offline on Thursday. Management reported the intrusion started at 1:30 am Paris time, prompting teams to take immediate precautionary measures while offering backup solutions to subscribers. The incident coincides with warnings from cybersecurity chief Vincent Strubel regarding unprecedented threat levels across Europe.
articles.description: France's cybersecurity chief urges collective action to combat unprecedented threat levels in the nation.

articles.headline: Solomon Islands signs security treaty with Australia
articles.title: Solomon Islands signs security deal with Australia
articles.summary: The Solomon Islands and Australia signed a security treaty on Wednesday prohibiting foreign military bases on the island nation. Australia will provide 740 million Australian dollars over ten years to support infrastructure and education. The agreement requires the Solomon Islands to consult Canberra on critical infrastructure deals, marking a shift away from recent Chinese influence.
articles.description: Solomon Islands will have to consult Canberra before making new security or infrastructure deals under new pact.

articles.headline: Kenyan man wrongly convicted of attack on British couple sues Met Police
articles.title: Met Police ruined my life, says Kenyan man wrongly convicted over attack on UK couple
articles.summary: Ali Kololo spent over a decade in prison after being wrongly convicted and sentenced to death following a 2011 attack on a British couple in Kenya. Kololo is now suing London's Metropolitan Police, alleging a senior officer gave misleading evidence and acted unlawfully. Kenya's High Court quashed the conviction in April 2023, while the Met is challenging compensation in court.
articles.description: Evidence from a British police officer helped convict Ali Kololo over a 2011 attack in the Kenyan resort of Lamu.

articles.headline: America’s Thanksgiving holiday seen through different eyes
articles.title: America’s Thanksgiving holiday seen through different eyes
articles.description: As millions of Americans celebrate Thanksgiving, Indigenous people gather in Plymouth for the National Day of Mourning.

articles.headline: Leaked Russian statistics reveal nearly 500,000 military fatalities
articles.title: Russia's own figures show it has lost nearly 500,000 people in Ukraine war
articles.summary: Leaked official data from Russia's statistics agency Rosstat, analysed by the BBC and independent outlet Mediazona following a cyber-attack, indicates that at least 490,334 Russian soldiers have died since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine began in 2022. The records demonstrate severe casualties among young adults and specific military units, far exceeding figures acknowledged publicly by Moscow while aligning with open-source tracking efforts.
articles.description: Leaked data reveal how the full-scale invasion of Ukraine has fundamentally changed mortality patterns in Russia.

articles.headline: Russian air strikes across Ukraine kill five and damage energy infrastructure
articles.title: Russian strikes on Ukraine kill five, cause power outages in five regions
articles.summary: Russian military strikes across multiple Ukrainian regions killed at least five people, injured dozens, and severely damaged essential energy facilities, according to local authorities. The attacks caused widespread power outages in Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zaporizhia, Odesa, and Kharkiv. Furthermore, the Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant temporarily lost external power following shelling, forcing it to switch to diesel generators during the ongoing conflict.
articles.description: A Ukrainian official says attacks on Zaporizhia and Dnipropetrovsk regions damaged a number of energy sites.

articles.headline: Rapid Support Forces drone attacks kill nineteen people in Sudan
articles.title: Sudan’s RSF kills at least 19 in drone attacks on Blue Nile state
articles.summary: At least 19 individuals were killed and 20 others wounded after paramilitary Rapid Support Forces launched overnight drone strikes targeting Damazin, the capital of Sudan's Blue Nile state. A rights group and military sources reported that the bombardment hit residential areas, electricity infrastructure, and a nearby dam. This violence forms part of the ongoing civil war between Sudanese military factions that began in April 2023.
articles.description: The attacks on Blue Nile state also wounded at least 20 people – in a drone war that is quickly escalating.

articles.headline: After Brexit, is Britain heading back to the EU?
articles.title: After Brexit, is Britain heading back to the EU?
articles.description: A decade after the Brexit vote, a new deal brings Britain and the EU closer, with economic gains for both sides.

articles.headline: Georgian police clash with Besiktas fans over Palestinian flag during match
articles.title: Georgian police clash with Turkiye’s Besiktas fans over Palestinian flag
articles.summary: Georgian police clashed with fans of Turkish club Besiktas after a Palestinian flag was unfurled during a Europa League game against Hapoel Beer-Sheva in Batumi on Thursday. The incident caused a thirty-minute match suspension after officers reportedly used pepper spray in the stands. Besiktas and the Turkish Football Federation condemned the security forces for using disproportionate force during the event.
articles.description: Match between Besiktas and Hapoel Beer-Sheva suspended for 30 minutes after confrontation between fans and police.

articles.headline: Israeli air strike kills senior Hamas security official in Gaza
articles.title: Israeli strike in Gaza kills senior Hamas official, his wife and children
articles.summary: An Israeli military air attack in the Gaza Strip killed Muhammad Majid Abu al-Awf, the director of the Internal Security Service in northern Gaza, along with his wife and two daughters. The enclave's Ministry of Interior stated that the strike targeted their residence in the Shati refugee camp. This incident occurred shortly after the killing of another senior security official amid continuing violence in the region.
articles.description: Gaza's internal security director and his family are among seven Palestinians killed by Israeli forces on Wednesday.

articles.headline: My dad's watch stopped the moment he died - I found it in the ashes of Hong Kong tower fire
articles.title: My dad's watch stopped the moment he died - I found it in the ashes of Hong Kong tower fire
articles.description: The city marks a year since a huge blaze tore through seven apartment blocks, killing 168 people.

articles.headline: Clashes erupt at Besiktas football match in Georgia over banner
articles.title: Clashes at Besiktas match against Israeli club spark diplomatic row
articles.summary: Turkish football club Besiktas supporters clashed with police in Batumi during a UEFA Europa League fixture against Hapoel Beer-Sheva after displaying a pro-Palestinian banner, resulting in sixteen detentions and three injured officers. Georgia's Interior Ministry denied using disproportionate force during the incident, prompting Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan to contact his Georgian counterpart regarding citizen safety.
articles.description: Turkish football fans clashed with police in Batumi, temporarily halting the match, which had been moved from Istanbul over security concerns

articles.headline: Canada Supreme Court to rule on Quebec religious symbols ban
articles.title: In Canada, Quebec’s religious symbols ban faces a Supreme Court test
articles.summary: Canada's Supreme Court is ruling on a legal challenge against Quebec's legislation restricting religious symbols for public employees, a law that has deeply affected Muslim women and prompted families like Navien Waly to face severe professional and social hurdles. The controversial policy, rooted in the province's secularism debate, has triggered widespread concern over civil rights and discrimination across the region.
articles.description: Canada’s top court weighs Bill 21, the Quebec law that shapes where Muslim women can work and where they feel welcome.

articles.headline: Huawei found guilty of trade secrets conspiracy and bank fraud in U.S.
articles.title: Huawei found guilty of stealing US trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
articles.summary: Following a two-month trial in a Brooklyn court, a United States jury found Chinese technology firm Huawei guilty of ten out of twelve counts, including conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud. Jurors acquitted the company of an overarching racketeering charge. Defence attorney Brian Heberlig announced that Huawei plans to appeal the convictions following the sentencing scheduled for September 2027.
articles.description: The verdict follows a months-long trial in New York.

articles.headline: Chinese Communist Party investigates Shanghai party secretary Chen Jining
articles.title: Who is Chen Jining, China’s latest Politburo member under investigation?
articles.summary: The Chinese Communist Party launched an anticorruption probe into Shanghai secretary Chen Jining for alleged serious violations of discipline and law. Announced by the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection, the investigation makes Chen the fourth high-ranking Political Bureau member to be ousted in two years. President Xi Jinping's ongoing purge aims to enforce strict party discipline ahead of the upcoming congress.
articles.description: Chen is the fourth high-ranking Politburo member to be pushed out in two years.

articles.headline: Congress president urges alliance unity to remove BJP in Uttar Pradesh
articles.title: Leave aside any differences, remove BJP in U.P., says Congress chief
articles.summary: Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge called upon party workers in Lucknow to strengthen the Samajwadi Party and Congress alliance and discard differences to defeat the Bharatiya Janata Party in Uttar Pradesh. Addressing a Constitution Day event, Kharge criticised ruling leaders over voting rights and the judiciary, while local police temporarily detained several party members during a subsequent protest march.
articles.description: ‘To win, we all have to fight together and leave aside egoistic talk; we have to strengthen the alliance and remove Modi-Yogi from power,’ said Mallikarjun Kharge

articles.headline: Delhi High Court sets aside cancellation of NGO foreign funding licence
articles.title: Delhi HC sets aside Centre’s order cancelling FCRA licence of NGO
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court nullified a central government order that cancelled the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act registration of the Socio Legal Information Centre, ruling that allegations of aggressive political activism lacked supporting evidence. Justice A.J. Bhambhani stated that the organisation deployed funds in accordance with its legal-aid objectives and described the 2022 Ministry of Home Affairs cancellation order as untenable and illegal.
articles.description: ‘Based on the record, this court is unable to discern any material based on which it could be said that the appellant’s activities would likely prejudicially affect the sovereignty, integrity, or security of India or public interest,’ Justice A.J. Bhambhani said

articles.headline: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot attempts to form coalition government
articles.title: Could Netanyahu take Israel into another war with Iran to cling to power?
articles.summary: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot is working to assemble a coalition government to avert potential political maneuvers by interim Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu regarding Iran. Eisenkot currently lacks a majority in the 120-seat Knesset. Intelligence officials and analysts dispute claims of an imminent military threat from Tehran, suggesting any new conflict could be politically motivated to delay ongoing leadership negotiations.
articles.description: As Israeli opposition leader Eisenkot moves to form a government, could war with Iran derail talks and save Netanyahu?

articles.headline: Leaked documents reveal FIFA considered 96-year private equity deal
articles.title: Leaked FIFA documents show Infantino’s 96-year private equity plan for World Cup
articles.summary: Leaked documents reviewed by The Associated Press show FIFA president Gianni Infantino planned to sell stakes in the World Cup for 96 years through a for-profit subsidiary named FIFA Forward Enterprises. The secretive project, developed with Joshua Kushner's firm Thrive Capital, collapsed following a global backlash. Infantino now faces his first presidential election challenge ahead of a March vote in Morocco.
articles.description: The leaked documents, including a FIFA in-house risk assessment, show its own finance officials “were not directly privy to the construction of this transaction”

articles.headline: Trump administration prepares new tariffs following excess industrial capacity probe
articles.title: U.S. set to slap tariffs on China, EU and others after probe on excess industrial capacity: report
articles.summary: The United States administration is set to release findings from a Section 301 investigation concerning excess industrial capacity across sixteen trading partners, with new import duties expected. According to sources, the proposed levies will stack on previous tariffs and replace measures struck down by the Supreme Court in February. The probe covers major economies including the European Union, China, and India.
articles.description: India was also named among 16 ⁠major U.S. trading partners; Together, the duties are meant to ​rebuild Trump’s global “Liberation Day” tariffs that were struck down by the U.S. Supreme Court in February

articles.headline: United States intelligence agency may have waterboarded more detainees than admitted
articles.title: Report: CIA tortured more people with waterboarding than US agency admitted
articles.summary: Newly obtained documents from a federal probe suggest the United States Central Intelligence Agency subjected more individuals to waterboarding than previously acknowledged. The New York Times secured redacted investigative files detailing a 2012 interview where a translator observed an unconfirmed incident in Afghanistan. The Central Intelligence Agency historically admitted to waterboarding only three detainees during post-September 11 interrogations.
articles.description: A New York Times report lends credence to long-held belief that torture method was more widely used than acknowledged.

articles.headline: Diesel tanker carrying thousands of tonnes sinks near Ibiza killing one
articles.title: Diesel tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes capsizes near Ibiza, killing one
articles.summary: A Malta flagged chemical tanker named Med Emre sank twenty five nautical miles from Ibiza while carrying up to 7,000 tonnes of diesel. Balearic Islands emergency services confirmed that seventeen crew members were rescued, but one later died after hospitalisation. Authorities and Spain are assessing potential environmental impacts following the vessel incident which occurred while travelling toward Barcelona.
articles.description: The possible environmental damage is still being assessed by Spain's sea rescue service.

articles.headline: COP31 climate conference concludes in Antalya without a cover decision
articles.title: COP31 and the unmet promises of climate action
articles.summary: The 31st Conference of the Parties in Antalya, Türkiye, ended two days behind schedule without reaching a final cover decision due to disagreements over naming fossil fuels. The summit highlighted an ongoing inability to operationalize previous commitments from Baku and Belém. According to the Global Carbon Budget 2025, current emission trajectories risk exhausting the carbon budget for 1.5 degrees celsius warming within four years.
articles.description: COP31 has once again laid out the gap between what countries promise and what they are actually prepared to do. With the window to keep warming below 1.5 degrees rapidly closing, the coming year should be spent on fixing what is broken

articles.headline: Flipkart chief executive Kalyan Krishnamurthy to step down
articles.title: Kalyan Krishnamurthy to step down as Flipkart CEO
articles.summary: Flipkart announced that Chief Executive Officer Kalyan Krishnamurthy will step down after more than eleven years with the Bengaluru-based e-commerce firm. Walmart International President Chris Nicholas credited Krishnamurthy with driving rapid expansion and scaling flagship events. Chief Product and Technology Officer Balaji Thiagarajan and the board will oversee operations until a successor is named in the coming weeks.
articles.description: In the interim, Chief Product and Technology Officer Balaji Thiagarajan and the Flipkart board will oversee operations

articles.headline: Egyptian prosecutors detain driver following Cairo fuel tanker fire tragedy
articles.title: Egypt detains driver over Cairo fuel tanker fire that killed 31
articles.summary: Egyptian authorities ordered the detention of a 21-year-old driver suspected of causing a collision that overturned a fuel tanker on Cairo's ring road, sparking a massive fire that killed 31 people on Wednesday. The Ministry of Health and Population confirmed the final death toll alongside dozens of injuries, prompting officials to pledge medical care and financial support for affected families.
articles.description: Prosecutors order drug tests for the 21-year-old suspect, who says he was overtaking when the crash happened.

articles.headline: Bangladesh garment workers clash with police over low wages
articles.title: Bangladesh garment workers clash with police over low wages
articles.description: Bangladeshi garment workers clashed with police after a 36% minimum wage increase fell short of their demands.

articles.headline: Mexico seeks talks with United States over SpaceX rocket debris
articles.title: Mexico seeks US talks about suspected SpaceX debris
articles.summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum announced on Thursday that the government is requesting bilateral discussions with United States aviation authorities regarding airspace permissions and rocket debris following recent SpaceX launches in Texas. Material from a Starship launch washed ashore in Tamaulipas, prompting environmental protection agency PROFEPA to collect the debris while SpaceX disputed its origin.
articles.description: Mexico concerned as SpaceX ramps up rocket launches from Starbase near border in Texas.

articles.headline: Saudi air defences intercept Houthi drones following strike on Hodeidah
articles.title: Saudi-led coalition intercepts Houthi attacks after Hodeidah strike
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia reported that its air defense systems intercepted multiple drones over Ras Tanura and the Eastern province on Wednesday morning. According to coalition spokesman Turki Al-Maliki, the action followed a Saudi-led coalition air strike on the rebel-held Yemeni port city of Hodeidah. The escalation comes amid rising tensions and mutual attacks targeting strategic regional infrastructure.
articles.description: The escalation comes after the Yemeni rebel group threatened to attack the kingdom's Red Sea ports in retaliation.

articles.headline: Elon Musk pledges SpaceX shares for every child in America
articles.title: Musk pledges two SpaceX shares for every US child
articles.summary: Elon Musk announced plans to gift two SpaceX shares valued at approximately eighteen billion dollars to every child in the United States, following regulatory approval to deploy one million satellites. The initiative aims to broaden public participation in the space economy, though astronomers warned the satellite constellation would harm astronomical research facilities.
articles.description: US children would receive one share from SpaceX and one from him personally, Musk said.

articles.headline: Pakistan launches its first astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali to space station
articles.title: From stargazing to space: Pakistan watches its first astronaut take flight
articles.summary: Muhammad Zeeshan Ali became Pakistan's first astronaut after lifting off on a Chinese rocket from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre on Wednesday morning. Crowds watched the historic launch live in Islamabad at the headquarters of the Pakistan Space & Upper Atmosphere Research Commission. The spacecraft successfully docked at China's Tiangong space station hours later as part of a joint mission.
articles.description: Students and stargazers packed SUPARCO's auditorium before dawn to watch Zeeshan Ali reach orbit on a Chinese rocket.

articles.headline: Bomb threats target municipal headquarters and court in Maharashtra
articles.title: Bomb threats to BMC, NMMC headquarters and Belapur court trigger security checks
articles.summary: Authorities in Maharashtra launched security checks and evacuations on November 26, 2026, after receiving bomb threats via email at the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation headquarters, Navi Mumbai Municipal Corporation headquarters, and Belapur court. Deputy Commissioner of Police Maneesh Kalwaniya stated that nothing suspicious was found, while police suspect the threats may be the work of a mischief-maker.
articles.description: Threat email reportedly names Diljit Dosanjh’s upcoming concert and Amitabh Bachchan’s residence among targets; police find nothing suspicious at BMC

articles.headline: Gukesh and Sindarov draw third game at World Chess Championship
articles.title: World Chess Championship: Nothing to separate Gukesh, Sindarov after three games
articles.summary: Indian player D. Gukesh and Uzbek opponent Javokhir Sindarov played out a draw in the third game of the World Championship match in Geneva. The encounter lasted sixty moves over nearly five hours, resulting in a 1.5-1.5 score after three consecutive draws ahead of the rest day on November 27, 2026.
articles.description: The Uzbek Grandmaster overcomes time trouble to eke out a draw; the reigning champion’s Rio variation catches the challenger off guard; after a long battle, the players head for first breather

articles.headline: United States trade representative announces new tariffs amid anticipated international negotiations
articles.title: Faisal Islam: Why Trump's new tariffs are less of a threat
articles.summary: United States Trade Representative Jamieson Greer announced new tariff measures on Thursday following months of hearings and consultations. The duties aim to address excess industrial capacity and replace previous rules struck down by the Supreme Court. While global trade flows have adapted significantly since previous measures, the upcoming legislative battles in Congress and negotiations at the Miami resort summit will determine the long-term impact of these policies.
articles.description: Other countries have rerouted trade in response to his first tariff salvo, now they are looking beyond Trump's tenure.

articles.headline: Madras High Court praises Tamil Nadu police for tracing missing persons
articles.title: Madras High Court commends Tamil Nadu police for tracing 2,510 missing persons within a fortnight
articles.summary: The Madras High Court commended the Tamil Nadu police on November 26, 2026, for successfully tracing 2,510 missing individuals during a two-week special drive conducted between October 30 and November 13. Justices A.D. Jagadish Chandira and B. Karthikeyan recorded their appreciation while hearing a habeas corpus petition in Chennai.
articles.description: Justices A.D. Jagadish Chandira and B. Karthikeyan record their appreciation for a special drive conducted by the police to trace missing men, women, boys and girls

articles.headline: Experts discuss census challenges and methodology during book launch
articles.title: Experts examine key aspects, challenges of conducting Census
articles.summary: Former Registrar General and Census Commissioner C. Chandramouli and law professor Vinay Sitapati discussed enumeration challenges, caste census legislation, and technology adoption during a book launch event organised by the Chennai International Centre in Chennai on November 26, 2026.

articles.headline: Supreme Court schedules contempt petitions hearing over Thirupparankundram lamp-lighting
articles.title: Thirupparankundram ‘deepathoon’ row: Supreme Court agrees to list plea to detail Vijay’s role
articles.summary: The Supreme Court allowed the listing of a contempt petition on November 27, 2026, concerning the failure to light the Karthigai Deepam at the Thirupparankundram Hill summit. Filed by Rama Ravikumar, the plea seeks an affidavit from the Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary regarding compliance with a November 20 court order. Hindu parties argue that state authorities and temple trustees failed to properly execute the ceremonial lighting ceremony.
articles.description: The application said the four Sthanikars had denied giving any opinion to light the lamp at the Deepa Mandapam nor were they consulted

articles.headline: Microsoft declares emergency overhaul following historic global technical outage
articles.title: Microsoft declares ‘Code Red’ after historic outage, internal memos show
articles.summary: Microsoft Corporation declared a severe emergency alert to fix engineering vulnerabilities after a major November outage disrupted global services including Exchange Online and Teams. According to internal company memos reviewed by Reuters, executives cited fragmented diagnostic data and slow patch deployments. Leadership established five new workstreams and set a resolution target of one hour for future incidents.
articles.description: The November 12-13 outage ​hit governments from Australia and Japan to the United States, delayed trading firms ⁠and disrupted airline communications, fueling broader concerns about the vulnerability of critical digital infrastructure

articles.headline: Watch: Roofs torn off and streets under water as severe weather hits US
articles.title: Watch: Roofs torn off and streets under water as severe weather hits US
articles.description: Hundreds of thousands have been affected by storms in the country as the Thanksgiving holiday weekend begins.

articles.headline: Two Indian nationals injured in Houthi militia attack in Riyadh
articles.title: At least two Indians among 11 injured in Houthi attack in Riyadh; New Delhi condemns strike
articles.summary: Two Indian citizens and three Nepalese nationals were among eleven people injured on November 24, 2026, when Yemen's Houthi militia targeted a tower in the Saudi capital of Riyadh. Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence described the incident in the King Abdullah Financial District as a terrorist attack. The Indian embassy confirmed the injuries and stated that assistance is being provided.
articles.description: Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence said a tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District came under what it described as a "terrorist attack" by Houthi militia

articles.headline: Protesters gather in Zagreb following psychiatric care abuse scandals
articles.title: Psychiatric care under scrutiny after abuse scandals in Croatia and Bosnia
articles.summary: Thousands gathered in Zagreb on Saturday to protest following abuse scandals in Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina that led to thirteen healthcare worker arrests and institutional head resignations. Demonstrators carried pillows marked with bloody handprints in memory of Kristian Josip Peris, who died after staff allegedly restrained him improperly.
articles.description: Persistent failures in psychiatric care have been exposed, including staff shortages, poor training and weak oversight.

articles.headline: Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali docks at Chinese space station
articles.title: Pakistan rejoices as country’s first astronaut enters orbit
articles.summary: Muhammad Zeeshan Ali docked at China's Tiangong space station on Wednesday, becoming the first Pakistani in orbit and the first foreign astronaut aboard the facility. Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif praised the milestone as proof of bilateral friendship. Ali will spend up to ten days on the station during the joint crewed mission aimed at expanding international research.
articles.description: Zeeshan Ali makes history as the first foreign national to board China's space station

articles.headline: Landmine casualties rise globally as the international ban faces withdrawals
articles.title: Why are landmine casualties rising as the global ban comes under threat? | Explained
articles.summary: Landmines and unexploded ordnance killed or injured more individuals in 2025 than in any year since 2020, according to the annual Landmine Monitor report released by the International Campaign to Ban Landmines. Published on November 25, 2026, the findings coincide with the Mine Ban Treaty experiencing its first-ever withdrawals since coming into force on March 1, 1999.
articles.description: Why is the Mine Ban Treaty facing a crisis? Why are more civilians falling victim to landmines? Are countries turning away from the landmine ban?

articles.headline: Medical interns appear before Kolkata Police amid ongoing campus protests
articles.title: Medical interns appear before Kolkata Police, others students join the march
articles.summary: Three medical interns from Medical College, Kolkata appeared before Kolkata Police on November 26, 2026, following police summons. Supported by hundreds of students and senior doctors marching to Bowbazar Police Station, the interns faced questioning after receiving show-cause notices for speaking to media about hospital mismanagement during an October stampede.
articles.description: An FIR registered at Bowbazar police station against medical interns; junior doctors and interns had staged a demonstration outside the principal’s office at Medical College Kolkata until late on November 18, demanding the withdrawal of show-cause notices issued to eight interns a day earlier

articles.headline: Union home secretary and intelligence director review security in Jammu
articles.title: Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, IB Director meet top security officials in Jammu
articles.summary: Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan and Intelligence Bureau Director Mahesh Dixit convened a high-level security assessment in Jammu on November 26, 2026. The discussions involved senior leadership from the police, Army, and paramilitary forces. This high-profile visit follows the recent killing of local Lashkar-e-Taiba recruit Lateef Bhat in Kulgam district and ongoing anti-terror operations in the Kishtwar region after two officers were found dead.
articles.description: The top security officials of the country met senior officials of the police, Army, paramilitary and different wings of the intelligence and security agencies

articles.headline: India warns against technology weaponisation and urges inclusive governance
articles.title: India warns against using tech for strategic one-upmanship, calls for inclusive AI governance
articles.summary: India cautioned the United Nations Security Council against using technology for strategic one-upmanship during a high-level open debate on conflict resolution. Permanent Representative Harish Parvathaneni emphasized that artificial intelligence must remain human-centric and called for inclusive international cooperation. United Nations Secretary General Antonio Guterres also voiced serious concerns regarding algorithmic targeting in modern warfare.
articles.description: India’s UN Ambassador asserted that amid the rapid integration of AI into military and intelligence spheres, responsibility for the use of lethal autonomous weapons systems must always rest with humans

articles.headline: China launches Shenzhou-24 flight carrying first foreign astronaut to Tiangong
articles.title: China launches crewed spaceship carrying first Pakistani astronaut to its space station
articles.summary: China launched its Shenzhou-24 space mission on November 25, 2026, from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre, carrying a three-person crew that includes the first foreign astronaut to board the Tiangong space station. Zeeshan Ali, a forty-year-old pilot from Pakistan, will spend five to ten days conducting experiments alongside Chinese commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer Wu Yi.
articles.description: Using a Long March-2F rocket, the spacecraft took ‌off at 8:18 a.m. (0018 GMT) ‌from ⁠the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre ⁠in northwest China

articles.headline: Guinea-Bissau military leaders delay presidential election
articles.title: Guinea-Bissau military leaders delay presidential election until 2028
articles.summary: Transitional president Major-General Horta Inta-a issued a decree on November 27, 2026, postponing presidential and legislative votes by two years to November 2028. The military government, which seized power in November 2025 by overthrowing Umaro Sissoco Embalo, cited insufficient technical, material, and financial conditions. Regional bloc ECOWAS had urged a transparent transition back to civilian rule for the nation.
articles.description: Military leaders say presidential and legislative poll scheduled for December 6 will now take place in November 2028.

articles.headline: Nitin Gadkari allocates one lakh crore rupees for West Bengal roads
articles.title: West Bengal roads will be like America in five years says Nitin Gadkari, announces infrastructure projects worth ₹1 lakh crore
articles.summary: Union Minister Nitin Gadkari announced infrastructure funding on November 26, 2026, during an event in Kolaghat alongside Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari. The central allocation aims to improve regional connectivity across the state and includes fourteen thousand rupees for the Kolkata ring road. The state government promised full cooperation regarding land acquisition and regulatory clearances to facilitate timely execution.
articles.description: Among the major announcements was the construction of a ₹ 14,000-crore Kolkata Ring Road that will ease traffic congestions in Kolkata

articles.headline: Cockroach Janta Party holds Nagpur constitution rally
articles.title: CJP holds Constitution Day rally in Nagpur; Dipke targets Centre, ECI
articles.summary: The Cockroach Janta Party organised a Save Democracy rally at Samvidhan Square in Nagpur on November 26, 2026, drawing approximately 5,000 attendees. Founder Abhijeet Dipke, co-convener Ashutosh Ranka, and actor Prakash Raj criticized the Union government led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi over alleged electoral irregularities and institutional suppression. Speakers demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
articles.description: “There is not a single institution in this country that has not been hijacked. The Election Commission is the foremost among them,” alleges Cockroach Janta Party founder

articles.headline: Congress blames rural economic distress for potential BJP electoral losses
articles.title: Rural distress will cost BJP in coming polls, says Congress
articles.summary: On November 26, 2026, Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh stated that economic distress in rural India, driven by inflation and stagnant incomes, could cost the Bharatiya Janata Party in upcoming elections. He accused the federal government of weakening the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act and increasing the financial burden on vulnerable communities, citing recent electoral setbacks in Rajasthan as evidence of growing public anger.
articles.description: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh says the burden of inflation is considerably heavier in rural areas, where household incomes are already limited and purchasing power has declined sharply

articles.headline: United States shelves business deal proposals intended to end Ukraine conflict
articles.title: U.S. shelves proposals to use business deals with Russia to end Ukraine war, FT reports
articles.summary: The administration of United States President Donald Trump has shelved proposals to utilize corporate business deals as incentives for Russia to conclude the war in Ukraine, according to a Financial Times report published on November 25, 2026. Envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner informed European officials that energy and aviation ventures are no longer part of the diplomatic pitch.
articles.description: Donald Trump’s envoys Steve ‌Witkoff and Jared ​Kushner told European officials that ⁠corporate tie-ups were no longer ‌a core aspect of the U.S. pitch to Russia

articles.headline: Israeli judges recommend dropping most serious corruption case against Benjamin Netanyahu
articles.title: Netanyahu’s corruption trial: Is it really all over?
articles.summary: Judges in Benjamin Netanyahu's corruption trial recommended dropping the most serious bribery case against the Israeli caretaker prime minister on November 25, 2026, stating that the prospects of conviction were low. The proceedings, which began in 2020 across three separate cases involving media favours and gifts, have dogged his political career. Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara stated that the court proposals would be examined as Netanyahu called for an end to boycotts.
articles.description: Court recommendations put the Israeli leader's trial, political future and efforts to evade prosecution back in focus.

articles.headline: Telangana high court sentences two police officials in contempt case
articles.title: HC awards two-week imprisonment to Cyberabad Police Commissioner, Medchal DCP in contempt case
articles.summary: On November 26, 2026, the Telangana High Court sentenced Cyberabad Police Commissioner M. Ramesh and Medchal Deputy Commissioner of Police N. Koti Reddy to two weeks of simple imprisonment in a contempt case over a land dispute in Jeedimetla. Justice C.V. Bhaskar Reddy suspended the sentence for a week to allow the officials to seek legal remedy, while closing proceedings against Principal Home Secretary Shikha Goel and imposing a fine of 2,000 rupees on each officer.

articles.headline: Syrian children continue learning amid the ruins of war in Idlib
articles.title: Syrian children continue learning amid the ruins of war in Idlib
articles.description: Syria reopened a semi destroyed school in Idlib province

articles.headline: National Company Law Appellate Tribunal approves ₹480 crore for Jet Airways employees
articles.title: NCLAT clears ₹480 crore in Jet Airways employees’ dues, sets two-week deadline
articles.summary: The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal has ordered the release of four hundred eighty crore rupees in provident fund and gratuity dues to Jet Airways employees within two weeks. The ruling follows a seven-year legal battle after the airline entered liquidation in November twenty twenty-four. The decision dismisses appeals from the State Bank of India and other financial creditors seeking to include these employee dues in the liquidation estate.
articles.description: The relief comes after a seven-year legal battle following the airline's grounding in 2019. In November 2024, the Supreme Court ordered its liquidation

articles.headline: INDIA bloc plans anti-revision rallies in Bhopal, Ahmedabad and Kolkata
articles.title: INDIA bloc to expand anti-SIR campaign with rallies in Bhopal, Ahmedabad and Kolkata
articles.summary: The opposition INDIA bloc intends to expand its Vote Bachao Desh Bachao campaign into Bharatiya Janata Party-ruled states by staging rallies in Bhopal, Ahmedabad and Kolkata over the coming weeks. While provisional dates are set for December and January, senior leaders noted that logistics remain under discussion. The alliance continues opposing the special intensive revision of electoral rolls, which they characterize as vote theft.
articles.description: After its Delhi mobilisation, the opposition alliance plans to take the “Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao” campaign to BJP-ruled States, with a similar event also being considered in Varanasi ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly election

articles.headline: Amit Shah accuses Congress of obstructing women reservation legislation
articles.title: Women will get 33% reservation, Congress cannot stop it: Amit Shah
articles.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah criticized the Congress party on Thursday for allegedly hindering the implementation of a 33% reservation for women in legislative bodies. Speaking at a Constitution Day event in Delhi, Mr. Shah also reaffirmed the Bharatiya Janata Party commitment to enacting a Uniform Civil Code across states governed by the party. He defended government welfare programs and highlighted achievements regarding national security.
articles.description: The Home Minister says the Bharatiya Janata Party, under Prime Minister Narendra Modi, is committed to ensuring political representation for women

articles.headline: India and Israel maintain deep strategic ties spanning defense and surveillance
articles.title: Phone spying to missiles: Why India-Israel strategic ties go beyond Modi
articles.summary: India and Israel maintain a robust strategic partnership centered heavily on defense trade and military technology cooperation, according to researchers and analysts. Despite political controversies surrounding arms shipments and surveillance tools, New Delhi continues procuring Israeli systems because suppliers impose fewer operational restrictions compared to Western alternatives.
articles.description: The opposition Congress party calls Israel’s war on Gaza a genocide, but its leader still wants strong ties with Israel.

articles.headline: Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia CEO amid unfinished independent investigation
articles.title: Nvidia ignominy: Is it a new normal?
articles.summary: Jensen Huang has resumed his role as president and chief executive officer of Nvidia, whose semiconductor technology supports global artificial intelligence infrastructure. His reinstatement on November 25, 2026, occurred while an independent investigation into his departure remains incomplete. The company board now faces pressure to prove the ongoing probe is genuinely independent following his return with significant fanfare.
articles.description: The financial markets provided a thumb up to the come back of Mr. Huang, who now vows to be “a better CEO”, as Nvidia shares surged 31.5% on November 23, adding $1 trillion to market capitalisation (M-cap)

articles.headline: French court upholds order for actor Gerard Depardieu to stand trial for rape
articles.title: French actor Gerard Depardieu to stand trial for alleged 2018 rape
articles.summary: A Paris court upheld an order for French actor Gerard Depardieu to stand trial for the 2018 rape of actress Charlotte Arnould. Defence lawyer Delphine Meillet confirmed the 77-year-old actor faces one rape charge. Arnould accused Depardieu of raping her twice when she was 22. If convicted, Depardieu faces 15 to 20 years in prison as the highest-profile figure in France's MeToo movement.
articles.description: Paris court of appeal dismisses allegations relating to a second incident involving actress Charlotte Arnould.

articles.headline: Supreme Court directs tightening of front of package nutrition labelling
articles.title: Supreme Court sets four-month deadline for FSSAI to finalise stricter food labelling norms
articles.summary: The Supreme Court ordered the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India to treat total sugars and saturated fat as nutrients of concern alongside salt in food packaging graphics. Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran directed that labels feature separate hexagons with standardised pictograms and specific warning terms. The verdict stems from an application filed by the public charitable trust 3S and Our Health Society.
articles.description: The court has asked FSSAI to treat ‘total sugars’ and ‘saturated fat’, rather than ‘added sugar’ and ‘added fat’, alongside salt, as the nutrients of concern

articles.headline: India attracts $31 billion in climate equity funding over five years
articles.title: India attracts $31 billion in climate equity funding, but capital remains concentrated in power, transport
articles.summary: India secured thirty-one billion dollars in sustainability and climate equity funding between twenty twenty-one and October twenty twenty-six, according to a joint report by the Indian Venture and Alternate Capital Association and Boston Consulting Group. More than ninety percent of investments concentrated in power and transport sectors. The report estimates India requires five hundred billion dollars annually through twenty seventy to meet its climate transition goals.
articles.description: Bridging this mismatch between project requirements and investor horizons will be critical to diversifying climate finance beyond power and transport and mobilising the investments needed for India’s long-term climate transition.

articles.headline: Chief Minister Revanth Reddy announces recruitment process for 25000 government jobs
articles.title: 25K government jobs will be filled soon, taking total beyond one lakh: Revanth Reddy
articles.summary: Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy announced that twenty-five thousand government jobs will soon be filled, pushing total recruitment past one lakh. Speaking at a public meeting in Nagarkurnool district on Thursday, Reddy distributed Indiramma saris and social security pensions. He also criticized former Chief Minister K. Chandrasekhar Rao for allegedly neglecting regional irrigation projects and compromising state interests in water sharing during his decade-long tenure.
articles.description: Telangana Chief Minister reiterates his allegation that KCR neglected irrigation projects in the erstwhile Mahabubnagar district during his 10-year rule

articles.headline: Karnataka Special Investigation Team clears B. Nagendra in Valmiki Corporation scam
articles.title: SIT’s chargesheet gives clean chit to Nagendra in Valmiki Corporation scam
articles.summary: The Karnataka Special Investigation Team filed its final chargesheet before the Lokayukta Special Court on November twenty-five, clearing former minister B. Nagendra of involvement in an eighty-nine crore rupee misappropriation scandal at the Valmiki Corporation. Investigators named Nagendra as a witness rather than an accused, diverging from separate inquiries by the Central Bureau of Investigation and Enforcement Directorate. The scandal originated following an official's suicide in May twenty twenty-four.

articles.headline: Protesters gather in Delhi to demand scrapping of electoral roll revision
articles.title: Right to vote cannot be compromised: People Against SIR protest in Delhi on Constitution Day
articles.summary: Hundreds of demonstrators under the banner of People Against SIR gathered at Valmiki Sadan in New Delhi on Thursday to demand the complete withdrawal of the special intensive revision of electoral rolls. Security forces blocked protesters from marching to Jantar Mantar. Activists and political figures attended the demonstration, criticizing authorities over the perceived threat to universal adult franchise and voting rights.
articles.description: Over 200 protesters, including student groups, farmers’ unions and women’s organisations, demand scrapping of the SIR and action against the CEC; police barricades prevent march to Jantar Mantar

articles.headline: China defence ministry criticizes Japan over South China Sea disputes
articles.title: China's Defence Ministry urges Japan to stop 'stirring up' South China Sea disputes
articles.summary: The Chinese Defence Ministry demanded that Japan halt interference in the South China Sea following Tokyo decisions to provide radar and drone equipment to the Philippines for coastal surveillance. Ministry spokesperson Chen Xi stated that Japan holds no standing in maritime territorial disputes overlapping multiple regional governments.
articles.description: The comments were in response to an ⁠announcement earlier this month that Japan will provide the Philippines with radars and drones to boost its coastal surveillance capabilities

articles.headline: Teenager's death in Colombian police raid raises extrajudicial killing concerns
articles.title: How a teen’s death raises questions about Colombia’s security crackdown
articles.summary: Eighteen-year-old Ricardo Martinez was killed during a September police raid targeting a paramilitary commander in northern Colombia. President Abelardo de la Espriella praised the operation, but relatives and human rights defenders allege Martinez was an innocent civilian falsely presented as a combatant. The incident ignited fears of a resurgence of state-backed extrajudicial killings known as the false positives scandal.
articles.description: President Abelardo de la Espriella's campaign against armed groups has resulted in accusations of extrajudicial killing.

articles.headline: NDA-backed candidates lead initial phase of panchayat polls in Andhra Pradesh
articles.title: NDA-backed candidates lead in first phase of panchayat polls in three districts of Andhra Pradesh
articles.summary: The first phase of gram panchayat elections across Chittoor, Annamayya and Sri Sathya Sai districts saw brisk voter turnout exceeding 75% by the close of polling on Thursday. Initial counting results indicated a strong lead for candidates supported by the Telugu Desam Party-led National Democratic Alliance, particularly in Annamayya district. Minor tensions and protests occurred at select polling locations, prompting police intervention and an order for repolling in one ward.
articles.description: Brisk polling was recorded in Chittoor, Annamayya and Sri Sathya Sai districts, with turnout crossing 75% in all three. Counting indicated an early advantage for TDP-backed candidates, while protests and tension were reported at a few polling stations

articles.headline: Sporadic violence marks urban and rural local body polls in Andhra Pradesh
articles.title: Sporadic incidents of violence mark polling in 23 ULBs and 3,240 Gram Panchayats in Andhra Pradesh
articles.summary: Elections across twenty-three urban local bodies and over three thousand gram panchayats concluded on Thursday with scattered incidents of violence, primarily reported in the Rayalaseema region. Tentative turnout figures reached 62.50 percent for urban bodies and 74.67 percent for panchayats. Cadres from rival political parties clashed over allegations of irregularities, bogus voting, and rigging, prompting intervention by local police forces to control the crowds.
articles.description: Polling percentage in ULBs is tentatively put at 62.50, while the Gram Panchayats registered a percentage of 74.67; tension gripped Ahobilam in Nandyal district when the YSRCP supporters resorted to stone-pelting resulting in damage to a few vehicles and injuries to several persons

articles.headline: West Bengal opposition parties criticize police visits to deleted voters
articles.title: West Bengal Opposition raises alarm over police visits to deleted voters’ homes
articles.summary: Opposition parties in West Bengal have expressed concern regarding police visits to the homes of deleted voters to gather information and documents. The Mamata All India Trinamool Congress termed the visits an intimidation tactic after the Supreme Court instructed tribunals to prioritize excluded voter appeals, though State poll officials denied any involvement in the police actions.
articles.description: We do not have any such instructions and have no involvement in this, says Additional CEO, West Bengal

articles.headline: Madras High Court petition seeks Central Bureau of Investigation probe into schools fraud
articles.title: PIL filed in Madras HC seeking CBI probe into ₹400-crore schools fraud case
articles.summary: A public interest litigation petition filed in the Madras High Court requests that the investigation into an over four hundred crore rupee private schools fraud case involving former Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi be transferred from the Chennai Central Crime Branch police to the Central Bureau of Investigation, with the petitioner also calling to examine Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson.
articles.description: An advocate from Tirunelveli complains that Chennai Central Crime Branch is selectively probing the case only against former School Education Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi and had not examined Finance Minister Marie Wilson

articles.headline: The fiscal cost of cash-transfer schemes
articles.title: The fiscal cost of cash-transfer schemes
articles.description: A social policy is often based on expected electoral gain, and is implemented without any ex ante appraisal; since cash transfers and subsidies are perpetual in nature and politically hard to reverse, such continuous commitment of financial resources demands prior evaluation and real-time monitoring to address potential shortcomings

articles.headline: Yes Bank additional tier-one bond verdict creates financial uncertainty for retail shareholders
articles.title: Yes Bank AT1 bond verdict: 60 lakh retail shareholders face ₹8,415-crore bill
articles.summary: The Supreme Court verdict upholding the cancellation of a write-down on Yes Bank Additional Tier-one bonds could impact nearly sixty lakh small shareholders and large investors who may bear the cost of reversing the eight thousand four hundred fifteen crore rupee write-down, according to analysts and a proxy advisory firm following sharp drops in bank share values.
articles.description: Independent market analyst Ambareesh Baliga said nearly 60 lakh small investors could be affected, having already borne the brunt of the earlier crisis.

articles.headline: Seven people injured following explosion at Bangkok oil refinery
articles.title: Nine injured, three critically, after Bangkok oil refinery explosion
articles.summary: An explosion and subsequent fire at a Bangkok oil refinery operated by Bangchak Corporation left seven people injured, with four in critical condition. Emergency responders brought the blaze under control within thirty minutes after the incident occurred at the Phra Khanong facility. Bangchak Corporation suspended production at the site which processes up to 120,000 barrels of oil daily while investigations into the cause proceed.
articles.description: Black smoke could be seen across Bangkok's skyline after the blast, as officials urged residents to leave the area.

articles.headline: Israel's Yashar party and Democrats announce coalition government agreement
articles.title: Israel's Gadi Eisenkot reaches deal with left-wing parties
articles.summary: Israel centrist party Yashar led by Gadi Eisenkot and the left-wing Democrats have agreed to a coalition deal that allocates four ministerial portfolios to the Democrats, including an expanded national security ministry. Mr. Eisenkot faces a December deadline to form a government following an inconclusive election outcome earlier in October.
articles.description: The left-leaning Democrats are the second party to agree to a coalition deal with Yashar after the right-wing Israel Beiteinu party did so on Nov. 24

articles.headline: Why is France roiling?
articles.title: Why is France roiling?
articles.description: Al Jazeera’s Ramy Allahoum looks at how France's financial crisis is shaping next year’s vote.

articles.headline: Pep Guardiola calls for global action against Gaza crisis at conference
articles.title: Pep Guardiola calls on world to ‘disobey horror’ over Gaza and praises BDS
articles.summary: Former football coach Pep Guardiola urged international participants at the BDS@20 European conference in Barcelona to disobey the horror of the conflict in Gaza. Speaking to activists, academics, and trade unionists, Guardiola stressed that the shared demand is to stop genocide, break a siege, and end forced displacement. Rebecca O'Keeffe of Irish Sport for Palestine praised his willingness to use his global platform.
articles.description: Football icon says it is more urgent than ever to demand an end to Israel's 'apartheid, colonialism and occupation'.

articles.headline: Qatari and Egyptian leaders discuss Gaza ceasefire and regional security in Cairo
articles.title: Qatari, Egyptian leaders discuss Gaza ‘ceasefire’ and regional security
articles.summary: Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi met in Cairo on Thursday to coordinate diplomatic efforts and discuss the implementation of a Gaza ceasefire. The leaders stressed the importance of political dialogue, humanitarian aid delivery, and economic cooperation. The talks were attended by senior officials from both nations, including Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani.
articles.description: Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani is in Cairo for an official visit aimed at further strengthening bilateral relations.

articles.headline: Indian machine tool sector targets 11 percent CAGR to reach ₹62,000 crore
articles.title: Machine tool industry looks at 11 % CAGR
articles.summary: According to the Indian Machine Tool Manufacturers’ Association, the Indian machine tool sector is projected to achieve an 11 percent compound annual growth rate over the next five years, reaching over ₹62,000 crore. Representatives stated in Coimbatore on November 26, 2026, that the 2025-26 market stood at ₹36,419 crore, with domestic production up 19 percent while rising demand pushed imports to ₹21,628 crore.
articles.description: Domestic production increased 19% year-on-year to ₹17,387 crore.

articles.headline: Trade experts advise India against rushing into agreement despite proposed tariffs
articles.title: Experts say new U.S. tariffs do not pose substantial threat, India should not rush into trade deal
articles.summary: Trade specialists and exporters stated that newly proposed tariffs by the United States do not represent a critical threat to Indian shipments. The Office of the United States Trade Representative proposed a net duty that could be lowered if a bilateral agreement is signed. Analysts recommend proceeding cautiously to safeguard domestic economic interests rather than finalising a hasty trade deal.
articles.description: The latest proposal by the USTR takes the tariff framework on India back to what it was at the start of trade deal negotiations

articles.headline: US judge blocks FCC from conducting early review of Disney ABC stations
articles.title: US judge blocks Trump’s FCC attempt to target Disney’s ABC stations
articles.summary: United States District Judge Loren AliKhan granted Disney a preliminary injunction preventing the Federal Communications Commission from holding early reviews of eight ABC television station licenses. Judge AliKhan stated the agency appeared to be retaliating against the broadcaster for exercising First Amendment rights, following pressure from President Donald Trump. FCC Chair Brendan Carr and an agency spokesperson defended their authority to hold broadcasters accountable.
articles.description: The judge said the FCC chair has taken US President Donald Trump's rhetoric ‌‌as his 'marching orders'.

articles.headline: Sarvam AI launches Token Factory commercial service for AI models
articles.title: Training vs inference: What’s the distinction at the heart of the Sarvam AI-China models controversy? | Explained
articles.summary: Bengaluru startup Sarvam AI introduced a commercial service named Token Factory on November 16, 2026, providing access to both indigenous and Chinese-developed artificial intelligence models. The launch sparked debate concerning government backing under the IndiaAI Mission, leading investor Hemant Mohapatra and co-founder Pratyush Kumar to defend the platform's commercial inference operations on social media.
articles.description: Can India build an indigenous AI ecosystem while hosting models developed in China? What is Sarvam’s Token Factory? What does it mean for India’s AI ambitions?

articles.headline: Centre for Development of Advanced Computing targets indigenous 32,000-core GPU by 2028
articles.title: C-DAC targets indigenous 32,000-core GPU by mid-2028, seeks private partners; to put pressure on rival chip prices
articles.summary: The Centre for Development of Advanced Computing aims to deliver a full-fledged indigenous graphics processing unit with approximately 32,000 cores by mid-2028. Speaking in Coimbatore on November 26, 2026, Director General E. Magesh stated that the government research institution is seeking private partners for fabrication and commercialisation to increase price competition against existing chip suppliers.
articles.description: The government R&D institution says it aims to put pressure on competing suppliers through volume production; it is seeking industry partners to take its functional GPU model from FPGA to silicon

articles.headline: Andalusia regional politics offers insight into Spain's upcoming national elections
articles.title: Andalusia offers a glimpse into Spain’s future as far right gains ground
articles.summary: Spain's southern region of Andalusia operates under a coalition government formed by the conservative People's Party and the far-right Vox party. As voters prepare for snap elections, opinion polls place the People's Party ahead of Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez's Socialists, with Vox anticipated to increase its vote share. Analysts note that the regional arrangement between the two right-wing parties could serve as a precursor to national governance.
articles.description: Ahead of Sunday's election, Vox's influence is already clear in Andalusia, where right-wing alliances reshape politics.

articles.headline: Italy denounces Ukrainian strikes against Russian vessels in Libyan territorial waters
articles.title: Why is Italy angry with Ukraine for striking Russian ships off Libya?
articles.summary: Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani criticized Ukraine for violating Libya's sovereignty after Ukrainian forces struck Russian vessels off the coast of Benghazi. The attack killed two naval officers from the self-styled Libyan National Army, prompting strong condemnation from Libyan authorities and domestic political friction in Rome. Italy maintains strategic energy and migration control interests in Libya, relying heavily on the region for crude oil imports.
articles.description: Analysts say Rome fears instability in Libya could hurt its energy interests and efforts to curb irregular migration.

articles.headline: UN tribunal casts doubt on evidence used by UNRWA to dismiss staff
articles.title: UN ruling disputes Israeli allegations used to dismiss UNRWA Gaza staff
articles.summary: A United Nations tribunal ruled that the UN Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees unfairly dismissed a Palestinian employee named Abu Awad in January 2024. The judicial body found that the terminations relied on unverified Israeli allegations regarding the October 2023 attacks without proper due process. The ruling highlighted issues with intercepted communications and awarded compensation to the affected worker.
articles.description: Tribunal raises questions about the credibility of UNRWA's decision to dismiss its staff without substantiated evidence.

articles.headline: Cyberabad authorities propose unified mobility app and parking curbs to ease traffic congestion
articles.title: Cyberabad plans unified mobility app, proposes parking curbs to ease traffic
articles.summary: During a panel discussion at Cyberabad Moves 2026 in Raidurgam, officials discussed plans for a unified mobility application integrating public transport, journey planning, and electric vehicle charging stations.
