According to speakers, the platform aims to address urban traffic, while Transport for London Chief Technology Officer Shashi Verma suggested that introducing parking fees could effectively discourage private vehicle usage.
articles.description: Proposed mobility app to integrate Metro, RTC, cab services and 600 EV charging points, while private companies have been asked to cut usage of private vehicles by up to 20%

articles.headline: Watch: Vijay promised women’s safety. Did his government deliver? | Focus Tamil Nadu
articles.title: Watch: Vijay promised women’s safety. Did his government deliver? | Focus Tamil Nadu
articles.description: A woman IAS officer in Tamil Nadu has filed a harassment complaint against Kallakurichi TVK MLA C. Arul Vignesh. The case has raised questions about Chief Minister Vijay’s commitment to women’s safety and his government’s response. In this episode of The Hindu Focus Tamil Nadu, we examine the Madras High Court’s intervention and the questions of accountability facing the TVK government.

articles.headline: Karnataka government announces constitutional lessons in schools starting next academic year
articles.title: Lessons on Constitution in all schools in Karnataka from next academic year, says Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar
articles.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar announced that lessons on the Constitution will be introduced across all government and private schools in the state starting the next academic year. Speaking in Mysuru, he emphasized the importance of constitutional values, warned against attempts to delete vulnerable groups from electoral rolls, and highlighted the state government's welfare guarantee schemes.
articles.description: Separate committee to be formed to incorporate lessons into curriculum, says Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar at Constitution Day celebrations in Mysuru

articles.headline: Telangana aims to reach 5 GW data centre capacity by 2029
articles.title: Telangana aims to achieve 5 GW data centre capacity by 2029: Bhatti
articles.summary: Deputy Chief Minister Bhatti Vikramarka announced that Telangana plans to become India's leading data centre hub by achieving five gigawatts of capacity by 2029 in collaboration with industry leaders. Speaking in Hyderabad on Thursday, Vikramarka stated that current capacity stands at 300 megawatts, with two gigawatts in development, while inviting stakeholders to the upcoming Invest Telangana Global Summit.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh universities to introduce AI-integrated engineering curriculum in 2026
articles.title: Universities in Andhra Pradesh to introduce AI-integrated R-26 engineering curriculum
articles.summary: State universities in Andhra Pradesh will implement the AI-integrated R-26 engineering curriculum starting in the 2026-27 academic year to enhance technical fundamentals and graduate employability. According to Andhra Pradesh State Council of Higher Education Chairman S. Vijaya Bhaskara Rao, the framework aligns with National Education Policy 2020 objectives, incorporating emerging technologies across disciplines with a credit structure ranging from 160 to 164 credits.
articles.description: The curriculum seeks to make engineering education more relevant to evolving industry requirements, improve employability and promote innovation, research and entrepreneurship, says APSCHE Chairman

articles.headline: Infectious diseases from free-ranging domestic animals threaten wildlife in the Nilgiris
articles.title: Infectious diseases from free-ranging domestic animals threaten Nilgiris wildlife
articles.summary: Frequent contact between wildlife and free-ranging domestic animals has raised significant conservation concerns regarding disease transmission across Tamil Nadu. A Forest Department report submitted to the Madras High Court indicated that five of twelve documented infection-related wildlife deaths since 2005 occurred in the Nilgiris district, where necropsies confirmed fatalities from canine distemper and rabies among species such as leopards and Nilgiri langurs.
articles.description: Five of the 12 reported instances of wildlife deaths since 2005 likely due to infections contracted from feral animals were recorded in the Nilgiris district, shows report by Forest Department

articles.headline: Committee demands inclusion of tenant farmers in Telangana crop loss survey
articles.title: Enumerate Telangana tenant farmers in crop loss survey; support financially distressed farmers: Committee
articles.summary: The Telangana Tenant Farmers Recognition Struggle Committee has urged the State government to include tenant farmers in the ongoing Agriculture Department crop loss survey addressing El Nino drought impacts. During a press conference in Hyderabad on Thursday, members highlighted that tenant farmers face severe financial distress and lack recognition cards, which are necessary to access bank loans, welfare schemes, and minimum support prices.

articles.headline: Gérard Depardieu to stand trial for alleged rape of actress
articles.title: Gérard Depardieu to stand trial for alleged rape of actress in 2018, court rules
articles.summary: A Paris appeals court has confirmed that French actor Gérard Depardieu will stand trial for the alleged rape of actress Charlotte Arnould following an incident at his home in August 2018. Arnould, who waived her right to anonymity, pursued a civil complaint after initial dismissal, while the 77-year-old actor has consistently denied all allegations of coercion and violence through his legal representatives.
articles.description: A Paris appeals court rules Depardieu will go on trial for the alleged rape of Charlotte Arnould.

articles.headline: Global maritime trade faces stagnation in 2026 amid disruptions
articles.title: Global shipping faces zero growth in 2026; India gains ground amid maritime disruptions: UNCTAD
articles.summary: Global maritime trade is projected to see zero growth in 2026 due to geopolitical conflicts and major sea route disruptions in the Red Sea, Black Sea, and Strait of Hormuz, according to a report released on November 26 by the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development. While these disruptions have severely strained international shipping and inflated freight rates, India has emerged as a key beneficiary through increased container capacity at ports like Mundra and Nhava Sheva.
articles.description: While the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and disruptions in the Red Sea, Black Sea and Panama Canal have severely strained global shipping, diversions have strengthened the position of Indian ports in long-haul container networks.

articles.headline: Iraqi prime minister orders federal takeover of border crossings and oilfields in Kurdish region
articles.title: How an oil feud is deepening rift between Baghdad and Iraq’s Kurdish region
articles.summary: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered federal authorities to seize control of all border crossings and oilfields in the northern Kurdish region to combat smuggling. The Kurdistan Regional Government denounced the measures as a constitutional violation, while the Federal Supreme Court issued a ruling backing Baghdad on November 24, 2026, amid an escalating political confrontation.
articles.description: Prime Minister al-Zaidi's move to take control of border crossings and oilfields has drawn a sharp response from Erbil.

articles.headline: Turkish president hosts eastern Libyan military commander Khalifa Haftar in Ankara
articles.title: Haftar meets Erdogan: Can Turkiye reunify Libya as it courts rival sides?
articles.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan hosted eastern Libyan military commander Khalifa Haftar in Ankara on November 25, 2026, to discuss national reunification. Following a 2020 ceasefire, Turkiye has engaged both Tripoli and Benghazi administrations to protect its Mediterranean maritime boundary agreement, economic investments, and regional diplomatic interests.
articles.description: Maritime agreement pivotal for Turkiye's Eastern Mediterranean gas claims as Libya's unification process faces hurdles.

articles.headline: D. Gukesh expresses energetic form after drawing second game against Javokhir Sindarov
articles.title: World chess championship: I feel energetic on the board, says Gukesh
articles.summary: Indian grandmaster D. Gukesh stated he feels energetic on the board after drawing his second match against Javokhir Sindarov in Geneva on November 26, 2026. During the ongoing 14-game World chess championship, Gukesh also criticized the new fast classical time control of 45 minutes, arguing it functions more like rapid chess.

articles.headline: Jordan parliament reviews antiterrorism law amendments following church attack
articles.title: Jordan Parliament debates ‘antiterror’ law after deadly Karak church attack
articles.summary: Jordan's House of Representatives referred proposed amendments to the 2006 Anti-Terrorism Law to its Legal Committee on Wednesday. The changes would raise minimum prison terms to between 10 and 15 years while retaining the death penalty for serious offences. The legislation follows an October 23 attack at a church in Hamoud that killed nine people and wounded 34, prompting debate over national security and free expression.
articles.description: House votes to refer draft amendments to the 2006 Anti-Terrorism Law to its Legal Committee for review.

articles.headline: Universal basic income proposals gain traction amid artificial intelligence job fears
articles.title: Is UBI the solution to mass unemployment in an AI economy?
articles.summary: Proposals for universal basic income are gaining attention as rapid advances in artificial intelligence raise concerns about mass unemployment. Proponents argue unconditional cash payments could prevent poverty and sustain consumer spending. However, critics like King's College London economics professor Jonathan Portes caution that adequate funding is politically and economically challenging, while trials show only modest impacts on work hours.
articles.description: AI's rapid advance has led to calls for universal payments to prevent poverty and wealth inequality.

articles.headline: Film shows testimonies of international doctors amid Gaza genocide
articles.title: Film shows testimonies of international doctors amid Gaza genocide
articles.description: A documentary shows footage from international doctors who bore witness to the collapse of the Gaza's medical system.

articles.headline: Israel reaffirms solidarity with India on anniversary of Mumbai terror attacks
articles.title: Israel says it stands firmly with India in fight against terror on 26/11 anniversary
articles.summary: Israel’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated on November 26, 2026, that it stands firmly with India in the joint fight against terrorism while honoring victims of the 2008 Mumbai attacks. The coordinated assault by 10 Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists left 166 people dead and over 300 injured across multiple iconic locations, underscoring a shared international commitment to defeating cross-border terror.
articles.description: Five Israelis were also killed by the terrorists at Nariman House during the 2008 attacks

articles.headline: Samajwadi Party and Congress experience tension over Uttar Pradesh seat-sharing
articles.title: SP-Congress seat-sharing: the uneasy arithmetic of U.P.’s Opposition alliance
articles.summary: Friction emerged between the Samajwadi Party and the Congress after the regional party unilaterally released candidates following initial negotiations where it offered only 26 seats. Political observers noted that fielding four Muslim candidates in Western Uttar Pradesh aims to project the party as the primary representative of Muslim voters, a demographic largely backing the alliance.
articles.description: As the Samajwadi Party unilaterally declares five candidates after floating a 26-seat formula for Congress, old wounds, local turf wars, competing memories, and a tug-of-war over Muslim votes test the alliance in UP

articles.headline: Samajwadi Party releases election manifesto promising graduate allowances and free power
articles.title: SP’s election manifesto promises ₹5,000 monthly allowance for graduates, free power and MSP guarantee
articles.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav released the party manifesto on November 26, 2026, promising a monthly allowance of 5,000 rupees for unemployed graduates, a 100 percent waiver on farmers' electricity bills, and free irrigation power in Uttar Pradesh. The document also outlines proposals for a caste census, urban employment guarantees, and increased reservations for marginalized communities.
articles.description: The manifesto released by the SP chief Akhilesh Yadav promises 100% waiver of farmers’ outstanding electricity bills within three months of forming the government

articles.headline: Telangana Chief Minister accuses central leaders of voter suppression conspiracy
articles.title: Modi, Shah conspiring to remove votes to regain power fourth time: Telangana CM Revanth Reddy
articles.summary: Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy alleged that senior national leaders are conspiring to remove voter names to secure a fourth consecutive term. Speaking at a Constitution Day march in Hyderabad, he contrasted democratic voting rights with current political actions. Regional leaders and party officials participated in the event, highlighting ongoing ideological debates concerning constitutional values across the country.
articles.description: Telangana Chief Minister participates in Samvidhan Raksha March held in Hyderabad

articles.headline: Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor dies aged 65
articles.title: Tributes for Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor after his death aged 65
articles.summary: Andy Taylor, the lead guitarist for the pop group Duran Duran, passed away at home in the United Kingdom at the age of sixty-five following a long battle with prostate cancer. According to a statement from his family and bandmates, the musician died peacefully surrounded by his relatives. Taylor co-wrote several major hits during the band's global success in the 1980s.
articles.description: Simon Le Bon and his other bandmates say Taylor "brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music".

articles.headline: Heavy rainfall severely disrupts traffic and inundates parts of Thiruvananthapuram
articles.title: Heavy rain submerges parts of Keralam’s Thiruvananthapuram; Thampanoor worst hit as traffic grinds to a halt
articles.summary: An intense two-hour downpour on November 26, 2026, submerged major roads and brought normal life in Thiruvananthapuram to a near-standstill. Thampanoor emerged as one of the worst-affected areas, with knee-deep water surrounding transit hubs and stalling vehicles, prompting authorities to divert traffic while residents blamed poor drainage maintenance for the recurring flooding.
articles.description: Knee-deep water submerges roads around the Thiruvananthapuram Central railway station and the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation bus terminal. Traders say Thiruvananthapuram city Corporation and successive governments have failed to find an effective and lasting solution to waterlogging

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay advises students to remain vigilant against corruption
articles.title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay warns students against corruption, says steps being taken to curb it
articles.summary: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam president and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay urged students on November 26, 2026, to resist corruption during a felicitation event near Chennai. He highlighted alleged irregularities in school education procurement and library book funding, asserting that his administration is actively taking steps to control systemic graft across government departments.
articles.description: Speaking at a felicitation event for toppers of Classes X and XII from various districts held at a private wedding hall in Neelankarai near Chennai,, he said corruption was not new, but it could not be dismissed as something people had grown accustomed to.

articles.headline: BITS Pilani researchers patent low-cost microalgae nutrient medium
articles.title: BITS Pilani-Hyderabad researchers develop affordable way to grow microalgae
articles.summary: Researchers at the Birla Institute of Technology and Science (BITS) Pilani, Hyderabad Campus, have patented a low-cost nutrient medium for mass cultivating microalgae. Developed by Sandip S. Deshmukh, K. Pranav Narayan, and Sama Sanghamitra, the formulation uses agricultural-grade fertilisers to reduce costs to about ₹2.40 per 100 litres. The technology was successfully tested in a 10,000-litre open pond and could aid biofuels, carbon capture, and biotechnology applications.

articles.headline: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar urges striking ASHA workers to resume duty
articles.title: Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar tells striking ASHA workers not to ‘blackmail’ government
articles.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar urged striking ASHA workers to end their agitation and return to work, stating that the government cannot be blackmailed. Speaking in Mysuru on November 26, 2026, he rejected demands for a written assurance, warning it would prompt similar requests from other groups. He assured workers that their demands would be addressed during the Cabinet and Legislature session.
articles.description: Rejecting their demand for a written assurance, the CM urged workers to end strike and resume duties.

articles.headline: Egyptian authorities arrest motorist following deadly tanker crash and fire
articles.title: Egyptian authorities arrest motorist over tanker crash that killed 31
articles.summary: Law enforcement officials in Egypt apprehended an unnamed driver who confessed to causing a severe traffic collision and subsequent fire on a Cairo ring road that left 31 people dead and 21 others injured. Investigators determined that the motorist struck a fuel tanker while changing lanes at high speed on Wednesday evening, prompting the vehicle to overturn and ignite.
articles.description: Officials say the man confessed to travelling at speed and clipping the fuel truck as he was overtaking traffic.

articles.headline: Mangaluru-Bengaluru highway widening project concludes after decade of delays
articles.title: 10 years and doubled cost: The four-laning saga of Mangaluru-Bengaluru NH 75 in Dakshina Kannada and Hassan
articles.summary: The widening of the national highway between Hassan and Dakshina Kannada districts concluded after a decade, with total expenses nearly doubling. Commuters faced severe difficulties during construction due to contractor insolvencies, prolonged delays, and poor road conditions. Although travel times decreased, local users continue to raise safety concerns and express frustration regarding speed limitations enforced on the newly completed sections.
articles.description: The key highway connecting the state capital with coastal Karnataka becomes completely four-lane except the 26 km stretch of Shiradi Ghat between Maranahalli and Addahole

articles.headline: With the rise of AI, are we close to having universal basic income
articles.title: With the rise of AI, are we close to having universal basic income
articles.description: Is UBI the solution to mass unemployment in an AI economy?

articles.headline: United Kingdom sanctions Yemen Houthi group and senior leaders
articles.title: ‘Symbolic’: Why did UK sanction Yemen’s Houthis amid attacks on Saudi?
articles.summary: The United Kingdom has imposed sanctions and travel bans on Yemen's Houthi group and four senior leaders, including Interior Minister Abdulkarim Amir al-Din Hussein al-Houthi. Announced on Tuesday, the measures target the Iran-backed group for renewed aggression and attacks on civilian infrastructure in Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping lanes. Analysts note the practical impact of the asset freezes will likely be limited.
articles.description: UK sanctions Iran-backed group and its leaders, accusing them of undermining stability in the Middle East.

articles.headline: Centre confirms Mumbai Police lookout circular against Saurav Das
articles.title: Mumbai Police issued Look Out Circular against CJP's Saurav Das: Centre tells Delhi HC
articles.summary: The central government informed the Delhi High Court that the Mumbai Police issued a lookout circular against Campaign for Judicial Accountability and Reform co-convenor Saurav Das. Mr. Das was previously stopped at the Delhi airport from boarding a flight to London. The high court scheduled the next hearing for December 9.
articles.description: Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma said the travel advisory issued to Mr. Das was in his own interest, as he could face serious complications if the passport authorities subsequently found his explanation unsatisfactory

articles.headline: German police arrest two Iraqi nationals over alleged Cologne synagogue bomb plot
articles.title: German police arrest two Iraqis over alleged Cologne synagogue bomb plot
articles.summary: German prosecutors announced the arrest of two Iraqi nationals, identified as Mostafa Al-R. and Ameer J., following raids across three states. The suspects allegedly belong to an Islamist organisation that plotted explosive attacks against Jewish and other European targets, including a Cologne synagogue in March. The investigation was initiated based on intelligence provided by Germany's domestic intelligence agency.
articles.description: Germany has suffered a series ⁠of attacks and plots in recent years, including a fatal attack in July in which a man who pledged ‌allegiance to Islamic State attacked a Pride celebration in Berlin

articles.headline: ED attaches properties worth 702 crore rupees in homebuyers fraud case
articles.title: ED attaches Ozone Group properties worth ₹702.70 crore in homebuyers’ fraud case
articles.summary: The Directorate of Enforcement Bengaluru Zonal Office attached immovable assets valued at 702.70 crore rupees belonging to Ozone Group. According to the agency, funds collected from buyers and housing loans were diverted to repay liabilities rather than complete incomplete housing projects. This latest action follows a previous provisional attachment of assets worth 423.37 crore rupees executed on October 4, 2025, as investigations into the alleged fraud continue.
articles.description: Agency alleges ₹1,305 crore fraud; says funds collected for housing projects were diverted to repay loans, investors and meet corporate expenses

articles.headline: Fuel truck explosion on Giza highway kills at least thirty one people
articles.title: Highway explosion in Giza: How deadly are Egypt’s roads and railways?
articles.summary: An overturned fuel truck caught fire on a ring road in Giza's Imbabah district, resulting in thirty one deaths and twenty one injuries. The public prosecutor initiated an investigation after twenty seven vehicles burned during the incident. Egypt recorded thousands of road fatalities between 2019 and 2025 according to the Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics amid ongoing scrutiny over transportation safety.
articles.description: Egypt has suffered another tragedy as a deadly road explosion kills 31 and injures dozens.

articles.headline: Jewish Network for Palestine challenges UK ban on Hamas
articles.title: ‘Proscribing free speech’: Why a Jewish group is challenging UK’s Hamas ban
articles.summary: The Jewish Network for Palestine filed an application to reverse the British government proscription of Hamas. The group argues that the ban infringes on freedom of speech and has been used against its members. Home Secretary Shabana Mahmoud has ninety days to consider the application following the formal submission on Thursday.
articles.description: The Jewish Network for Palestine says the complete ban on Hamas was being used to stifle free speech.

articles.headline: US Army hails controlled explosion of toxic explosives in Iowa
articles.title: US Army says controlled blast of explosives in Iowa was 'huge success'
articles.summary: The United States military declared a controlled detonation of nearly five tonnes of deteriorating lead azide in Middletown, Iowa, a massive success. Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle stated that mitigation efforts exceeded expectations with no initial air readings above zero. The operation proceeded following legal challenges and public concern, drawing relief from local residents alongside calls for continued transparency.
articles.description: Officials say no lead has been detected in the surrounding area, which continues to be tested following concerns from locals.

articles.headline: Thanksgiving dinner costs increase across the United States
articles.title: Thanksgiving dinner costs rise, putting pressure on US households
articles.summary: American households face financial strain as the cost of a typical Thanksgiving meal rises significantly from last year. According to data from The Century Foundation, grocery prices and travel expenses have increased due to supply chain pressures and tariffs. Many hosts are now scaling back celebrations or borrowing money to cover holiday expenses.
articles.description: Turkeys see a 26-percent price rise, forcing families to reconsider hosting and opt for potluck-style celebrations.

articles.headline: Palestine football coach Ihab Abu Jazar discusses team challenges
articles.title: Palestine coach says team represents suffering but also offers hope
articles.summary: Palestine national football team coach Ihab Abu Jazar spoke about managing his professional responsibilities while his family experiences displacement in Gaza. The forty-six-year-old coach led his squad to Asian Cup qualification despite the ongoing conflict. He emphasized that the team serves as a vital symbol of hope and resilience for Palestinians worldwide.
articles.description: Despite navigating personal hardships, Ihab Abu Jazar calls it a 'badge of honour' to coach the Palestine football team.

articles.headline: Kenyan High Court rules Ebola quarantine facility unconstitutional
articles.title: Kenya gov’t violated constitution with Ebola quarantine site, court says
articles.summary: A Kenyan court ruled that the government breached the constitution by permitting a United States-backed Ebola quarantine facility at Laikipia airbase without public consultation. High Court Judge Patricia Nyaundi ordered construction to halt until officials meet legal requirements. The project had previously sparked violent protests among local residents in Nanyuki.
articles.description: Kenya's High Court orders halt to ⁠further works at quarantine facility until details of deal with US are disclosed.

articles.headline: Bangkok oil refinery fire leaves seven injured and halts production units
articles.title: Massive fire at Bangkok oil refinery leaves several injured, Bangchak Corp shuts all units
articles.summary: A major fire broke out at the Phra Khanong oil refinery in Bangkok on November 26, 2026, injuring at least seven people according to the Erawan Emergency Medical Centre. Bangchak Corp, which operates the facility with a capacity of 1,20,000 barrels per day, shut down all production units. The blaze started around 2.45 p.m. local time, causing loud blasts and black smoke over the capital before being extinguished thirty minutes later.
articles.description: Flames rose high above the site, followed by black smoke that swept across the Thai capital’s skyline

articles.headline: Telangana defence sector outpaces IT and pharma growth
articles.title: Defence, aerospace sector outpaces IT and pharma growth in Telangana: Minister Uttam Kumar Reddy
articles.summary: Telangana Minister for Irrigation and Civil Supplies N. Uttam Kumar Reddy stated on November 26, 2026, that the state's defence and aerospace sector is growing faster than IT and pharma. Speaking at the CII Telangana Defence and Aerospace Conclave 2026 in Hyderabad, the former Indian Air Force pilot highlighted doubled production and exports while promoting the upcoming Raksha Expo 2026 to boost global manufacturing supply chains.
articles.description: Telangana well positioned to emerge as a major partner in global defence and aerospace manufacturing networks, Uttam Kumar Reddy said at CII conclave in Hyderabad

articles.headline: India warns Netflix against airing Pakistani content
articles.title: Jo Bachay… government warns Netflix on Pakistani series
articles.summary: The Union Ministry of Information and Broadcasting urged Netflix to adhere to its commitment of avoiding Pakistani content, citing national security and cross-border terrorism. The warning follows the catalogue listing of a Pakistani series. Film bodies condemned the potential release, while Netflix and the producer have not commented on the status.
articles.description: According to official sources, the government warned Netflix that the 2025 advisory banning Pakistan-origin content from streaming platforms was still in effect

articles.headline: Defence Space Agency seeks Indian partners for advanced technologies
articles.title: Defence Space Agency seeks Indian partners for AI, anti-jamming and space surveillance tech
articles.summary: Air Vice Marshal Manu Midha announced that the Defence Space Agency is seeking partnerships with domestic startups and research institutions to develop orbital analytics and anti-jamming systems. Speaking in Chennai, Midha emphasized the growing military importance of space infrastructure. The initiative aims to strengthen strategic autonomy and reduce reliance on foreign supply chains.
articles.description: Space has become a contested military theatre, says Air Vice Marshal Manu Midha at Tec-Verse 2026; armed forces seek secure networks and software-defined radios

articles.headline: Karnataka groundnut cultivation declines due to drought and rising prices
articles.title: Drought affects groundnut cultivation in Karnataka; prices rise amid supply shortage
articles.summary: Severe drought conditions in Karnataka caused widespread crop failure across 1.49 lakh hectares, delaying market arrivals and driving up groundnut prices ahead of the Kadlekai Parishe festival. According to Agriculture Department data, sowing reached only 1.59 lakh hectares against a target of 2.54 lakh hectares. Farmers in districts like Kolar and Chitradurga reported poor yields, drying borewells, and increased costs, pushing hybrid variety prices to 10,809 rupees per quintal.
articles.description: According to Agriculture Department data, groundnut sowing this year stood at 1.59 lakh hectares against the target of 2.54 lakh hectares. Of the area sown, crop failure has been recorded across 1.49 lakh hectares, accounting for 93.71% of the total sown area

articles.headline: Madras High Court appoints monitor for public library book scam probe
articles.title: Tamil Nadu public libraries book purchase scam: Madras High Court nominates DGP Venkataraman to monitor DVAC probe
articles.summary: The Madras High Court nominated Director General of Police G. Venkataraman on November 25, 2026, to monitor the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti Corruption investigation into a library book procurement scam. Justice V. Lakshminarayanan ordered periodical status reports after noting that the Tamil Nadu government purchased substandard AI generated books costing up to 1,645 rupees each for public libraries.
articles.description: Justice V. Lakshminarayanan empowers the nominated officer to suggest measures to the investigating officer and directs the Director of Vigilance and Anti Corruption to coordinate with him

articles.headline: Supreme Court repeatedly adjourns bail plea hearings for activist Umar Khalid
articles.title: Umar Khalid’s bail plea: A timeline of court hearings and adjournments
articles.summary: Activist and former Jawaharlal Nehru University scholar Umar Khalid withdrew his Supreme Court bail plea on February 14 after facing numerous adjournments by the apex court. Arrested under the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act for alleged involvement in the February 2020 North East Delhi riots, he had previously been denied bail by the Karkardooma Court and the Delhi High Court.
articles.description: In jail since September 2020, Umar Khaild withdrew his bail plea from the top court citing a “change in circumstances” following a series of adjournments

articles.headline: Pakistani astronaut recites verses by poet Muhammad Iqbal in space
articles.title: Iqbal in space: Urdu poet’s verses unite India, Pakistan beyond Earth
articles.summary: Muhammad Zeeshan Ali recited a couplet by national poet Muhammad Iqbal while floating inside China's Tiangong space station on Wednesday. The poet's verses have previously been referenced in space by Indian astronauts, including Rakesh Sharma in 1984 and Kalpana Chawla in 1997. Iqbal was a 20th-century philosopher whose ideas helped shape Muslim politics in South Asia before his death in Lahore in 1938.
articles.description: Pakistan's first astronaut recited Iqbal on board China's space station, echoing two earlier encounters in orbit.

articles.headline: ED alleges KPSC officials leaked veterinary recruitment exam papers
articles.title: KPSC recruitment scam in Karnataka: How question papers and answer keys reached candidates ahead of exams | Explained
articles.summary: The Enforcement Directorate filed a complaint under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act against senior officials, including former chairman Shivashankarappa Sahukar and controller Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar. Investigators allege that officials leaked question papers for veterinary officer recruitment held on January 8 and 9, 2026, in exchange for bribes ranging from twenty to forty lakh rupees.
articles.description: The ED has filed a filed a prosecution complaint under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) against the former KPSC Chairman Shivashankarappa Sahukar, member B.V. Geetha Shivamurthy, Controller of Examinations Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar and his associate Basavaraj Kannale

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu government signs seventy-eight memoranda of understanding for investments
articles.title: 78 MoUs signed at second edition of VETTRI Tamil Nadu Investment and Conversion Conclave
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu government signed seventy-eight memoranda of understanding worth fifty-eight thousand two hundred fourteen crore rupees on November 25, 2026, during the VETTRI conclave in Chennai. Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay presided over the event, which aims to generate over sixty-five thousand jobs across multiple districts. New industrial projects include facilities by Royal Enfield, PMC Hydraulics, JK Fenner, and WEG.
articles.description: The MoUs involve investments worth ₹58,214 crore, with the potential to generate 65,786 jobs across various sectors.

articles.headline: Locals vandalise church in Odisha village over land dispute
articles.title: Church on ‘government land’ vandalised in Odisha village, peace committee formed
articles.summary: Residents in Patraguda village of Odisha's Koraput district vandalised a prayer hall built on government land, leading local authorities to establish a peace committee on November 26, 2026. The incident followed a police complaint by the sole Christian family in the settlement. Police have registered a case against seven individuals as revenue inspectors investigate the plot status and ownership claims.
articles.description: The incident came to light after an individual belonging to the only Christian family in the tribal village, lodged a police complaint on November 21, alleging that a group of locals had vandalised the Beersheba Pentecostal Church

articles.headline: Norse Atlantic suspends flights and warns of imminent bankruptcy
articles.title: Airline Norse Atlantic suspends flights, warns of possible bankruptcy
articles.summary: Norwegian airline Norse Atlantic suspended operations on November 26, 2026, stating that the board will file for bankruptcy unless short-term financing is secured immediately. The budget carrier cited critical liquidity issues and soaring jet fuel costs linked to ongoing supply disruptions. Pakistan International Airlines recently cancelled two flights after Norse abruptly halted a wet-lease agreement between the companies.
articles.description: Norse ​continues to consider ‌options to secure short-term financing and is in discussion with investors regarding a possible takeover that would include a financing solution

articles.headline: Explosion rocks Bangkok oil depot
articles.title: Explosion rocks Bangkok oil depot
articles.description: A Large explosion at an oil depot in Bangkok sent flames and smoke into the sky.

articles.headline: Why has North Korea expelled a Swiss diplomat from Pyongyang?
articles.title: Why has North Korea expelled a Swiss diplomat from Pyongyang?
articles.description: At the centre of the diplomatic dispute lies the Songdowon International Children’s Camp.

articles.headline: National Congress Party leader Sharad Pawar hospitalized in Mumbai for dehydration
articles.title: Sharad Pawar admitted to hospital in south Mumbai due to dehydration
articles.summary: Sharad Pawar, leader of the National Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar), was admitted to Breach Candy Hospital in south Mumbai on November 26, 2026, due to dehydration. His daughter and Member of Parliament Supriya Sule confirmed the hospitalization on social media, noting her father's persistent travel habits. This marks the second time within a month that the 85-year-old politician has required medical care following an earlier respiratory infection in November.
articles.description: This is the second time in a month that the 85-year-old Mr. Pawar was admitted in a hospital

articles.headline: Seven injured in explosion at oil facility in Thailand’s Bangkok
articles.title: Seven injured in explosion at oil facility in Thailand’s Bangkok
articles.description: Authorities urge residents in area surrounding oil depot in eastern Bangkok to evacuate their homes.

articles.headline: Staff Selection Commission plans indigenous devices for computer-based examinations
articles.title: SSC plans to use indigenous examination devices to take computer-based tests beyond private centres
articles.summary: The Staff Selection Commission aims to develop an indigenous examination device and closed-circuit television solution to conduct computer-based tests in village and district schools. Chairman S. Gopalakrishnan stated during Tech Verse 2026 in Chennai that the initiative reduces reliance on private centres, enhances hardware security, and minimizes malpractice risks through edge-based video analytics.
articles.description: The Staff Selection Commission has floated an RFP for indigenous examination tablets, attracting interest from over 25 bidders, says its chairman. It is also exploring edge-based CCTV systems, as defence officials seek homegrown space, AI and communication technologies

articles.headline: Tata Trusts challenges N. Chandrasekaran reappointment at Bombay High Court
articles.title: Tata Trusts decides to move Bombay High Court challenging N. Chandrasekaran’s reappointment
articles.summary: Tata Trusts decided to approach the Bombay High Court to challenge the reappointment of N. Chandrasekaran as chairman of Tata Sons, approved by the board on September 17, 2026. The Trusts argue the decision violated the Articles of Association because nominated members did not vote in unison during the meeting.
articles.description: The Tata Trusts termed this “reappointment illegal”, as it violated the company’s Articles of Association

articles.headline: Indigenous groups mark National Day of Mourning on Thanksgiving
articles.title: Thanksgiving and National Day of Mourning: What is the history?
articles.summary: Indigenous activists and supporters gathered in Plymouth, Massachusetts, on November 26, 2026, to observe the 57th annual National Day of Mourning. Participants highlighted centuries of colonisation, land dispossession, and broken treaties that are traditionally overlooked by mainstream Thanksgiving narratives. The protest originated in 1970 after an Indigenous speaker was disinvited from a colonial anniversary event.
articles.description: Indigenous activists challenge Thanksgiving narratives and highlight ongoing struggles for sovereignty and recognition.

articles.headline: Rescuers recover bodies after flood at illegal Indonesia gold mine
articles.title: Rescuers recover bodies after flood at illegal Indonesia gold mine
articles.description: At least 13 miners died and others remain missing after heavy rain flooded an illegal gold mine in West Java, Indonesia.

articles.headline: Madras High Court rules Muslims cannot be barred from mosque prayers
articles.title: No Muslim, irrespective of political affiliation, can be prevented from offering Namaz in mosques: Madras High Court
articles.summary: Justice V. Lakshminarayanan of the Madras High Court ruled on November 26, 2026, that no Muslim can be prevented from offering namaz in any mosque due to political affiliations. The petition involved a dispute in Salem city between Bharatiya Janata Party member M. Syed Ibrahim and Indian Union Muslim League office-bearer Syed Moosa.
articles.description: Justice V. Lakshminarayanan says, as per Islam, it is only for Allah, the almighty, and not for ordinary mortals, to decide who is a Muslim and who is not. The orders were passed while disposing of a writ petition (criminal) filed by a BJP Minority Morcha office-bearer against IUML office-bearer.

articles.headline: Chief Justice Surya Kant warns lawyers against pursuing political agendas in courts
articles.title: Constitution Day: CJI Surya Kant says lawyers must not masquerade political agendas as professional duty
articles.summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant stated on November 26, 2026, at Supreme Court Bar Association Constitution Day celebrations that lawyers must not disguise political agendas as professional duties. The CJI also addressed systemic challenges including judicial pendency, case delays, and unequal access to legal representation across the justice system.
articles.description: Courts must not be targetted for personal gain, CJI Surya Kant says

articles.headline: Pankaj Advani becomes first Indian to win Crucible Cup
articles.title: Snooker 900: Pankaj Advani becomes first Indian to win Crucible Cup
articles.summary: Pankaj Advani defeated Malta's Tony Drago 6-0 in Reading to become the first Indian to win the Crucible Cup under the Snooker 900 format. Advani dropped only three frames throughout the tournament, overcoming opponents including Neil Robertson and Joe Perry. The victory ensures that India will host the subsequent edition of the international tournament in 2027.
articles.description: Advani, the reigning world billiard champion, displayed a blend of skill and composure to beat defending champion and former world snooker champion Neil Robertson of Australia 5-2 in his first match

articles.headline: Thirteen workers die in Indonesia gold mine flood
articles.title: At least 13 dead in Indonesia gold mine flood as rescue efforts intensify
articles.summary: At least thirteen workers died and thirteen others remained missing after flooding struck an unauthorised gold mine in Indonesia’s West Java province. Local search and rescue chief Desiana Kartika Bahari confirmed the death toll, noting that 325 personnel faced difficult terrain during operations in the mountainous Pongkor area near Bogor.
articles.description: Rescue workers facing tough conditions, with narrow, deep and slippery excavation pits and minimal lighting.

articles.headline: NTA to reconduct three UGC-NET papers after errors
articles.title: What led to the re-test of three UGC-NET papers? | Explained
articles.summary: The National Testing Agency announced that the University Grants Commission-National Eligibility Test for English, sociology, and commerce will be held again following complaints of multiple errors. An investigative committee recommended the re-test to ensure fairness, while results for the remaining eighty-four subjects will be declared as scheduled without any delays.
articles.description: What were the errors in the question papers? Why are candidates concerned? What happens to candidates who sat for the other 84 exams?

articles.headline: Thirteen miners killed following floods at illegal Bogor gold mine
articles.title: Thirteen dead as mine disaster highlights illegal hunt for gold
articles.summary: Authorities confirmed on November 26, 2026, that 13 people died and another 13 remain missing after heavy rain flooded an illegal open-pit gold mine in Bogor, Indonesia. Rescue teams faced narrow, slippery shafts during ongoing operations. The disaster underscores the persistent dangers and widespread prevalence of unregulated small-scale mining driven by soaring global gold prices.
articles.description: Indonesian authorities say another 13 are missing in the illegal gold mine, which flooded on Monday.

articles.headline: Cockroach Janta Party founder claims government is jealous of Oxford invite
articles.title: Government ‘jealous’ that 27-year-old invited to Oxford: Dipke on Das being stopped from flying to U.K.
articles.summary: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke alleged on November 26, 2026, that the government blocked CJP co-convenor Saurav Das from traveling to the United Kingdom for events at the London School of Economics and Oxford University out of jealousy. The Ministry of External Affairs stated Mr. Das received a show-cause notice regarding passport birth details.
articles.description: Saurav Das approached the Delhi High Court after he was stopped from flying to the U.K. for an event at Oxford University, where he was slated to speak on the “cockroach movement”

articles.headline: Meta officials meet Congress leaders following content moderation bias allegations
articles.title: Meta officials meet Congress leaders amid allegations of bias in content moderation
articles.summary: Representatives from the technology firm Meta met with Indian Youth Congress functionaries in Delhi on November 24, 2026, following protests over alleged political content restrictions. According to Congress sources, Meta defended its synthetic content policies while denying political bias, and the disputed Instagram accounts were later restored.
articles.description: Meta was represented by Aman Jain and Natasha Jog, while Congress leader Supriya Shrinate attended the meeting

articles.headline: Indian defence forces increase monitoring of messaging apps over security risks
articles.title: What led to the Defence Forces advisory on data security? | Explained
articles.summary: India's defence forces heightened vigilance on messaging platforms following intelligence reports regarding potential infiltration attempts by Pakistan-based intelligence operatives. Officials stated that operatives targeted unofficial WhatsApp groups utilized by military, paramilitary, and civil defence personnel by employing spoofed mobile numbers to secretly gather sensitive information without detection.
articles.description: The reiterated advisory, circulated to defence and security establishments, flagged attempts by these operatives to gain unauthorised access to messaging groups using spoofed or compromised Indian mobile numbers

articles.headline: DR Congo summons Ugandan diplomat over military chief's threats
articles.title: DR Congo demands answers over Ugandan general's threats
articles.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo summoned Uganda's top envoy in Kinshasa to address provocative social media posts by Ugandan military chief General Muhoozi Kainerugaba. The general appeared to support a rebel takeover in eastern DR Congo and criticized foreign mercenaries. The Congolese foreign ministry denounced the remarks on November 25, 2026, demanding official clarification and measures to prevent further diplomatic friction.
articles.description: Gen Kainerugaba threatened a rebel takeover of a mineral-rich area in DR Congo in controversial X posts.

articles.headline: French navy intercepts suspected drug-smuggling semi-submersible
articles.title: French navy intercepts suspected drug-smuggling semi-submersible
articles.description: French forces intercepted a semi-submersible suspected of drug trafficking in the Atlantic.

articles.headline: Australian Parliament passes Digital Duty of Care legislation for tech firms
articles.title: Australia’s Digital Duty of Care law: Why Big Tech is under pressure
articles.summary: The Australian Parliament enacted the Digital Duty of Care Bill on November 25, 2026, legally obligating online services, social media platforms, games, apps, and artificial intelligence chatbots to protect users. Companies violating the new regulations face financial penalties reaching up to five percent of their global turnover or 109.2 million Australian dollars. The legislation amends the Online Safety Act 2021 by replacing previous safety codes with a single enforceable duty of care.
articles.description: The law places a legal duty on online services to protect users from serious harm; but the conservative opposition and the United States say the law could lead to censorship of lawful speech

articles.headline: Samajwadi Party leader predicts social polarisation in Uttar Pradesh elections
articles.title: Social polarisation will replace communal polarisation in UP: Ramji Lal Suman
articles.summary: Samajwadi Party leader Ramji Lal Suman stated that the upcoming Uttar Pradesh state election will feature social polarisation instead of traditional communal divisions. Speaking on November 26, 2026, the Rajya Sabha member highlighted strategies for Dalit and Other Backward Classes unity, addressed the party's upcoming manifesto releases, and criticized the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party's governance. He also discussed regional electoral alliances and outreach efforts directed at marginalised communities.
articles.description: Rajya Sabha MP and National General Secretary of the Samajwadi Party said the BJP stood exposed and the marginalised will no longer become the foot soldiers of Hindutva. With the public mood in favour of progressive forces, he advised the Congress to adopt a practical approach in seat-sharing negotiations

articles.headline: Cost of living exceeds minimum wages in three Karnataka cities, study reveals
articles.title: Study finds cost of living way higher than minimum wage in Bengaluru, Mysuru and Mangaluru
articles.summary: An academic study by Kolkata-based forum Fact or Value reveals that the monthly cost of living in Bengaluru, Mangaluru, and Mysuru significantly exceeds statutory minimum wages, leaving most employed residents earning below basic needs. Released on November 24, 2026, the report relies on formulas from the 15th Indian Labour Conference, Supreme Court precedents, and government data. The findings highlight income gaps amid stalled wage revisions in Karnataka.
articles.description: While the monthly cost of living is calculated to be ₹41,752 in Bengaluru, between 59.9% and 74.6% of employed residents earn less, exposing the stark income gap

articles.headline: Jharkhand Chief Minister moves resolution against amended Mines and Minerals Act
articles.title: Jharkhand CM moves resolution against amended Mines and Minerals Act, claims ₹13,000 crore annual revenue loss
articles.summary: Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren moved a resolution during the special Assembly session on November 26, 2026, seeking the withdrawal of the amended Mines and Minerals Act. According to Mr. Soren, the legislation passed by Parliament in August will cause an annual revenue loss of approximately ₹13,000 crore, significantly impacting public welfare funding.
articles.description: Moving the resolution, Hemant Soren said the amendment, passed by Parliament in August, would adversely affect the State's financial position and its ability to fund welfare and development programmes

articles.headline: European football clubs face mixed results in Champions League matches
articles.title: Champions League: Man United and PSG held to draws, Bayern loses
articles.summary: Manchester United and Paris Saint-Germain were both held to 2-2 draws by Sporting Lisbon and Roma respectively on November 26, 2026, while Bayern Munich suffered a 2-1 defeat against Lille. In other matches, Barcelona secured a 4-1 victory over Sabah, Liverpool defeated Club Brugge 3-0, Atletico Madrid beat Viking 2-0, and Inter Milan overcame Stuttgart 2-0.
articles.description: Barcelona and Liverpool register big wins; Real Madrid tops table

articles.headline: Jannik Sinner ruled out of 2027 Australian Open following knee surgery
articles.title: Jannik Sinner ruled out of 2027 Australian Open after knee surgery
articles.summary: World number two Jannik Sinner will miss the Australian Open in January 2027 as he recovers from right knee surgery performed in Finland. According to Tennis Australia chief Andrew Abdo, the Italian player aims to return for the 2028 tournament, leaving Alexander Zverev to take over the top ranking during his absence.
articles.description: Sinner, a two-time champion at Melbourne Park, has not played a match since winning the 2026 Wimbledon title in July.

articles.headline: Sri Lankan mass grave revives search for justice regarding Muslim massacres
articles.title: Sri Lanka mass grave revives quest for answers to forgotten Muslim massacre
articles.summary: The discovery of skeletal remains in a Kurukkalmadam mass grave has renewed efforts by families to identify victims and secure dignified burials for relatives killed during Sri Lanka's civil war. The conflict saw significant violence against the Muslim population by Tamil rebels in the early 1990s, including massacres and forced expulsions.
articles.description: As Sri Lanka's Tamil separatists fought a deadly war with the army, they also killed hundreds of Muslims.

articles.headline: Bank of Korea raises key interest rate and upgrades growth forecast
articles.title: South Korea’s central bank hikes interest rates amid AI chip boom
articles.summary: The Bank of Korea increased its benchmark interest rate by 0.25 percentage points to 3.25 percent on November 26, 2026, driven by robust domestic growth and high inflation. Citing strong artificial intelligence investments and soaring semiconductor exports, the central bank also upgraded its gross domestic product growth forecasts to 3.9 percent for 2026 and 4.1 percent for 2027.
articles.description: Bank of Korea raises key rate by 0.25 percent amid booming exports of semiconductors.

articles.headline: Leaders pay tribute to victims and security personnel on Mumbai attack anniversary
articles.title: 2008 Mumbai terror attacks: Tributes paid to martyrs on 18th anniversary
articles.summary: Political leaders and senior officials gathered at the Mumbai police headquarters on November 26, 2026, to honor victims and security personnel killed during the 2008 terror attacks. The coordinated strikes, executed by ten Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists arriving by sea from Pakistan, resulted in 166 fatalities and over 300 injuries across multiple iconic locations over three days.
articles.description: Ten LeT terrorists from Pakistan arrived by sea on November 26, 2008, and killed 166 people, including 18 security personnel, during a 60-hour siege of Mumbai

articles.headline: European spacecraft captures images of stadium-sized crater on asteroid Dimorphos
articles.title: New images reveal crater on asteroid hit by NASA’s DART planetary defence mission
articles.summary: New images released by the European Space Agency reveal a stadium-sized impact crater and chaotic tumbling on the asteroid Dimorphos following its collision with NASA's DART spacecraft in September 2022. The Hera spacecraft captured the close-up views from a distance to evaluate how the kinetic impactor technique altered the celestial body's trajectory for planetary defense.
articles.description: The DART, short for Double Asteroid Redirection ⁠Test, spacecraft collided with Dimorphos on September 26, 2022; asteroid tumbles in space, with boulders flying around

articles.headline: India plans open-entry caste question for upcoming 2027 national census
articles.title: How should the Census count caste?
articles.summary: India's 2027 census will incorporate an open-entry caste question for populations outside Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, a method previously utilized during the 2011 socio-economic survey. While critics warn of reconciliation challenges arising from millions of distinct entries, officials plan to utilize code directories to process responses following the enumeration beginning in February 2027.
articles.description: The 2027 Census will enumerate caste through an open-entry question, risking a repeat of the 2011 Socio-Economic and Caste Census, which returned about 46.7 lakh caste names; recording the administrative category alongside the caste name would give India reliable caste-wise information on education, occupation and assets

articles.headline: Puerto Rico Supreme Court cancels government contract with Luma Energy
articles.title: Puerto Rico’s Supreme Court cancels major power contract
articles.summary: Puerto Rico Supreme Court ruled in favour of ending the government contract with Luma Energy following a lawsuit by San Juan. The five-to-four decision on Wednesday outlines a one-year transition period. Governor Jenniffer Gonzalez blamed Luma for constant interruptions and record electricity costs, while a federal control board warned the ruling creates enormous uncertainty without a clear successor company in place.
articles.description: The court's five-to-four ruling ends Luma Energy's operations after a contentious legal battle.

articles.headline: Indian rupee falls twenty paise against United States dollar
articles.title: Rupee falls 20 paise to 92.40 against U.S. dollar in early trade
articles.summary: The Indian rupee depreciated twenty paise to 92.40 against the United States dollar on November 26, 2026. Forex traders stated that higher crude oil prices and United States tariff proposals against India fuelled dollar demand. The United States proposed twenty-five percent tariffs following an investigation, while India rejected the allegation and expressed commitment to a bilateral trade agreement.
articles.description: The U.S. proposed 25% tariffs on imports from India, with a provision to cap them at 17% if the two countries agree to a bilateral trade deal, giving it a slight edge over Asian competitors

articles.headline: Artificial intelligence models achieve breakthroughs on longstanding mathematical problems in 2026
articles.title: Top 10 math problems AI models have taken a run at in 2026 (so far)
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence models have achieved significant milestones by tackling major unresolved mathematical problems throughout 2026. On November 25, OpenAI announced that an internal model established the theoretical speed limit for matrix multiplication, following a July 20 achievement where mathematician Levent Alpöge used Anthropic's Claude model to disprove the Jacobian conjecture. While many experts celebrate these technological advancements, others express concern regarding methodological transparency and education.
articles.description: A flurry of announcements landed in the third week of November claiming that various artificial intelligence (AI) models had solved longstanding mathematical problems

articles.headline: German boat dealer suspected of supplying migrant smuggling networks
articles.title: Watch: BBC confronts German man suspected of supplying migrant gangs with small boats
articles.summary: A German boat dealer is suspected by European authorities of supplying small boats and engines to migrant smuggling gangs operating in the English Channel. According to documents seen by the BBC, equipment from MaReBoote was linked to nearly a third of small-boat crossings to the United Kingdom in early 2026. Managing director Marvin Reuter is currently contesting extradition to France to face charges.
articles.description: Marvin Reuter is contesting extradition to France, where he could face smuggling, criminal conspiracy and involuntary manslaughter charges.

articles.headline: German boat dealer investigated over English Channel migrant smuggling
articles.title: German boat dealer suspected of supplying Channel smuggling gangs, BBC finds
articles.summary: European authorities are investigating a German boat dealer accused of supplying vessels and engines to migrant smuggling networks operating in the English Channel. Marvin Reuter, managing director of MaReBoote, is contesting extradition to France after being linked to numerous illegal crossings and two fatal accidents. French prosecutor Samuel Finielz confirmed a European Arrest Warrant was issued for the German company head in May 2025.
articles.description: Nearly a third of crossings in early 2026 allegedly involved boats or engines from the German man's firm.

articles.headline: Six people killed in small plane crash off Mississippi
articles.title: Six killed, including children, in plane crash off Mississippi coast
articles.summary: First responders recovered the bodies of six members from two families after a small plane crashed in the Gulf of Mexico off the Mississippi coast on Tuesday. The Cessna 210 was travelling from New Orleans to Fort Myers when air traffic control lost contact at about 3:45 pm. Authorities are investigating the cause, including potential weather impacts like dangerous icing conditions.
articles.description: US authorities are investigating the reason behind the crash that killed members of the Stokes and Knox families.

articles.headline: Yashasvi Jaiswal emerges as a reliable opening batter for the Indian Test team
articles.title: Jaiswal — the all-terrain red-ball machine
articles.summary: Following India's transition after the World Test Championship final in June 2023, left-handed batsman Yashasvi Jaiswal secured his place as a Test opener. Making his debut in Roseau on July 12, 2023, he scored 171 runs and subsequently demonstrated notable adaptability across diverse pitch conditions in the Caribbean, South Africa, and home series against England, establishing himself as a prolific run-scorer for the national side.
articles.description: The four away Tests right at the start of his career were a great learning experience for him. After his debut in the Caribbean where the pitches played low and slow, those in South Africa were of the exactly opposite kind and opened the young man’s eyes to the challenges that would confront him in the longest format

articles.headline: Madras High Court issues John Doe order regarding Thirupparankundram hill lamp lighting
articles.title: Thirupparankundram Deepathoon row: What does John Doe order passed by Madras HC mean?
articles.summary: The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court issued a John Doe order restraining the public from violating a Supreme Court ruling on lighting a ceremonial lamp at Thirupparankundram hill. The Supreme Court previously permitted the event as a limited arrangement, despite ongoing ownership disputes between Hindu worshippers and a local dargah regarding the site's hilltop location.
articles.description: The Madras High Court restrained anyone from violating the November 20 Supreme Court order which allowed the lighting of the lamp on the hillock as a ‘limited one-time arrangement’ only.

articles.headline: Jannik Sinner withdraws from the 2027 Australian Open due to knee surgery
articles.title: Jannik Sinner out of Australian Open 2027 due to knee injury
articles.summary: Italian tennis player Jannik Sinner will miss the 2027 Australian Open while recovering from recent right knee surgery. Tennis Australia chief executive Andrew Abdo confirmed on November 26, 2026, that the defending champion will be absent from the tournament beginning January 17 in Melbourne. Sinner previously underwent a minor operation on November 24 following persistent joint inflammation that failed to respond to prior treatments.
articles.description: “Jannik loves competing here in Melbourne and is looking forward to returning for AO 2028. We wish him all the very best with his recovery and look forward to seeing him back on court soon”

articles.headline: Karnataka approves India's first comprehensive care and rehabilitation policy for burns survivors
articles.title: Karnataka charts India’s first comprehensive care and rehabilitation policy for burns survivors
articles.summary: The Karnataka Cabinet has approved a policy for the prevention, treatment, rehabilitation, and social reintegration of burns survivors, making it the first state in India to implement such a framework. The initiative involves establishing 15-bed burns care wards in district and medical college hospitals while upgrading the Mahabodhi Burns Care Centre at the Bangalore Medical College and Research Institute into a Centre of Excellence to address statewide treatment gaps.
articles.description: 15-bed burns care wards to be set up in district hospitals; Bangalore Medical College and Research Institute’s Mahabodhi Burns Care Centre to be upgraded as Centre of Excellence

articles.headline: Macy’s postpones its centenary Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York due to severe weather
articles.title: Macy's postpones Thanksgiving parade due to severe weather
articles.summary: Macy’s postponed its 100th annual Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York to Saturday due to an approaching nor'easter storm expected to bring high winds and heavy rain. Executive producer Will Cross said balloons would be deflated for safety, while New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani confirmed increased security for the rescheduled procession amidst regional state of emergency declarations.
articles.description: The move represents the first postponement of the iconic event, and comes after a forecast of strong winds and heavy rain.

articles.headline: Prakash Ambedkar warns of potential blood revolution if the Constitution is not protected
articles.title: Country could face a ‘blood revolution’ unless the Constitution is saved: Prakash Ambedkar
articles.summary: Vanchit Bahujan Aghadi chief Prakash Ambedkar warned on November 25, 2026, that India faces a potential blood revolution unless the Constitution is safeguarded. Speaking at the Samvidhan Samman Sabha, Ambedkar alleged that the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party and Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh are threatening democratic ideals through communal politics and by exacerbating regional divides between northern and southern states. He also criticized major opposition figures and raised concerns regarding national security.
articles.description: Prakash Ambedkar said it is “unfortunate” that the ideals of the Constitution were under threat as Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and the BJP is doing everything to be in power

articles.headline: India pavilion wins Visitors’ Lion at Venice Biennale
articles.title: India Pavilion bags Visitors’ Lion at Venice Biennale; PM Modi calls it ‘proud moment for country’
articles.summary: The India Pavilion won the Visitors’ Lion for Best National Participation at the 61st International Art Exhibition of the Venice Art Biennale, running from May 9 to November 22. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat celebrated the achievement, which highlights the nation's growing cultural influence and showcases works by five artists at the historic Arsenale venue.
articles.description: The pavilion, under the theme ‘Geographies of Distance: Remembering Home’, explored memory and belonging in a rapidly transforming world

articles.headline: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei denies supporting AI control over humanity
articles.title: Anthropic CEO Amodei denies wanting humanity to ‘surrender’ free will to AI
articles.summary: Anthropic Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei addressed reports regarding artificial intelligence governance in a post on X, stating he does not support surrendering human free will to autonomous systems. Responding to an Axios article, Amodei clarified that delegating specific tasks to technology differs from granting global governance authority, as industry leaders continue to debate the timeline and risks surrounding artificial general intelligence.
articles.description: Dario Amodei's remarks come amid predictions AI could soon surpass human intelligence.

articles.headline: Prime Minister Modi highlights constitutional achievements on Constitution Day
articles.title: Govt.’s endeavour has been to deepen Constitution’s connect with people, strengthen unity: PM Modi
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi observed Constitution Day on November 26, 2026, by emphasizing the founding text's role in advancing social and economic justice across the nation. In an op-ed, he detailed welfare initiatives that lifted millions out of poverty, constitutional amendments involving goods and services tax and reservations, and past challenges including the Emergency and Jammu and Kashmir's special status.
articles.description: He pays tribute to Dr. Rajendra Prasad, Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar and all members of the Constituent Assembly, which adopted the Constitution on November 26, 1949; highlights the founding principles’ role in strengthening democracy and promoting social and economic justice

articles.headline: Union Minister Pralhad Joshi announces selected applicants for Kashi Tamil Sangamam
articles.title: 1,400 of 46,080 applicants selected to attend Kashi Tamil Sangamam: Education Minister
articles.summary: Union Minister of Education Pralhad Joshi announced on Tuesday that fourteen hundred applicants out of forty-six thousand eighty were selected for the fifth Kashi Tamil Sangamam running from November 28 to December 12, 2026. Participants will travel to Varanasi in seven groups. The edition introduces a nationwide student programme studying the Thirukkural literary work by poet Thiruvalluvar.
articles.description: The fifth edition of the Kashi Tamil Sangamam features the launch of a nationwide student engagement programme focused on learning the Thirukkural

articles.headline: Petitioners accuse Tamil Nadu government of defying Supreme Court temple lighting order
articles.title: Thirupparankundram row: Supreme Court to examine if wilful disobedience occurred, as State and Hindu parties spar
articles.summary: Petitioners accused the Tamil Nadu government of defying a Supreme Court order regarding the ceremonial lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp in Madurai. During a hearing before Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi on November 25, 2026, senior advocate Guru Krishnakumar alleged that the State circumvented the directive by lighting the festival lamp at an alternative customary location instead of the disputed hilltop stone pillar.
articles.description: Madurai Collector claims all arrangements made to light the lamp on the Deepathoon, as per the SC’s November 20 order, but temple did not send team; temple cites ‘historical continuity’; Hindu parties accuse State, temple of collusion to defy order

articles.headline: India separates Sheikh Hasina return plans from extradition requests
articles.title: MEA separates Sheikh Hasina’s plans to return to Bangladesh from issue of extradition
articles.summary: The Indian Ministry of External Affairs stated on November 25, 2026, that former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina returning home voluntarily using a travel document is separate from Bangladesh's formal extradition request. Official spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal also expressed deep concern regarding ongoing violence against minorities in Bangladesh during the press briefing.
articles.description: ‘The case of a citizen willing to return voluntarily to her country on a travel document is a matter separate from the extradition request,’ MEA’s official spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said

articles.headline: Plane crash off Mississippi coast kills six members of a Florida family
articles.title: Plane crash off coast of Mississippi kills extended family of six on fishing trip
articles.summary: A small aircraft carrying six members of an extended Florida family crashed into the Gulf of Mexico on November 24, 2026, while returning from a fishing trip. Authorities including the Coast Guard confirmed that divers located the victims inside the fuselage of the Cessna 210. The Federal Aviation Administration and the National Transportation Safety Board are investigating the incident.
articles.description: Shortly before losing contact with the plane, an air traffic controller at Gulfport–Biloxi International Airport advised the pilot of precipitation and adverse weather in the area

articles.headline: John Wright recalls discovering Jasprit Bumrah during a 2013 domestic match
articles.title: How John Wright spotted Jasprit Bumrah
articles.summary: Former India head coach John Wright recounted how he first noticed fast bowler Jasprit Bumrah during a March 2013 match between Mumbai and Gujarat in Ahmedabad. Working as part of the Mumbai Indians support staff, Wright was drawn to the young bowler's consistent delivery of high-pace yorkers. The chance encounter has since drawn renewed attention following a viral photograph of the pair meeting in Lincoln.
articles.description: ‘I watched him bowl an over; they were all yorkers; he tried to bowl everything as yorkers; and he had a bit of pace,’ John Wright reminisced about Jasprit Bumrah

articles.headline: Macy's postpones 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday due to severe weather
articles.title: Bad weather postpones Macy’s 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade for first time ever
articles.summary: Organizers announced that Macy's 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade will be postponed from November 26 to November 28, 2026, due to severe weather bringing intense winds and rain to New York City. Mayor Zohran Mamdani supported the decision, noting potential hazards from high winds that could endanger spectators and oversized balloons. This marks the first time in the event's history that it has been rescheduled.
articles.description: The postponement came as New York City is set to get slammed by a storm bringing intense winds and rain to the region

articles.headline: ICE officers smash car window, pepper spray bystanders
articles.title: ICE officers smash car window, pepper spray bystanders
articles.description: Masked ICE agents smashed a car window and forcibly opened its door to arrest a man in California.

articles.headline: California coastal areas face severe flooding threats as king tides peak
articles.title: California warns of flooding as King Tides peak over Thanksgiving
articles.summary: Coastal areas of California are bracing for potential flooding as king tides peak during the United States Thanksgiving holiday, with water levels reaching over eight feet in some locations on Wednesday and Thursday. The National Weather Service reported that these high tides are breaking records set just last month and are being strengthened by a strong El Nino weather pattern. Meanwhile, additional storm systems are forecast to impact the Pacific Northwest and the eastern United States.
articles.description: Parts of the Canadian province of British Columbia may also be affected by the storms and flooding, which come as millions of people travel for the holiday.

articles.headline: Maharashtra Cabinet approves free foodgrains for farmers and infrastructure projects
articles.title: Maharashtra Cabinet approves free foodgrains for over 42 lakh farmers
articles.summary: The Maharashtra Cabinet approved free foodgrains for more than 4.2 million farmers not covered under Direct Benefit Transfer across 33 drought-affected districts on Wednesday. Chaired by Chief Minister Devendra Fadvanis, the Cabinet also cleared a 55,48-crore rupee provision for the Narmada-Tapi diversion project in Nandurbar, established a separate MPID tribunal for financial fraud cases, and advanced the Maharashtra Private-Aided Schools Regulation Bill.

articles.headline: Election Commission directs states to correct electoral roll errors using Form 8
articles.title: ECI directs states to correct erroneous entries in SIR rolls through Form 8 during ongoing Special Summary Revision
articles.summary: The Election Commission of India directed chief electoral officers across twenty-five states and union territories on November 25, 2026, to rectify erroneous voter entries identified during the Special Summary Revision. Booth Level Officers will visit electors to verify demographic details and obtain Form 8 applications, ensuring no modifications occur through automated matching procedures.
articles.description: The ECI move follows complaints of incorrect entries in several cases in the final published SIR lists

articles.headline: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed to Saturday due to East Coast storm
articles.title: Storms push Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City to Saturday
articles.summary: Organisers announced on Wednesday that the annual Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City has been postponed to Saturday because of an East Coast storm threatening lashing winds and coastal flooding. Executive producer Will Coss stated that participant and spectator safety is the top priority for the 100th procession. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani confirmed that an expanded police presence will secure the route for the rescheduled holiday event.
articles.description: The parade, which marks its 100th edition, got a last-minute rain check ahead of heavy gusts on Thursday.

articles.headline: France's political mainstream faces potential presidential wipe-out in 2027
articles.title: France's political mainstream risks presidential vote debacle with no clear candidate
articles.summary: France's political center faces a potential wipe-out in the April-May 2027 presidential election due to the dominance of hard-right and hard-left leaders. Analysts note that divisions, personal rivalries, and a lack of preparation plague legacy parties. While candidates like Edouard Philippe and David Lisnard compete on the right, commentators warn that the middle ground currently lacks a unified strategy or programme.
articles.description: Hard-right and hard-left candidates dominate the polls ahead of next year's presidential election.

articles.headline: Zambian authorities ban planned protests over presidential term limit proposals
articles.title: Zambia bans protest against push to remove presidential term limits
articles.summary: Zambian police banned a planned November 25 protest against removing presidential term limits, citing clash risks with a rival pro-government youth group demonstration. The ruling party petitioned parliament to allow President Hakainde Hichilema a third term, drawing opposition from civil society and detained political figures facing disputed treason charges, though the government insists the president respects the constitution.
articles.description: Critics fear the campaign could undermine democratic safeguards as senior opposition figures remain behind bars.

articles.headline: Donald Trump expresses willingness to discuss Medicare for All with Democratic senator
articles.title: A meeting with Democrats over healthcare? Trump says he’s open to it
